नई दिल्‍ली, 44 जनवरी, 2026 


सा.का.नि. 34(a&).— बॉयलर अधिनियम, 2025 (2025 का 2) की धारा 40, द्वारा प्रदत्त शक्तियों का प्रयोग 
करते हुए तथा भारतीय बॉयलर विनियम, 7950 के अधिक्रमण में, ऐसे अधिक्रमण से पहले किए गए अथवा लोप की गई 
बातों को छोड़कर, केन्द्रीय बॉयलर बोर्ड निम्नलिखित मसौदा विनियमों को बनाने का प्रस्ताव करती है, को उक्त अधिनियम 
की धारा 40 की उप-धारा (॥) के अनुसार इनसे प्रभावित होने की संभावना वाले सभी व्यक्तियों की जानकारी के लिए 
एतदद्वारा प्रकाशित किया जाता है और यह नोटिस दिया जाता है कि उक्त मसौदा विनियमों पर, इस अधिसूचना को 
प्रकाशित करने वाले भारत के राजपत्र की प्रतियां जनसामान्य को उपलब्ध कराए जाने की तारीख से तीस दिनों की अवधि 
के समाप्त होने के बाद विचार किया जाएगा; 


उक्त मसौदा विनियमों से संबंध में निर्धारित अवधि के भीतर किसी व्यक्ति से प्राप्त आपत्तियों या सुझावों पर 
केन्द्रीय बॉयलर बोर्ड द्वारा विचार किया जाएगा;

और उद्योग मंत्रालय (उद्योग संवर्धन और आंतरिक व्यापार विभाग), कमरा नं. 726U, उद्योग भवन, नई दिल्ली- 007

प्रणाली को अपनाएगा जो इसे इन सभी तैयार सामग्रियों के मूल चार्ज का पता लगाने में सक्षम बनायेगी और 
निरीक्षक अथवा सक्षम व्यक्ति, जैसा भी मामला हो, को निर्माता द्वारा उनके संबंधित चार्ज में सभी प्लेट्स 
और बार्स का पता लगाने और अपेक्षित परीक्षणों का साक्षी रहने के लिए सभी सुविधाएं प्रदान की जाएगी। 
जब निरीक्षण या सक्षम व्यक्ति जैसा भी मामला हो, सामग्री और परीक्षण के परिणामों से संतुष्ट होगा तो

निरीक्षक या सक्षम व्यक्ति, जैसा भी मामला हो, को सामग्री की परीक्षण रिपोर्ट की दो प्रतियां उसके हस्ताक्षर 
हेतु प्रदान की जाएंगी। 


45. जब स्टील का उत्पादन वहां नहीं किया गया हो जहां उसे रोल किया जा रहा है- (4) जहां स्टील 
का उत्पादन उस कारखाने में नहीं किया जाता जहां इसे रोल किया जाता है, तो प्रपत्र ५(भाग-क) अथवा 
प्रपत्र |/(भाग-ग), जैसा भी मामला हो, में सामग्री के परीक्षण के साक्ष्य हेतु नियुक्त सक्षम व्यक्ति को एक 
प्रमाण पत्र प्रस्तुत किया जाएगा जिसमें खुली भट्टी अथवा इलैक्ट्रिक प्रक्रिया अथवा कोई ऑक्सीजन प्रक्रिया 
जिससे उसका निर्माण किया गया था, उसे आपूर्ति करने वाले स्टील निर्माता का नाम, साथ ही स्टील निर्माता 
की बुक्स के संदर्भ हेतु चार्जेस की संख्या का उल्लेख होगा। 

(2) चार्ज की संख्या को पहचान के उद्देश्य से प्रत्येक प्लेट अथवा बार पर अंकित किया जाएगा। 


46. निर्माता का प्रमाणपत्र

मामला हो, में ऐसा प्रमाण-पत्र सक्षम व्यक्ति को प्रस्तुत करेगा, जो इस बात की गारंटी प्रदान करता है कि 
इस सामग्री को खुली भट्टी अथवा इलैक्ट्रिक प्रक्रिया, अम्लीय अथवा क्षारीय द्वारा तैयार किया गया है और

काटे जाने पूर्व तैयार ट्यूब के सिरे से लिये जाएंगे। 

(i) वे सिरे पर चिकने होने चाहिए और खुरदुरेपन अथवा कमियों से मुक्त होने चाहिए।

परीक्षण किया जाए। 


(i) बड़े आकार के ट्यूबों के लिए, तन्यता क्षमता परीक्षण के नमूने में ट्यूब से लंबाई में काटी गई स्ट्रीप 
शामिल होगी और जिसे गेज ca के भीतर सीधा और आगे ताप प्रक्रिया न किया गया हो। 


(ग) यदि कोई परीक्षण नमूना कमी अथवा त्रुटिपूर्ण मशीनिंग को दर्शाता है तो उसे नष्ट कर दिया जाएगा 
और दूसरे नमूने से प्रतिस्थापित किया जाएगा। 


(a) सभी नमूनों का सामान्य तापमान पर परीक्षण किया जाएगा। 


(2) (क) यहां विनिर्दिष्ट परीक्षण पहले 00 ट्यूब्स के लिए न्यूनतम 2 ट्यूब्स पर किया जाएगा और प्रत्येक

53. परीक्षणों की संख्या और परीक्षण नमूनों का प्रावधान - TI और बेंड परीक्षण हिस्सों को प्रत्येक

(i) (क) परीक्षण नमूना, विनिर्माता और सक्षम व्यक्ति के बीच सहमति के अनुसार कास्टिंग से

(ख)संबद्ध परीक्षण नमूने हेतु करार में सटीक स्थान और संलग्नता की पद्धति शामिल होगी। यदि 
सक्षम व्यक्ति विनिर्माता के साथ ऐसा कोई करार नहीं करता है तो परीक्षण नमूने प्रदान करने 
का तरीका विनिर्माता द्वारा निर्धारित होगा। 

(ग) तथापि विनिर्माता का विवेकाधिकार, नीचे उप नियम (4) में दर्शाये गये एक से अधिक गलन 
प्रक्रिया से तैयार कास्टिंग के परीक्षण पर लागू नहीं होगा। 


(i) = (क) यदि परीक्षण नमूनों को कास्टिंग के साथ संलग्न किया जाता है, तो प्रत्येक गलन प्रक्रिया से

59. परीक्षण हिस्सों का चयन- () परीक्षण के लिए या तो उसके हिस्सों का उपयोग किया जाएगा अथवा 
अतिरिक्त सामग्री या पर्याप्त आकार के परीक्षण हिस्से उपलब्ध कराये जाएंगे। हेडर के मामले में उदाहरण 
के लिए परीक्षण रिंग के सरप्लस हिस्सों का उपयोग किया जा सकता है। डाई में स्वैग किये गये फ्लैंग्स के 
मामले में बचे हुए पंचिंग का उपयोग परीक्षण हिस्सों के रूप में किया जा सकता है, जिस मामले में पंचिंग 
की सामग्री की पहचान पर्याप्त रूप से उस फ्लैंग से की जाएगी। यह परीक्षण अर्ध-तैयार सामग्री पर भी 
किया जा सकता है उदाहरण के लिए किसी बार अथवा बिलट पर बशर्ते कि तैयार फ़ोर्जिंग की भांति इसका 
भी लगभग समान रूप से अपचयन हुआ हो और ताप प्रक्रिया से गुजरा हो। बंद सिरे वाले हेडर के लिए 
डिशिंग या रिड्यूसिंग से पहले परीक्षण रिंग को काटा जाएगा और ये हेडर के समान उसी ताप प्रक्रिया के 
अधीन किया जाएगा। ऐसे हेडर के मामले में जिन्हें विशेष कवर से बंद किया गया है, परीक्षण रिंग को ताप 
प्रक्रिया के बाद काटा जाएगा। इसी तरह की प्रक्रिया अन्य फ़ोर्जिंग के परीक्षण हिस्सों के लिए की जाएगी। 


(2) परीक्षण के लिए, एक तथा समान कास्ट के हिस्से जो उसी ताप प्रक्रिया बैच के हों और इसके साथ-साथ 
समान परिमाप के हों उन्हें एक समूह में रखा जा सकता है तथा प्रत्येक समूह से कम से कम एक परीक्षण 
हिस्सा लिया जाएगा। 

(3) प्रासंगिक परीक्षण हिस्सों का उपयोग जहां व्यवहार्य हो, हेडर के लिए किया जाएगा। 200 मिमी से कम 
बाहरी व्यास वाले हेडर के लिए लंबवत परीक्षण हिस्सों की अनुमति है।

322 . पाइपों का निरीक्षण - (7) निर्धारित स्थान पर लगाने से पूर्व पाइपों का परीक्षण किया 
जाएगा। परीक्षण में परीक्षण दबाव वह होना चाहिए जो MH पाइपों के लिए मानक परिस्थितियों के लिए 


[भाग ॥--खण्ड 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 307 


निर्धारित किया गया है। निरीक्षण प्राधिकारी से प्रपत्र ४ (भाग-ख), में एक प्रमाण पत्र, जिसमें कहा गया 
हो कि यह उसके द्वारा किया गया है, स्वीकार किया जा सकता है। यदि सक्षम व्यक्ति परीक्षण से संतुष्ट है, 
तो पाइप को निर्धारित स्थान पर लगाया जा सकता है । मुख्य निरीक्षक निर्दिष्ट किए जाने वाले दबाव और 
तापमान पर उपयोग के लिए पाइप लाइन की उपयुक्तता के संबंध में स्वामी को अपने अनुमोदन 
की सूचना देगा। 


(2) बॉयलर के बाद के निरीक्षण में या किसी अन्य समय पर, सक्षम व्यक्ति भाप-पाइप का 
बाहरी निरीक्षण कर सकता है और इस उद्देश्य के लिए फ्लैंजेस पर लैगिंग के एक हिस्से को हटाने 
की आवश्यकता हो सकती है, और पाइप बनाया जा सकता है। यदि इस निरीक्षण के 
परिणामस्वरूप सक्षम व्यक्ति की राय है कि पाइप या उस समय की कोई भी स्थिति असंतोषजनक 
है, तो वह मुख्य निरीक्षक को मामले की रिपोर्ट करेगा, जो किसी भी पाइप या पाइपों की पूरी लैगिंग 
को हटवा सकता है और उसका हाइड्रॉलिक परीक्षण करवा सकता है। ऐसे हाईड्रॉलिक परीक्षण में 
दबाव परीक्षण बॉयलर के डिजाइन दबाव या पाइप के अधिकतम स्वीकार्य कार्य दबाव जैसा भी 
मामला हो, के डेढ़ गुना से कम नहीं होना चाहिए। 


(3) (क) SH पाइप और फिटिंग के संबंध में प्रपत्र संख्या xiv में निरीक्षण पुस्तिका का एक ज्ञापन 
तैयार किया जाएगा। इस पुस्तक में, निरीक्षक, भाप पाइप और फिटिंग के सभी विवरणों और 
आयामों को लिखित रूप में दर्ज करेगा, जिसमें विभिन्न भागों के लिए गणना, हाईड्रॉलिक परीक्षण के 
विवरण और उनके निरीक्षण नोट शामिल हैं। 


(ख) बाद के निरीक्षण में, सक्षम व्यक्ति निरीक्षण और हाईड्रॉलिक परीक्षण की तारीख को नोटों के

जाना चाहिये। जब सक्षम व्यक्ति द्वारा आवश्यक पाए जाने पर निरीक्षण के बाद इकोनोमाइजर का 
हाइड्रॉलिक परीक्षण किया जाएगा। 


(2) जांच के बाद इकोनोमाइजर पर डाला गया परीक्षण दबाव इकोनोमाइजर के अधिकतम स्वीकार्य

384. निरीक्षण पुस्तिका का ज्ञापन- () हर इकोनोमाइजर के लिए फॉर्म-)९५॥ में एक निरीक्षक

(2) बाद के निरीक्षण में, सक्षम व्यक्ति निरीक्षण की तारीखें, हाइड्रोलिक टेस्ट जब किए जाएं, तो अलग- 
अलग पार्टस की स्थिति से जुड़े नोट्स के साथ दर्ज करेगा; 


(3) निरीक्षक या सक्षम व्यक्ति, जैसा भी मामला हो, निरीक्षण पुस्तिका के ज्ञापन में इकोनोमाइजर की 
सामान्य स्थिति और मरम्मत की स्थिति भी दर्ज करेगा; 


(4) (क) मुख्य निरीक्षक को ज्ञापन पुस्तिका प्रस्तुत करने पर, वह नए पंजीकृत इकोनोमाइजर के मामले में, 
सभी विवरण और कैलकुलेशन की जांच करेगा और जिस डिज़ाइन प्रेशर की अनुमति दी जानी है, उसे 
अनुमोदित करेगा। 

(ख) पुराने इकोनोमाइजर के मामले में, मुख्य निरीक्षक, निरीक्षक के निरीक्षण नोट्स और मरम्मत के लिए

(ग) इकोनोमाइजर के लिए एक बार अनुमोदित किया गया प्रेशर, मुख्य निरीक्षक के लिखित अधिकार के 
बिना नहीं बदला जाएगा। 

(घ) निरीक्षण पुस्तिका ज्ञापन को साफ़ और अद्यतन रखा जाएगा और निरीक्षण पुस्तिका, जब तक कि

385. पंजीकरण पुस्तिका- () इकोनोमाइज़र के लिए एक पंजीकरण पुस्तिका या निरीक्षण पुस्तिका

आद्याक्षर के साथ पंजीकरण पुस्तिका में दर्ज किया जाएगा। 


(2) मुख्य निरीक्षक यह भी देखेगा कि निरीक्षण पुस्तिका ज्ञापन में दर्ज किए गए बाद के निरीक्षण के नोट

386. निरीक्षण पुस्तिका ज्ञापन और पंजीकरण पुस्तिका का हस्तांतरण- एक राज्य से दूसरे राज्य में

अनुरोध पर जिसको इकोनोमाइजर हस्तांतरित किया गया है, उस अधिकारी को अग्रेषित किया जाएगा जो

(ख) ऐसे इकोनोमाइजर की मूल संख्या को नए उपकरणों में रखा जाएगा, बशर्ते कि इकोनोमाइजर ऐसे

(ग) एक बार आंवटित संख्या को दूसरे इकोनोमाइजर में दोबारा इस्तेमाल नहीं किया जाएगा। 


393. फीड पाइप का निरीक्षण- (4)(क) फीड पाइप को उसके स्थान पर स्थापित करने से पहले उसका 
निरीक्षण और हाइड्रॉलिक परीक्षण किया जाएगा, और हाइड्रॉलिक परीक्षण दबाव इकोनोमाइजर के 
अधिकतम स्वीकार्य कार्यात्मक दबाव को दुगना से कम नहीं होना चाहिए। 


(ख) मान्यताप्राप्त निर्माता या निरीक्षक प्राधिकारी से एक प्रमाण-पत्र कि यह पूरा किया जा चुका है इसे 
स्वीकार किया जा सकता है। 


(ग) यदि निरीक्षक या सक्षम व्यक्ति, जैसा भी मामला हो, परीक्षण से संतुष्ट है, तो पाइप लगाया जा सकता

(घ) फीड पाइप के लिए कोई अलग प्रमाण-पत्र जारी नहीं किया जाएगा और ना ही उनके निरीक्षण के लिए 
अलग से शुल्क लिया जाएगा। 

(ड़) छपाई रजिस्ट्री संख्या की प्राप्ति की तिथि से दो महीनों की अवधि के भीतर पूरा किया जाएगा। 

(2) . निरीक्षण के बाद या किसी भी समय, सक्षम व्यक्ति, फीड पाइप का बाहरी निरीक्षण कर सकता है 


और यदि वह इसे खराब स्थिति में पाता है तो वह मुख्य निरीक्षक को इस मामले की रिपोर्ट प्रस्तुत करेगा 
जो अपेक्षित हो तो पाइप का हाइड्रॉलिक परीक्षण कर सकता है।

397. कर्मशाला के उपकरण- (॥) वेल्डिंग संयंत्र और उपकरण अच्छी गुणवत्ता के होने चाहिए, और 
उनका रख-रखाव कुशल कार्यशील स्थिति में होना चाहिए। वेल्डिंग उपकरण कवर के अंदर होने चाहिए 
और इस प्रकार व्यवस्थित होने चाहिए कि विपरीत मौसमी परिस्थितियों और तेज हवाओं में भी वेल्डिंग 
कार्य को जारी रखा जा सके। यह प्रक्रिया इस प्रकार होनी चाहिए कि वेल्डिंग कार्यों की नियमित और 
व्यवस्थित मानीटरिंग की जा सके और वेल्डिंग ऑपरेटरों को कारीगरी की गुणवत्ता के दृष्टिकोण से 
कर्मशाला के परीक्षण अधिकारियों द्वारा समय-समय पर किया जाना है। इन परीक्षणों का रिकार्ड रखा 
जाएगा और जांच के लिए सक्षम व्यक्ति के लिए उपलब्ध होगा। 


(2) कर्मशाला वेल्डिंग संयंत्र उपकरण और गुणवत्ता नियंत्रण कर्मियों से युक्त होनी चाहिए। हालांकि 
विनाशकारी, गैर-विनाशकारी परीक्षण तथा प्रक्रिया के लिए उपकरण आवश्यक नहीं है। विनिर्माता इन 
सुविधाओं के लिए बाहरी पक्ष से समझौता कर सकता है और जिससे पक्ष वह यह समझौता करता है, जो 
उसका एक पत्र बॉयलर के मुख्य निरीक्षक या उसके प्रतिनिधि को उपलब्ध कराया जाना चाहिए और 
परीक्षण के दौरान पक्ष को प्रयोगशाला में सामग्री का निरीक्षण करने की अनुमति दी जानी चाहिए।

4. विभिन्न दबाव भागों के डिफ्लेक्शन की सावधानीपूर्वक जांच की जाएगी और दबाव को रिलीज 
करने के बाद कोई स्थायी सेट नहीं होगा। 


(3) यदि हाइड्रोलिक दबाव परीक्षण के दौरान या बाद में कोई आवश्यक मरम्मत पाई जाती है, तो बॉयलर 
को मरम्मत के पूरा होने के बाद फिर से ऊपर निर्दिष्ट दबाव परीक्षण के अधीन किया जाएगा और किसी 
भी de ट्रीटमेंट के बाद मरम्मत किए गए des जाइंट को विनियम 453 के अनुसार ele ट्रीटमेंट की 
आवश्यकता होती है | 


नोट: सक्षम व्यक्ति/निरीक्षण प्राधिकारी के अभ्युक्तियों और टिप्पणियों को निर्माता के कागजात के साथ 
दाखिल करने के लिए दर्ज किया जाएगा।

जाने चाहिए:- 


(i) सुरक्षा वाल्वों को कम से कम 2.5% नीचे के दबाव पर रीसेट किया जाना चाहिए, लेकिन 
सुरक्षा Ted सेट दबाव से 5% से अधिक नहीं होना चाहिए। 

(i) 32 मिमी से कम की बॉडी सीट वाले और 24 बार गेज या उससे कम के निर्धारित दबाव

फ्लैंज आयाम की विभिन्न तालिकाओं (तालिका एफ.टी) को पाइप और वेस्सेल के अनुकूल डिज़ाइन किया 
गया है जिसमें 427 °c के अधिकतम तापमान वाले वाष्प होते है। 

यदि तापमान 427 °c से अधिक होता है और तापमान 482 °c से अधिक नहीं होता है तब 
निम्नलिखित तालिका को अगले उच्चतर दबाव के लिए उपयोग किया जाना चाहिए। 

दिए गए दबाव हेतु ऐसे जल के पाइप जिनमें जल का तापमान 232 "८ से अधिक नहीं होता है, 
ऐसे जल के पाइप को अगले निम्नतर तालिका के लिए फ्लैंज के साथ लगाया जाना चाहिए न कि 
उल्लिलिखित दबाव और 427 "८ के अधिकतम तापमान हेतु अपेक्षित वाष्प के लिए। 

सभी मामलों में हाईड्रॉलिक परीक्षण दबाव को अधिकतम अनुमत कार्यशील दबाव के दोगुना होना 
चाहिए जिसके लिए पाइप का उपयोग किया जाना अध्यधीन है।

तापमान प्रचालन के लिए ऑपरेशन डेटा; 


(ख) पिछले वर्ष के दौरान किए गए बंद का विवरण उनके कारण और की गई कार्रवाई के 
साथ; 


(ग) balk के दौरान बॉयलर के दबाव भागों पर किए गए किसी भी गैर-विनाशकारी परीक्षण के 
PIS; 


(घ) HAR के पानी की गुणवत्ता को ऐसे बॉयलरों की आवश्यकता के अनुसार बनाए रखा 
जाता है गुणवत्ता का अधिग्रहण प्रणाली (डीएएस) के द्वारा या संयंत्र में या पानी के स्रोत पर 
हे गए पानी की गुणवत्ता रिकॉर्ड लॉगबुक के माध्यम से डेटा उपलब्ध कराया जाता 


(S) बॉयलर ट्यूब विफलता रिकॉर्ड (स्थान, मरम्मत/प्रतिस्थापित ट्यूबों की संख्या)। 


(2) विनियम 3॥॥ में दिये गए प्रावधान के अनुसार छत्तीस महीने की समाप्ति पर संबंधित सक्षम व्यक्ति 
द्वारा निरीक्षण किया जाएगा । तथापि, प्रमाणन अवधि समाप्त होने से पहले और प्रमाणन के छह महीने के 
बाद किसी भी समय पंद्रह दिन या उससे अधिक समय तक के बंद की स्थिति में, सक्षम व्यक्ति को 
विधिवत सूचित किया जाएगा ताकि उक्त बंद की अवधि के दौरान निरीक्षण निर्धारित किया जा सके। 


ख. विशेष रूप से निरंतर प्रक्रिया में संयंत्र में उपयोग किए बीस वर्ष की अवधि तक के (बिना 
फायर किए हुए) वेस्ट हीट बॉयलर। 

(॥) विशेष रूप से निरंतर प्रक्रिया में संयंत्र में उपयोग किए बीस वर्ष की अवधि तक के (बिना फायर 
किए हुए) वेस्ट dle बॉयलर के लिए विनियम 377 में दी गई प्रक्रिया और फिटनेस के प्रमाणीकरण 
के अनुसार निरीक्षण और राज्य में संबंधित सक्षम व्यक्ति द्वारा जारी प्रमाणन की तारीख से चौबीस महीने 


[भाग ॥--खण्ड 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 633 


की समाप्ति पर निरीक्षण किया जाएगा, और पैराग्राफ "क" में संचालन रिकॉर्ड से संतुष्ट होने पर, चौबीस 
महीने की एक और अवधि के लिए संचालन की अनुमति दी जाएगी। 


(2) जैसा कि विनियम 37 4 प्रावधान है, संबंधित सक्षम व्यक्ति द्वारा अड़तालीस महीने की समाप्ति पर 
निरीक्षण किया जाएगा। तथापि, प्रमाणन अवधि समाप्त होने से पहले और प्रमाणन के छह महीने के बाद 
किसी भी समय पंद्रह दिन या उससे अधिक समय के बंद की स्थिति में, सक्षम व्यक्ति को विधिवत सूचित 
किया जाएगा ताकि sad बंद की अवधि के दौरान निरीक्षण निर्धारित किया जा सके। 


ग. विशेष रूप से निरंतर प्रक्रिया में संयंत्र में उपयोग किए बीस वर्ष से अधिक की अवधि के (फायर 
किए गए) वेस्ट हीट बॉयलर । 

बीस वर्ष से अधिक की अवधि के बॉयलर विनियम 377 में दिये गए प्रावधान के अनुसार, निरीक्षण में राज्य 
के संबंधित सक्षम व्यक्ति की संतुष्टि के अधीन रहना जारी रहेंगे। तथापि, यदि इन विनियमों के प्रावधानों के 
अनुसार शेष कार्यशील अवधि मूल्यांकन (आरएलए) बायलर पर किया जाता है और यदि संतोषजनक 
पाया जाता है, तो उपरोक्त पैरा 'क' में दी गई प्रक्रिया का पालन किया जाएगा। 


घ. विशेष रूप से निरंतर प्रक्रिया में संयंत्र में उपयोग किए बीस वर्ष से अधिक के अवधि के (बिना 
फायर किए हुए) वेस्ट हीट बॉयलर। 

बीस वर्ष से अधिक की अवधि के बॉयलर विनियम 377 में दिये गए प्रावधान के अनुसार निरीक्षण में राज्य 
के संबंधित सक्षम व्यक्ति की संतुष्टि के अधीन रहना जारी रहेंगे। तथापि, यदि इन विनियमों के प्रावधानों के 
अनुसार शेष कार्यशील अवधि आकलन (आरएलए) बायलर पर किया जाता है और यदि संतोषजनक 
पाया जाता है, तो उपरोक्त पैरा 'ख' में दी गई प्रक्रिया लागू होगी।

MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade) 
(CENTRAL BOILERS BOARD) 
NOTIFICATION 

New Delhi, the 4th January, 2026 
G.S.R. 3l(E).—In exercise of the powers conferred by section 40 of the Boilers Act, 
2025 (2 of 2025), and in supersession of the Indian Boiler Regulations, 950, except as respects 
thing done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the following draft regulations, which 
the Central Boilers Board proposes to make is hereby published as required under sub-section () 
of section 40 of the said Act for the information of all persons likely to be affected thereby and 
notice is hereby given that the said draft regulations will be taken into consideration after expiry 
of a period of thirty days from the date the Gazette containing the publication of this notification 


is made available to the public; 


Any objections or suggestions which may be received from any person with respect to 
the said draft regulations within the period so specified will be considered by the Central Boilers 


Board; 


Objections or suggestions, if any, may be addressed to the Secretary, Central Boilers 
Board, Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal 


Trade), Room No. 26A, UdyogBhawan, New Delhi- ll0 Oll or sent by email 
(sandeep.kumbhar7@gov.in) within the period specified above. 


DRAFT REGULATIONS 
PRELIMINARY 


. Short title, application and commencement. — (l) These regulations may be called the 


Indian Boiler Regulations, 2026. 


(2) These regulations shall apply to all boilers including those working on the principles of 


natural circulations, forced circulation and forced flow with no fixed steam and water line. 
(3) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Definitions.—(7) In these regulations, unless the context otherwise requires,- 


[भाग ॥--खण्ड 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 644 


(a) “Act” means the Boilers Act, 2025 (2 of 2025); 

(0) “Appraisal Committee” means a Committee constituted by the Central Boilers Board 
to evaluate the performance of a firm or a company applying for recognition as 
Inspecting Authority; 

(c) “Central Boilers Board Examination Standing Committee’ means a Committee 
constituted by the Central Boilers Board to conduct examination for recognition of 
competent persons; 

(d) “design pressure of boiler”,- 

(i) in relation to a natural or assisted circulation boiler, means the maximum 
allowable working pressure in the steam drum of the boiler; 

(ii) in relation to a once through forced-circulation boiler, means the maximum 
allowable working pressure at the final superheater steam outlet; 

(6) “design temperature”, - 

(i) for unheated components, means, the fluid temperature inside the 
component, under operation; 

(ii) for heated components, means, the fluid temperature inside the component 
under sustained conditions increased by specified code allowances; 

(f) “Evaluation Committee” means a committee constituted by the Central Government 
to evaluate the performance of firm or a company applying for recognition as 
competent authority, well-known materialtesting laboratory, well-known steel maker, 
well-known foundry or forge, well-known tube or pipe maker and well-known remnant 
life assessment organisation; 

(g) “firm” means a firm and includes a company; 

(h) “form” means a form appended to these regulations; 

(i) “maximum allowable working pressure” means the design pressure of any part, 
adjusted to take into account the pressure drop and hydraulic head; 

(j) “pipe” means the cylindrical hollow parts, other than tube, drum or header with a 
design intent to carry a flow of steam or water or water-steam mixture during normal 
operation, including those that carry intermittent flow, such as drain pipes; 

The expression ‘pipe’ implies that there is no design intent to effect heat transfer 


through the wall of the pressure part; 


642 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(k) “tube” meansa tubular pressure part that is either exposed over much of its length 

to hot gases for purposes of heat transfer, or is directly butt welded to such a 
tubular pressure part including a tube stub on a drum or header. 

(2)Words and expressions used herein and not defined but defined is the Act or the rules 


made there-under shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in that Act or 
the rules. 


CHAPTER-4 


3. General requirements, application of standard conditions and exception 
thereto — 


()No boiler shall be registered under sub-section (5) of section 72 of the Act and no 
certificate shall be issued under sub-section (6) of that section with reference to a boiler, 
unless the standard conditions in respect of material, design and construction, specified in 
the subsequent chapters of these regulations, are satisfied in respect of such a boiler. 


(2) Notwithstanding anything in sub-regulation (), the Chief Inspector may, subject to the 
provisions of regulation 29, register a boiler and issue a certificate authorising the use 
thereof, under any of the following circumstances, namely:- 


(a) when the material used in the construction of a boiler, steam-pipe, economiser or 
superheater is not in conformity with theseregulations but used in other countries 
as being suitable for use in the construction of boilers and steam-pipes, provided 
that such material is not specifically prohibited by these regulations and that the 
methods of manufacture, fabrication and heat treatment conform to the specified 
Codes or Standards; 


(6) when the constructional features of a boiler, steam-pipe, economiser or 
superheater are not in conformity with these regulations but are not considered 
by the Board to be inferior in strength to those prescribed in these regulations 
and form part of the usual manufacturing practice of boilers and steam-pipes in 
other countries; 


(c) when a boiler, steam-pipe, economiser or superheater has been built in 
conformity with these regulations but no certificate as required under the 
regulations is forthcoming; 


(3) No structural part of a boiler, which is subject to pressure, shall be made of Bessemer 
process steel or of Cast or Malleable Cast Iron. 


(4) Where no specific provision is made in these regulations for design or manufacture of 
any pressure part, the Inspecting Authority may permit the design, manufacture, stage 
inspections and certification of such pressure parts including the valves; mountings and 


[भाग ॥--खण्ड 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 643 


fittings conforming to the Codes or Standards like British Standards (BS), European 
Standards (EN), American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Boiler and Pressure 
Vessel Code, Tubular Exchanger Manufacturers Association (TEMA), Technical 
Requirements Document (TRD), GOST and Japanese Industrial Standards (JIS), which 
are known to be commonly used in industrially advanced countries and the decision of 
Inspecting Authorities shall be binding on all Registering Authorities. 


(5) The tubes of boilers and heat exchangers made of titanium and other exotic metals may 
be approved as per international codes, including American Society of Mechanical 
Engineers (ASME), British Standards (BS), European Standards (EN), DIN, Tubular 
Exchanger Manufacturers Association (TEMA)with the minimum thickness specified in 
those codes of manufacture. 


4. Inspectionof boiler to comply into any foreign code—Notwithstanding anything 
contained in these regulations, the inspecting authority may inspect any boiler meant for 
export during the various stages of its construction so as to comply with the requirements of 
any foreign code and may grant a certificate in Part-A of Form-l. 


5. Exemption of boiler or boiler components.—Under sub-section (4) of section 38 of the Act, 
any boiler or boiler component may be exempted in the whole or any part of the State from 
the operation of all or any of the provisions of the Act, subject to the following conditions, 
namely:- 


(!) Design and construction of boiler or boiler component is in accordance with 
international code or standard including British Standards (BS), European 
Standards (EN), American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Boiler and 
Pressure Vessel Code, Tubular Exchanger Manufacturers Association (TEMA), 
Technical Requirements Document (TRD), GOST and Japanese _ Industrial 
Standards (JIS); 

(2) Materials used in the construction are not specifically prohibited under these 
regulations; 

(3) Design, construction and materials of boiler or boiler components are satisfied by 
the State Governments by necessary tests and examination like Remnant Life 
Assessment, which shall be carried out by the owner. 


6.Fee not prescribed in regulations. For any activity, which in the opinion of a State 
Government involves time and labour and for which no fee has been prescribed in these 
regulations, may be prescribed by the State Government.

25. Procedure for recognition of Competent Person.— 

(l)(a)This regulation provides requirements for the uniform qualification, examination, 
issuance and renewal of Central Boiler Board authorisation to act as a competent person for 
inspection and certification of boilers and boiler components under the Act during 
manufacture, erection, operation and maintenance throughout India. 


(2) Minimum qualifications and experience required are as under.— 


(a) shall be a graduate in Mechanical Engineering or Production or Power Plant or 
Metallurgical Engineering from a recognised institute; 


(0) minimum five years experience singly or cumulatively in the following fields related to 
boilers:- 
(i) Design; 
(ii) Manufacture; 
(iii) Commissioning; 
(iv) Operation and maintenance; 
(v) Inspection and_ certification during manufacture or operation and

American Society for Non-Destructive Testing (ASNT) or any other professional body 
recognised by ISNT or ASNT in Non-Destructive methods of testing in radiography and 
ultrasonic testing. 


(3) Central Boilers Board Examination Standing Committee Composition: -(a)For the 
purpose of these regulations, the Central Boilers Board constitutes the ‘Central Boilers 
Board Examination Standing Committee” consisting of the following persons-

interests - Members 
(0) Secretary, Central Boilers Board shall nominate the members; 


(4) The Process for Central Boilers Board Examination shall be as under— 

(a)an examination shall be conducted by the Central Boilers Board Examination Standing 
Committee or an agency or Regional Examination Standing Committees authorised by 
it, as per the following examination methods, namely: - 

(i) written examination consisting of design, manufacture, operation and maintenance of 


the boiler, Non Destructive Testing Techniques, inspection and certification of boilers 
during manufacture and use as per theseregulations( 70% weightage); 

(ii) candidate shall be required to secure at least 45% marks in each written examination 
papers and at least 60% marks in aggregate to qualify for viva-voce; 

(iii) viva-voce on the above (30% weightage ); 

(iv) candidate shall secure at least 60% marks in aggregate (written exam with 70% 
weightage and viva-voce with 30% weightage) in order to pass the examination; 


(v) the Central Boilers Board shall issue a passing grade certificate to the candidate 
after passing the examination; 


(6) application for appearing in the Central Boiler Board Examination shall be made in the 
format as provided by the Central Boilers Board Examination Standing Committee at 
such place and time as decided by the Central Boilers Board Examination Standing 
Committee or an agency or Regional Examination Standing Committees authorised by 
it.

(5) The process for Central Boilers Board authorisation shall be as under: — 
(a) the Competent Person shall perform the work without conflict of interest; 
(b) an applicant for a Central Boiler Board Authorisation shall meet the following 
requirements, namely:- 

(i) the applicant shall be in regular employment of, and exclusively engaged by a 
Central Boilers Board recognised Inspecting Authority: 

Provided that for inspection and certification of boilers during use under 
section 3 of the Act, applicant can work independently also without taking 
employment with the Central Boilers Board recognised Inspecting Authority ; 

(ii) | the applicant shall meet the minimum qualification and experience requirements 
as referred in sub-regulation (2) of this regulation; 

(iii) | the applicant shall have taken and passed the Central Boilers Board examination 
as referred to in sub-regulation (4) of this regulation; 

(iv) the applicant shall apply for an authorisation not later than three years after 
passing the Central Boilers Board Examination and a person whose authorisation 
has not been issued within the three year period shall be required to take the 
Central Boiler Board Examination and receive a passing grade; and 

(v) | the maximum age for the Competent Person shall be sixty-five years provided the 
person is medically fit; 


(c) (i) when the applicant meets the requirements as referred to in clause (b)and at the 
request of the applicant’s employer; a Central Boilers Board authorisation card and 
a certificate shall be issued: 

Provided that the request for authorisation card, only for undertaking 
inspection and certification of boilers during use under section 3 of the Acct, 
may also be made by the applicant; 

(ii) the application for an authorisation shall be on forms available with the Central 
Boilers Board; and 
(iii) a Competent Person may possess only one valid authorisation card; 


(d) (i) the validity of an authorisation certificate shall be three years from the date of issue or in 
co-terminus with the validity period of recognition of employing Inspecting Authority 
(wherever applicable), whichever is earlier; 


(ii) for undertaking inspection and certification of boilers during manufacture and 
erection, the Competent Person must be in regular employment of the Central Boiler 
Board recognised Inspecting Authority failing which the authorisation lapses; 


(iii) where the Competent Person leaves the employment, Central Boilers Board 
Authorisation Card shall be surrendered by the Inspecting Authority to the Secretary, 
Central Boilers Board within a period of seven days from the date of such leave; 


(iv) the request for renewal shall be made by Competent Person’s employer and the request

requirement as laid down in sub-clause (vi):

Procuring of materials. — (|) Where procuring materials directly from mills is 


not feasible due to small quantity, the following method shall be adopted, namely:- 


(a) materials fully identifiable, supported by a materials test report by material 
manufacturer but not covered by a form under these regulations,— 

(i) when a material is received with complete identification marks applied by the 
mill and supported by a materials test report, the manufacturer of boiler, boiler 
component, and spares shall demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Inspecting 
Authority that all requirements of the material specification specified under 
these regulations have been met; 

(ii) the materials test report issued by materials manufacturer shall be presented 
to the Inspecting Authority for verification; 

(iii) any additional tests as determined by the Inspecting Authority shall be 
conducted in a test house and results documented; 

(iv) Form-IV(Part-B) shall be prepared with specification, size, quantity, reported 
test results and jointly signed by manufacturer of boiler, boiler component or 
spares and the Inspecting Authority; 


(b) materials fully identifiable with mill markings for a production lot but not 
supported by materials test reports and forms under these regulations,— 


(i) the manufacturer of boiler, boiler components or spares shall present such 
materials to the Inspecting Authority for as marked by the mill. Shipping 
document or purchase order or as the case may be, drawing are also to be 
presented to establish required specification of materials; 

(ii) testing of materials shall be conducted as per materials specification and 


additional requirements of these regulations, if any; 

(iii) number of samples for tests shall be determined by the Inspecting Authority but 
not less than 0% of the quantity under consideration; 

(iv) test results are to be recorded in Form-IV(Part-B), signed by manufacturer and 
the Inspecting Authority; 

(५) plates or sheets qualified in the manner as provided above shall not be

29. Registration of second-hand boilers not in accordance with the standard 
conditions.—lf a second hand boiler is not conforming to the requirements of these regulations 
for its registration, then the same shall not be registered except in the following cases, namely:— 


(7) Water Tube Boilers: Where the documents required under its code of manufacture for 
its registration are furnished and its workmanship is not in any way doubtful, the second- 
hand Water Tube Boiler may be registered by reducing the working pressure of the parts of 
the boiler as calculated from the regulations by ten percent: 


Provided that a higher working pressure, being not more than the working 
pressure allowed by the code of manufacture, may be allowed on the recommendation

PART-II 


3. Materials ofconstruction for carbon, alloy,stainless steel and nickel alloy plates. — 
() Steel for plates shall be made by the open hearth, electric furnace or basic oxygen 
process or any other process which gives steel having equivalent specified properties. 


(2) General deoxidation practice shall be appropriate to the type of steel used, 
particularly where the deoxidation practice influences the level of the elevated 
temperature properties of steel. 


(3) Semi-killed steel may be used for plates in carbon(C) and carbon manganese(C- 
Mn) steel with an upper limit of the tensile strength not exceeding 56 kg /mm* and 
with thickness not exceeding 50 millimetre(mm). 


(4) The steel may be strand cast or cast in stationary molds. 


(5) If heats of the same nominal chemical composition are consecutively strand cast 
at one time, the heat number assigned to the cast product (slab) may remain 
unchanged until all the steel in the slab is from different heat. 


(6) When two consecutively strand cast heats have different nominal chemical 
composition ranges, the manufacturer shall remove the transition material by any 
procedure that positively separates the grades. 


(7) The ratio of reduction of thickness from a strand-cast slab to plate shall be at least 
3:, except that reduction ratios as low as 2:| are permitted if all the following 
limitations are complied with, namely:- 


(a) The specified plate thickness is seventy-fivemillimetre(mm)or more. 

(0) One or more of the following low hydrogen practices are used, namely:- 
(i) vacuum degassing during steelmaking; 

(ii) controlled soaking of the slabs or plates; 

(iii) controlled slow cooling of the slabs or plates. 

(c) The sulphur content is 0.004 percent or less, based upon heat analysis. 


(d) One or more of the following practices are used, namely:-(i) electromagnetic 
stirring during strand casting; 


(ii) soft reduction during strand casting; 

(iii) neavy pass reductions or other special practices during plate rolling; 
(iv) combined forging and rolling during plate rolling. 
( 


e) The plates are ultrasonically examined based on continuous scanning over 
hundred percent of the plate surface. 


(f) The plates are through-thickness tension tested. 


(g) Unless otherwise specified in the purchase order, plates shall be produced 
from plate-as-rolled. 
(8) Plates of fusion welded boiler drums, vessels, separators, headers and other 
pressure parts shall conform to the chemical composition given in Table 2/2in this 
chapter. 


(9) The steel shall not contain more than 0.05 per cent of sulphur or phosphorus. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 673 


(0) When the material is required for flame cutting or weldingor both, the carbon 
content shall not exceed 0.30% and due precautions shall be taken when the carbon 
content exceeds 0.26percent. 


(7) When steels are intended for service temperatures over 37/°C, the silicon 
content shall be not less than 0.i0percent or alternatively, the material shall be 
required topass the proof test for creep quality of carbon steel plates of boiler quality. 


(2) (a) In case of Carbon Steel,— 


(i) Plates having thickness of twelvemillimetre(mm)or less than that, not intended 
for hot forming, can be supplied in unnormalised or as rolled condition subject 
to the condition that the code of manufacture provides for the same. 


(ii) For plates having thickness more than twelve millimetre(mm), not intended for 
hot forming, shall be supplied in the normalised conditions: 


(iii) If normalising is to be performed by the fabricator, the plates shall be either 
normalised or heated uniformly for hot forming. However, the temperature to 
which the plates are heated for hot forming does not significantly exceed the 
normalising temperature: 


Provided that such normalising may be exemptedby the Competent 
Personif it is demonstrated by the manufacturer that equivalent properties can 
be produced by the rolling subsequent cooling. 


(iv) The boiler manufacturer may, if he so wishes order a check analysis.

(0) In case ofAlloy Steel,— 


(i) Except for Grade Qiplates, all plates shall be thermally treated either by 
annealing, normalising and tempering, or, when permitted by the purchaser, 
accelerated cooling from the austenitising temperature by air blasting or liquid 
quenching, followed by tempering. 


(ii) Grade 9 plates shall be thermally treated, either by normalising-and-tempering 
or by accelerated cooling from the austenitising temperature by air blasting or 
liquid quenching, followed by tempering. 

(iii) Grade 9/ plates shall be austenitised at 040°C to 080°C and shall be 
tempered at 730°C to 800°C. 


(c)In case ofStainless Steel,—The material shall be solution annealed to meet the 
mechanical property requirements of the applicable material grades. 


(d) In case ofNickel Alloys,—Grade N0667 shall be solution annealed at 50°C 
to 7230°C and quenched in water or rapidly cooled by other means. 


32.Freedom from defects, etc.— (l)Minor surface defects of the plates may be removed by 
mechanical means to achieve a smooth level surface provided that the minimum specified 
thickness is maintained. 
(2) Surface defects may be repaired by welding, only with approval of the Inspecting 
Authority provided that the plate is stress relieved after welding where necessary.

34. Testing and inspection. —The tests and inspections shall be made at the place of 
manufacture prior to despatch; but in the event of any of the material proving unsatisfactory 
in the course of being worked into boilers, such material shall be rejected, despite any 
previous certificate of satisfactory testing, and such further tests of the material from the 
same charge shall be made as the Competent Person may consider desirable. 


35. Selection of test pieces.—All test piecesof material shall be selected by the Competent 
Person and tested in his presence, andthereafter he shall satisfy himself that the conditions 
herein described are fulfilled. 


36. Tensile test pieces. —(l)The tensile test pieces shall be as per the relevant material 
specifications. 


(2) For plate thickness exceeding 60 millimetre(mm), test pieces shall be taken from the 
exterior third of the plate cross-section and wherever practicable, the rolled surface 
shall be retained on two opposite sides of the test piece.

38. Number of tensile tests.—Forthe purpose of test ofshell plates, butt straps and plates, 
gusset plates, end plates, furnace plates and flanging plates, one tensile test piece shall be 
cut from each plate as rolled. 


39. Bend testsin case ofcold bends,—(l)Test pieces shall be sheared lengthwise or 
crosswise from plates or bars, and shall not be less than 38 millimetre(mm) wide, but for small 
bars the whole section may be used. 


(2) (a)ln all cold bend tests, on samples 73 millimetre(mm) in thickness and above, the 
rough edge or burcaused by shearing may be removed by filling or grinding and 
samples 25 millimetre(mm) in thickness and above may have the edges machined, 
but the test pieces shall receive no other preparation. 

(0) The test pieces shall not be annealed unless the material from which they are 
cut is similarly annealed and in such case the test piece shall be similarly treated 
with the material before testing.

(4) For small sectional material the bend tests may be made from the flattened bar. 


(5) Bend tests may be made either by pressure or by blows. 


40.Number of bend tests.—A bend test shall be taken from each plate as rolled. The bend 
tests from shell plates, butt straps and other plates which have not to be flanged or worked 
in the fire or which when in use are not to be exposed to flame, shall be cold bend tested. 


4. Additional tests before rejection.—(i)(a)lfthe test pieces first selected by the 
Competent Person fail to fulfil the test requirementsunder these regulations, two further tests 
of the same heat may be made, but if either of these fail, the plates or bars from which test 
pieces were cut shall be rejected. 

(0) In all such cases further tests shall be made before any material from the same charge 
can be accepted. 


(2) If the unsatisfactory result of a test is due to technical conditions of the testing method or 
to a closely limited defect of a test piece, then, the failure can be left out of consideration 
in decision on the fulfilment of the requirement and another test piece may be 
substituted. 


(3)lf the unsatisfactory result of test is due to an unfavourable heat treatment, the plate and 
the test strip may be heat treated againandthereafter, the entire test shall be repeated. 


42.Branding.—(|)Every plate, section and bar shall be clearly and distinctly marked by the 
maker at two places with the number of identification mark by which they can be traced to 
the charge from which the material was made. 


(2) Every plate shall also be stamped by the steel maker as provided in IS: 2002andwiththe 
following information, namely:- 
(a) Name of manufacturer; 
(b) Specification; 
(c) Heat Number; 
(d) Plate Number, and 
(e) Stamp. 


43. Defacing of rejected material—In the event of the material failing to withstand the 
prescribed tests, the identification mark of the Competent Person which has been 
stamped on the material, shall be defaced by punch marks extending beyond the 
identification mark, in the form of a cross, thus denoting that the material has failed. 


680 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


44. Facilities for inspection— The maker shall adopt a system of making the ingots, billets, 
slabs, plates, bars, etc. so as to enable finished material to be traced to the original 
charge, and the Inspector or Competent Person, as the case may be, shall be given 
every facilityobymaker for tracing all plates and bars to their respective charges, and for 
witnessing the required testsand when Inspector or Competent Person, as the case may 
beis satisfied with the material and with the results of the tests,thelnspector or Competent 
Person, as the case may be,shall be provided two copies of test reports of the material for 
his signature. 


45.Steel not produced where rolled.—(l)Where steel is not produced in the works at which 
it is rolled, a certificate in Form V(Part-A)or Form IV(Part-C), as the case may be, shall be 
supplied to the Competent Person deputed to witness the testing of the material, stating 
the Open Hearth or Electric Process or any of the Oxygen Processes by which it was 
made, the name of the Steel-Maker who supplied it, also the numbers of the charges for 
reference to the books of the Steel-Maker. 

(2)The number of the charge shall be marked on each plate or bar for the purpose of 
identification. 


46. Maker’s certificate Before the mill sheets are signed, the maker shall furnish to the 


Competent Person with a certificate inForm V(Part-A)or Form IV(Part-C), as the case 
may be, guaranteeing that the material has been made by an Open Hearth or an Electric 
Process, acid or basic, and that it withstands satisfactorily test described above in the 
presence of the Competent Person.

48.Selection of Tubes for Test—(l) (a) (i)Test specimens required for the flattening, 
expandingor flaring test specifiedherein below shall be taken from the ends of finished tubes 
prior to upsetting swaging, expanding or any other forming operations or being cut to length. 
(ii) They shall be smooth on the ends and free from burrs and flaws. 


(b) (i) If desirable and practicable tensile test may be carried out on full section of the 


tubes up to the capacity of the testing machine. 


(ii) For large size tubes, the tensile test specimen shall consist of strip cut longitudinally 
from the tube and which is not straightened within the gauge length and further heat 
treated. 


(c) If any test specimen shows flaws or defective machining it shall be discarded and 


(d) All specimens shall be tested at room temperature. 


another specimen be taken into consideration. 


(2)(a)The test specified herein below shall be made on minimum two tubes for first hundred 
tubes and one per hundredor part thereof for tubes over 00 numbers from each lot. 


(b)Lot applies to all tube of same size andwall thickness of same heat andheat treatment. 


(3) (a)The test specimen shall comply with the requirementsas specified in table 2/9. 


(o)The hardness test may be carried out on the wall cross section or on a flat on the 
outside surface of the tube sample.

(b) (i)Pipes of grades Pi, P2, P5, P9, PI, P2, and P22 except P9, X20CrMoV2 
and N0667 shall be reheated and furnished in full annealed, isothermal annealed or 
normalised and tempered condition. 


(ii) If furnished in the normalised and tempered condition, the minimum tempering 
temperature for grade Pi, P2, P!! and Pi2 shall be 650°C and the minimum 
tempering temperature for grades P5, P9 and P22 shall be 675°C. 


(c)Pipes of grades Pi, P2 and P2 either hot finished or cold drawn may be given a final 


heat treatment at 650°C to 705°C, instead of heat treatment specified in clause (b) 
above at the option of the manufacturer. 


(0) Grades P9 shall be normalised at 040°C minimum and tempered at 730°C 
minimum as a final heat treatment. 


(e) Grades X20CrMoV2 shall be normalised at 020°C - 070°C and tempered at 
730°C - 780°C for a period of one hour minimum. 

(f) Grade NO667 shall be solution annealed at 50°C to 230°C and quenched in 
water or rapidly cooled by other means. 


(5) —(a)(i)The pipes shall be finished, cleaned free from harmful defects. 
(ii) They shall be reasonably straight, smooth, cylindrical and subject to the tolerance 
specified in this sub-regulation. Pipes manufacturer shall explore a sufficient number of 
visual inspections to provide reasonable assurance that they have been properly 
evaluated.

PART-V 


50.Castings of carbon, alloy and stainless steel.-() This regulation shall cover carbon, 
alloy and stainless steel castings used in the construction of boilers and steam pipes, 
including their fittings. 


(2) (a) All castings shall be supplied in the heat-treated conditionas following:- 
(i) carbon steel castings: annealing, or normalising, or normalising and tempering. 


(ii) alloy steel castings: annealing, or normalising and tempering, or hardening 
orquenching and tempering. 


(iii) stainless steel castings: solution annealing. 


(b) Heat treatment shall be carried out either at the discretion of the manufacturer or 
the Competent Person and shall be carried out at suitable temperatures to give 
the mechanical properties specified in regulation 54. 


(3) All castings shall be properly fettled and dressed and all surfaces shall be 
satisfactorily cleaned for inspection purposes. 


(4) The castings can be supplied as cast, rough machined or after final machining. The 
Non-Destructive Testing may be performed in as cast or in machined condition as 
per the non-destructive examination(NDE)requirements of relevant material 
specifications. 


5. Process of manufacture.— () The steel used for castings shall be made by an Open 
Hearth or Electric Furnace or any other process which gives steel having equivalent 


properties. 


(2) The steel shall comply with the chemical composition specified in the Table 2/32.

52. Freedom from and rectification of defects.-The steel castings shall have clean 
surfaces and shall be free from defectsand the specified permissible variations in size or 
thickness shall not be exceeded. Defects may be repaired by welding only, with the 
approval of the Inspecting Authority provided that the castings are stress-relieved after 
welding if necessary. 


53. Number of testsand provision of test samples.—Tensile and bend test pieces shall be 
prepared from test samples representative of each melt or heat-treatment batch as 
following:- 


(i) 


(ii) 


(v) 


(a)The test samples shall be cast attached to or separate from the castings as 
agreed between the manufacturer and the Competent Person. 

(b) The agreement for attached test samples shall include the precise location and 
method of attachment. If the Competent Person fails to make such an agreement 
with the manufacturer, the decision as to the manner of providing test samples shall 
rest with the manufacturer. 

(c)The discretion of the manufacturer shall not, however, apply to the testing of 
castings made from more than one melt as indicated in sub-regulation(4) below. 


(a)lf the test samples are attached to the castings, at least one tensile test, and 
when required one bend test, shall be made from each melt. 

(b) Such test samples shall not be detached from the castings until heat-treatment 
of the castings has been completed and they have been stamped by the Competent 
Person. 

(c) Test samples shall be stamped by the Competent Person after that heat- 
treatment process. 


(a)lf the test samples are cast separately, they shall be provided to the extent of 2 
per cent of the number of castings from each melt, but in no case there shall be less 
than 2 samples per melt, except by agreement between the manufacturer and the 
Competent Person. 

(b) The test samples shall be cast in moulds of the same material as is used for the 
castings and shall be made at the same time as the castings, and run from the 
same ladle. 

(c) The samples shall be stamped by the Competent Person so as to identify the 
castings to which they relate. 


(a)When a casting is made from more than one melt, at least four tensile tests, and 
where required four bends tests, shall be made from test samples situated as far 
apart as possible on the casting. 

(b) Some of the test samples shall be taken from as near the top and others near 
from the bottom of the casting as is practicable. 


Test samples shall be heat-treated with the castings they represent.

57. Procedure for welding.—()In order to maintain a high standard of workmanship in the 
practice of arc-welding repair to steel castings, a written down procedure taking care of the 
following requirements shall be followed. 


(2) (a) The surfaces of the steel, it is intended to weld shall be cleaned and freed from all 
foreign matter, otherwise it may resultinpoor penetration and unsoundweld metal. 


(b) The preparation for the welding of cracks shall be of the U or V types. When the later 
is used, the included angle shallbe not less than 70. Where cracks extend through 
the section of the casting, the choice between single and double preparation, U or V 
will be governed by: 


(i) the thickness of the casting; 
(ii) the location of the defect. In double preparation, U or V the root of the U or V 
should be sufficiently open to ensure complete penetration. 


(3) The selection of electrodes shall be compatible with the relevant material groups. The 
electrode manufacturer's recommendations for the use of the electrode shall be strictly 
followed. 


(4) Variations in composition, mass design and the extent of welding required make it 
impossible to lay down specific rules to establish conditions under which pre-heating 
should be applied.When after consideration of each casting in the light of the above 
variables it is deemed necessary to pre-heat, such pre-heating should be carried out at a 
temperature of 750°C-300°C. 


(5) (a)When the welding is carried out after the casting has received its normal heat 
treatment, a further heat treatment may be considered necessary. This treatment need 
be applied only in cases where welding has been such as to induce either internal 
stresses which would be detrimental to the casting, or locally hardened areas which 
would cause difficulty in machining. Where this further beat treatment is applied, the 
casting, where possible, should not be allowed to go cold after welding, but should be 
charged into a warm furnace and re-heated to a suitable tempering temperature which in 
general should be not less than 550°C. 


(6) When considering the advisability of applying this further treatment, its effect on the 
physical properties of the castings shallbe borne in mind. If the treatment, or the welding 
itself is such that the physical properties will be adversely affected, the full heat treatment 
required to produce satisfactory qualities shallbe substituted. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3()] 


भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण

(3) Heat treatment shall be as per relevant material specifications. 


(4) Where not machined, the forgings, shall have workman like surfaces as normally 
obtained by rolling, forging or drawing. 


Provided that the minimum required thickness is maintained, minor surface defects 
may be admitted and other defects removed by mechanical means so as to achieve a 
smooth surface. Surface defects may also be repaired, by welding only, with the 
approval of the Inspecting Authority provided that the parts are stress-relieved after 
welding where necessary. 


59. Selection of test pieces.—(i) For testing, either the parts themselves shall be used or 
additional material or sufficient size for test pieces shall be available. In the case of headers 
for examples, surplus lengths for test rings may be used. In the case of flanges swaged in 
dies, the punching left may be used as test pieces, in which case the identity of the material 
of the punching with that of the flange shall be evidenced in an adequate manner. The test 
may be performed also on the semi-finished material for example a bar or a billet, provided it 
is given approximately the same reduction and heat-treatment as the finished forging. For 
headers with closed ends, the test rings shall be cut off before dishing or reducing and shall 
be subjected to the same heat treatment as the headers themselves. In the case of 
headers, which are closed by special covers, the test ring shall be cut off after heat 
treatment. Similar procedure shall be followed for test pieces of other forgings. 


(2) For testing, piece of one and the same cast of the same heat treatment batch as well as 
of similar dimensions may be gathered into one group and at least one test piece shall 
be made from each group. 


(3) Tangential test piece shall be used for headers where practicable. For header with 
outside diameter less than 200 mn, longitudinal test pieces may be allowed.

6i. Bend tests.— ()Bend test pieces shall be of rectangular cross-section machined to a

mm. The test pieces shall be bent over the thinner section. 


(2) Test pieces shall be bent when cold through an angle of 780° without fracture, the 
internal radius of the bend being not greater than that specified in Table 2/37 for the 25 mm 
wide by 9 mm thick test piece.

62. Additional tests before rejection.— (|) In case either a tensile or a bend test fails, two 
further tests of the type which failed may be made on test pieces out from the same forging. 
If the results obtained from these retests are satisfactory, the forging shall be accepted, 
provided that in other respects they fulfil the conditions laid down above for steel forgings. If 
these retests do not give satisfactory results, the forgings represented may be re-heat- 
treated together with the remainder of the test blocks and presented for further testing. 


(2) In all cases where final retests do not give satisfactory results, the forgings represented 
by the test pieces which fail shall be rejected. 


PART-VII 


63.GENERAL GREY IRON CASTINGS (GRADE A).— (l) The castings shall be cast from 
metal melted or refined in any metallurgical plant other than an iron ore smelting furnace, for 
the use of which furnace permission in writing must be received from the Inspecting 
Authority. 


(2) The Composition of the iron as cast shall be left to the discretion of the manufacturer but 
the maximum percentage of phosphorus or sulphur or both may be specified by the 
Inspecting Authority, if it so desires. 


(3) The castings shall be accurately moulded in accordance with the pattern or working 
drawings supplied by the Inspecting Authority with the addition of such letters, figures or 
marks as may be specified and the drawings shall include the tolerances specified in the 
regulation. 


(4) (a)The castings shall be sound, clean out of twist and free from blow holes distortion 
and all surface and other defects. 
(0) They shall be well dressed or fettled and shall be machinable by normal methods. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण

64. Provision of test bars.—(|) Prior to testing, the Inspecting Authority shall state whether 
it requires tensile or transverse tests, or both, and itmay also specify cast on bars where the 
design of the casting and method of running permit. 

(2)(a)When the test bars are cast separately they shall be poured at the same time 
and from the same ladle, or metal as the casting or castings they represent. 

(0) The number of test specified in regulation 69 shall be applicable to all castings of 
each melt. 

(3)When the bars are cast-on, the mould for the casting and the mould for the test 
piece shall be joined together in such a manner that the liquid metal fills both moulds at the 
same operation. 

(4)All test bars shall be cast in green sand or dry sand or in loam moulds according 
to whether the casting or castings they represent are moulded in green sand, or in loam or 
dry sand, respectively. 


(5) The test bars shall not be subjected to any heat treatment after leaving the 
moulds.

PART-VIII 


7i.COVERED ELECTRODES FOR SHIELDED METAL ARC’ WELDING —(l) 
(a)(i) Thisregulationshallapply to covered electrodes of sizes 2.0 mm and larger in diameter 
for shielded metal arc welding of carbon steel, low alloy steels, stainless steels and non- 
ferrous materials. (ii)Electrodesofless than 2.0 mm in diameter shall not be used in boilers. 


(2 


(0) The covered electrode shall comply with the requirements specified in these 


regulations. 


(c) The characteristics and behaviour under ordinary working conditions shall be 
such that satisfactory weld deposits can be made by a welder of average skill and 
experience and that the following characteristics are obtained,namely:- 

(i) relative ease in the control of the slag and weld metal during welding; 


iii) nO undue degree of spatter; 


v) easy removability of the slag; 


ee अल अओअल अल अल 


— 


ii) good degree of stability of the arc; 


vi) no undue tendency to under-cut; 
vii)desired contour of the weld deposits: and 
(viii) low internal porosity of the weld metal. 


iv) desired rate of deposition and depth of penetration. 


The covered electrodes shall be classified into following categories and in 


accordance with applicable Specifications for Filler Alloys (SFA) of American Society 
of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Part IIC specificationsor AWS (American Welding 


Society) specifications or equivalent: 


Carbon steel electrodes 
Low alloy steel electrodes 
Stainless steel electrodes

(3) Covered electrodes may be made by any method that shall yield a product 
conforming to the requirements of these regulations and relevant Specifications for 
Filler Alloys (SFA)or American Welding Society (AWS) specification. 


(4) (a)The nominal size of the covered electrodes shall refer to the diameter of the core 
wire and the length shall not exceed 450 mm with provision for end gripping. 
(o)The tolerance on the specified diameter of the core wire of the electrodes shall be 
+ 0.05 mm. 
(c)The tolerance on the length of the electrodes shall be +0 mm or as specified in 
relevant Specifications for Filler Alloys (SFA)or American Welding Society (AWS) 
specifications. 


(5 


— 


(a)The core wire and covering shall be free from defects that would interfere with the 
uniform deposition of electrode. 

(b)The flux covering shall be sufficiently robust to withstand the normal conditions of 
transport, storage, handling and use, without damage and shall be uniform in 
thickness all over so that it fuses evenly. 

(c) The covering shall be concentric with coreand the permissible variation on 
maximum core plus one covering shall not exceed the minimum core plus one 
covering as under: 


(i) For diameter up to 2.5 mm 7 % of mean dimension, 
(ii) For diameter 3.2 to 4.0 mm 5 % of mean dimension, and 


(iii) For diameter 5 mm and larger 4 % of mean dimension. 


(6) At least one imprint of electrode classification shall be imprinted at the covering 
within 65 mm of grip end. The imprinting shall be legible both before and after 
welding. 


(7) (a)Covered electrodes shall be suitably packed to guard against damage during 
transportation. When stored, the electrodes shall be kept in their original bundles or 
packing in a dry store room and under such conditions, the electrodes shall be 
capable of giving results similar to those which they would have given on the date of 
their dispatch from the manufacturer for a period of two years or as recommended by 
the electrode manufacturer whichever is less. Usage of electrodes beyond this period 
may be permitted after conducting check tests as per specification, provided it is not 
restricted by the electrode manufacturer.

72.RODS AND ELECTRODES FOR GAS SHIELDED ARC 
WELDING.—(l)(a)Thisregulation apply to electrodes and rods of sizes 0.8 mm and larger in

of AWS or SFA specifications.

welding. 


(i) relative ease in the control of the molten pool during welding;

(iv) desired rate of deposition and depth of penetration. 

(v) no undue tendency to under-cut;

(vii) low internal porosity of the weld metal.

PART-I 


77. Preparation of plates.— (|)The edges of all plates and butt straps shall be machined or 
flame cut by machine and the caulking edges shall be bevelled to an angle not sharper than 
20° to the plane of the plate and between 70° and 80°wherever practicable. Gusset Plates 
may be sheared except on those edges, which are to be welded. 


(2)Plates which are to be flame-cut by machine without heat treatment or subsequent 
grinding or machining shall not have a carbon content higher than 0.25 per cent. 


(3) Where the carbon content exceeds 0.25 percent, heat treatment, grinding or 
machining shall be carried out. 


(4) The edges of all plates shall have a smooth finish. 


(5) Before commencingwelding of the joint (apart from tack welding), it shall be 
ascertained that the chamfered edges are in alignment and that the defects in 
alignment between the surfaces of the plates do not exceed as given in the table 3/:

78. Normalising or stress relieving of steel plates— (l) All plates which have been 
dished or flanged shall be stress relieved as components when cold worked and normalized 
when hot worked fully or partially. 


(2)Stress relieving of components may be combined with final stress relieving when 
stress relieving is envisaged later. 


79. Minimum thickness of plates.—No boiler plate shall be less than 6 mm in thickness. 
PART-II 


80.Cylindrical shells — (l) Each ring shall be formed from not more than two plates and 
rolled to cylindrical form to the extreme ends of the plate. The bending shall be done entirely 
by machine. Local heating or hammering shall not be used for correction of profile. 


(2)The longitudinal seam or seams may be placed in any suitable position but the 
seams in successive rings shall not fall in line and shall be staggered by minimum 50 mm. 


(3)In the case of brick set boilers the seam or seams shall be kept as far as 
practicable clear of the brickwork. 


8. Position of longitudinal seams.—Each ring of plate forming the shell, barrel or drum 
shell, where practicable, be in one piece and have its longitudinal seam well out of line with 
those of the adjoining rings. In Lancashire, Cornish, and other types of boilers, where parts 
of the shell are exposed to flame, the longitudinal seams shell, where practicable, be in the 
steam space, arranged alternately on each side of the crown and clear of the brick work. 


82. Circumferential and end seams.—Joint efficiency of circumferential seams shall be 
determined as detailed in sub-regulation (i) of regulation 769. In the event of tube holes 
forming a ligament at the location of circumferential seams, the joint efficiency shall be 
calculated as per regulation 77. 


83.Angle rings.—Angle rings for the attachment of end plates to shell plates and/or flue 
sections shall be rolled or machined so that they fit closely to the flat and cylindrical surfaces 
to be connected, and shall be machined or machine gas cut on the caulking edges. 


84. Thickness of shell angle rings.—Where shell plates and end plate are connected by 
means of an external angle ring, the angle rings shallnot be less in thickness than as follows:

85.Welded shell plates.—The requirements of welded shells shall be covered by the

PART-II 


86. Flat end plates.— (l) Wherever practicable, the flat or dished end plates of boilers shall 
be in one piece made from one rolled plate. Where diameter of boiler is so large as to make 
this impracticable, the flat end plates may be made from two pieces by fusion butt-welding. 
(See figures 2/ and 2/2). In the latter case, the line of welding shall be parallel to the 
horizontal axis of the boiler and shall be subjected to full radiographic examination. 


(2) Flanging of plates shall be done by machine. Cold forming of flanged end plate shall 
be followed by heat treatment. Such flanging shall be done hot, preferably in one 
operation, but where this is impracticable creep machine flanging may be used 
provided that the plate is worked at a suitable temperature and heated for an 
adequate distance beyond that portion of the plate under immediate treatment. 


(3) Hot forming of welded plates shall be permitted provided that the welded joint is 
subjected to 00 percent radiographic or Ultrasonic examination after hot forming. 


(4) Welded plates up to and including 20 mm thickness can be cold formed provided it 
complies with following conditions. 


(a) Before cold forming, the weld reinforcement shall be ground smooth, and the 
manufacturer shall take precautions, where necessary, in order to avoid crack 
formation in the weld metal or the heat affected zone. 


(b) If the inside radius of curvature after forming is less than 0 times the 
thickness, stress relieving shall be carried out. 


(c) After cold forming, the welded joints shall be visually examined and subjected 
to 00 percent radiographic or Ultrasonic examination throughout their length. 
Joints of any thickness which have been cold formed to a radius less than 0 
times the thic 


(d) kness shall be inspected for cracks by magnetic particle or penetrant 
methods. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


725 


(6) After completion of the flanging operation flanges shall be of true peripheral 
contour (either circular or straight as necessary to ensure accurate alignment 
with the connecting parts), and of good surface, free from bulges, grooves or 
other local irregularities; flat portions of the plate shall be free from set or 
distortion. 


(5) In the construction of unfired boilers when the dished ends do not form a part of the 
heating surface cold spun dished ends conforming to IS: 2825 may be used. 


(6) Care shall be taken to see that the flanges are circular and of good surface, free from 
local irregularities, and that they are parallel and square with the flat part of the plate. 


(7) Flat portions of end plates, on completion of all flanging and machining operations, 
shall be flat and free from set or distortion. 


87. Strengthening of flat end plate at manhole— (]) In all cases, the front end plate 
gusset stays below the furnaces shall be placed as closely as possible to the mudhole 
frame. 


(2) Where flat end plates are flanged for connection to the shell, the inside radius of 
flanging shall be not less than .75 times the plate thickness, with a minimum of 38 mm. 


88. End Plates in steam spaces.—When the end plates of boilers situated in the steam 
space are liable to contact with hot gases, the end plates shall be efficiently shielded from 
such contact. 


89. Hemispherical crowns.— (l) The segments for hemispherical shell crown plates shall 
be pressed in one heat to correct curvature and shall be butt-welded together in accordance 
with Figures 2/3, 2/4, 72/5 or 2/6. The cylindrical portion of the crown shall be tangential 
to the hemispherical portion. 


(2) Where hemispherical furnace crowns are pressed from one plate, they shall be 
pressed to form by machine in progressive stages without thinning and shall be 
annealedon completion. 


90. Dished end and crown plates.— () The dished end plates of boilers shall bepreferably 
in one piece made from one-rolled plate. If this is impracticable, owing to the large diameter, 
the dished end plate may be made from two plates, fusion butt welded together and in such 
cases the requirements of stress relieving and radiographic examination as provided for in 
regulation 86 shall apply and the line of weld shall be parallel to the horizontal axis of the 
boiler. 


(2) The inside radius to which a plate is dished shall not be greater than the external 
diameter of the shell to which it is attached, except in the case of Lancashire and 
Cornish boilers when the radius shall not exceed ’% times the diameter of the shell. 


726 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(3) The inside radius of curvature of the flanges to the shell or firebox shall not be less 
than four times the thickness of the crown or end plate and in no case less than 63 
mm. 


(4) The inside radius of curvature to uptakes shall be not less than twice the thickness of 
the crown plate and in no case less than 25 mm. 


(5) Bunged mouth-pieces may be welded on to end plates in place of the orthodox 
flanging for the attachment of furnace tubes. Such welding shall comply with 
provisions of regulation 97. 


(6) Manhole frames may be similarly welded on the front end plates, and will be subject 
to provisions of regulation 97. 


9.Tube plates—Smoke box tube plates shall be flanged for attachment to the barrel or 
shell and shall be flat and connected thereto by welding. 


92. Parts of flat tube plates within the tube nests.—(l) Where the total area of all tube 
nests in directly fired multi-tubular boilers exceeds 0.65 square meters, stay tubes shall be 
fitted. 


(2) Where the total number of tubes in horizontal multi-tubular waste heat boilers and 
direct fired loco type boilers is arranged in one nest, the area of which exceed .95 sq. 
m stay tubes shall be fitted. 


(3) In all cases where the total number of tubes is arranged in more than one nest, stay 
tubes shall be fitted. 


(4) The parts of tube plates which lie outside the nests of tubes shall be stayed or 
supported wherever the size of the area of plate subject to steam pressure 
necessitates staying or support, either by marginal stay tubes or other means. 


93.Flanging of end plates.—All flanges shall be a good fit to the shell and flues. Flogging 
and/or hammering in the fitting of these parts is prohibited. The caulking edges of all flanged 
plates shall be machined or machine gas cut. 


PART-IV 
94.Furnaces.—(l)No furnace or firebox top, whether plain or corrugated, shall exceed 22 
mm in thickness, and all circular sectioned furnaces when new, shall be as near the truly 
circular form as the type of joint will permit. 


(2) The use of Z angle rings for furnace foundation seams shall be prohibited. 


(3) Furnace crowns, uptakes and other plates not in tension may be joined by fusion 
welding provided the conditions laid down in regulation 95 to 0/ are complied with. 
The end connections of such plates to the shell or shell crown shall also comply with 
such conditions. This construction shall not apply to furnaces of Lancashire and 
Cornish type boilers consisting wholly or plain sections. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


727 


95. Furnaces of horizontal boilers.— () The sections of the internal flues shall each be in 
one plate and shall be bent while cold to circular form and shall be welded longitudinally. 


(2) The maximum permissible variation in diameter at any cross-section shall not exceed 
the thickness of the plate. 


(3) The weld shall be placed at the lower part of the flues, and shall break joint in 
successive sections by at least 305 mm. 


(4) Each flange for the circular seams shall be formed at one heat by suitable machinery. 
(5) The sections shall be allowed to cool gradually to avoid internal stresses. 
(6) The caulking edges of all flue flanges shall be machined or machine gas cut. 


(7) The circular seams shall be arranged so that they do not fall in line with those of the 
adjacent flue or with the circumferential seams of the shell and are at least 52 mm 
apart. 


(8) When flues are flanged for attachment to both end plates the total length of each 
completed flue shall not exceed the length of the shell measured from the inner 
surface of the back end plate to the inner surface of the front end plate, both 
adjacent to the shell. 


(9) Where the flues are flanged for attachment to the end plates, the end sections shall 
be 7.5 mm thicker than the remaining sections, except in cases where the calculated 
thickness is over 27 mm, when the end section shall be 22 mm in thickness. 


(0) The flanged portion of furnace rings shall have radius of curvature of not less than 
25 mm on water side. 


() Sections of corrugated flues may be fusion butt welded circumferentially and 
afterwards stress relieved by heat treatment. 


(2) As an alternative to adamson flanges, furnaces which are partly fitted with 
corrugated sections shall be strengthened by means of suitable stiffening rings 
adequately welded to the furnaces. In no case shall a flat stiffener be less than 63 
mm x 73 mm. 


96. Furnaces of vertical boilers — (/) The furnaces of vertical boilers may be constructed 
in one or more lengthwise sections, each section being rolled from one plate to a full circle. 
In such cases, the component sections may be jointed circumferentially by electrically butt 
welding and shall be stress relieved in accordance with regulation 23. 


(2) In the case of vertical boilers where tube plates form part of the firebox, the tube 
plate portion may be constructed in two vertical sections and the vertical seams when 
welded shall be stress relieved. The maximum permissible variation in diameter, at 
any cross-section shall not exceed 6 mm for fireboxes up to 900 mm in diameter, or 


728 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


0 mm for fireboxes over 900 mm in diameter, or half the thickness of the plate 
whichever is greater. 


(3) Circular furnaces shall preferably be tapered, a tapper of 38 mm in diameter per 300 
mm of height being recommended. The minimum water space at the bottom 
between the furnaces and the shell shall not be less than 50 mm for boilers up to 760 
mm in diameter and shall be not less than 63 mm for boilers over 760 mm diameter. 


(4) The method of welding shall be in accordance with regulation 5. Flats formed in 
the firebox for the insertion of water tubes shall have ample radius at the junction of 
the flat and the curved surfaces and shall be free from sharp corners or tool marks. 
The plate shall not be unduly thinned. 


(5) Ogee flanging where integral with the firebox or in a separate ring shall preferably be 
formed in one heat by suitable machinery and shall be allowed to cool gradually to 
avoid internal stresses. Rings of fire holes mouthpieces or foundation rings shall be 
made of mild steel. Z sections shall not be used for foundation rings. 


(6) Furnaces of vertical type boilers may be attached to the shell at the fire hole by a 
circular ring of substantial section fusion welded to shell and firebox. The opening in 
the shell for fire hole shall be substantially compensated by a ring welded on the 
outside of the shell plate. 


(7) At the fire hole the firebox plate and the shell plate may be flanged and fusion welded 
together. 


97. Fusion butt welded longitudinal seams.—Where the longitudinal seam is fusion butt 
welded,the precautions shall be observedas follows: 


(i) | Plates 20 mm and above in thickness shall be bevelled from both sides of each 
abutting edge but the bevel need not necessarily be the same on each side (see Figs. 
3/ and 3/2). Plates less than 20 mm in thickness may be bevelled from one side only 
of each abutting edge (see Figs. 3/3 and 3/4).The included angle of the bevel shall be 
not less than 60° and the bevelling may be any one of the forms shown in Figs. 3/

In order to obtain full penetration of the weld metal, a gap shall be maintained between 
the plates when they are being welded. Joints shall be welded from both sides, and the 
slag shall be removed after making each run. Before the second side of the joint is 
welded any slag or defect at the bottom of the first run shall be removed by grinding, 
chipping or machining. There shall be no appreciable undercutting of the plate. 


[भाग ॥--खण्ड 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


729 


(iii) For the purposes of relieving internal stresses, the plates adjacent to a fusion weld shall 
be efficiently annealed after welding. 


98. Furnace crown.— (l) The furnace crown shall be made from one plate and the seam 
connecting it to the furnace shall not fall in line with any circumferential seam of the boiler 
shell. 


(2) The furnace crown may be welded to the vertical portion of the firebox. The joint shall 
be fusion butt welded by the electric arc process, provided the conditions for fusion 
welding underregulation 97 are observed. Where the joint is to be welded, the edges 
of the furnace crown and the firebox body shall be bevelled in accordance with Fig. 
3/3 or Fig. 3/4. The depth of the flange of the furnace crown plate from the 
commencement of the curvature of the flanging radius shall be not less than four 
times the plate thickness with a minimum of 38 mm. On completion of welding the 
firebox shall be effectively stress relieved by heat treatment (also referregulation 
00). 


99. Cross tubes.— (l) Cross tubes shall be made from seamless steel pipes or from plate 
or strip rolled and electric resistance or fusion butt welded intopipesby electric arc process. 
The fusion welding shall conform to the requirements of Chapter-i2. Tolerances on these 
pipes shall conform to the requirements of regulation 25. Where welded pipes are used, 
the longitudinal welds shall be so situated that they are not exposed to the direct impact of 
flame. 


(2) Cross tubes shall not exceed 305 mm internal diameter. The minimum thickness 
shall be 8 mm. 


(3) Where welded construction is employed, the tubes shall be of sufficient length to 
enter the furnace plate and the flush with the water side all round or project not less 
than 6 mm and not more than 6 mm into the water space at any part of the 
circumference. Where the tubes are fusion welded in position, the firebox plates shall 
be suitably chamfered and the joints shall be welded externally and internally (see 
Fig. 3/5).
