00. Uptakes.— (l) The uptakes shall be formed from seamless steel pipes or from plate or 
strip rolled and electric resistance welded or fusion butt welded intopipesby electric arc 
process. The tolerances on these pipes shall comply with the requirements of regulation 
25. 


730 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(2) The uptake shall be fusion butt welded by the electric arc process to the upward 
flange of the opening in the firebox crown plate provided the conditions for fusion 
welding givenin regulation 97 are observed. The edges of the upward flange and the 
adjacent end of the uptake shall be bevelled in accordance Fig. 3/3 or Fig.3/4. The 
depth of the crown plate opening from the commencement of the curvature of the 
flanging radius shall be not less than twice the plate thickness with a minimum of 25 
mm. On completion of welding the uptake and crown plate shall be effectively stress 
relieved by heat treatment. 


(3) Where the firebox crown plate is also fusion welded to the body of the firebox, the 
firebox complete with uptake shall be effectively stress relieved by heat treatment on 
completion of the welding. 

(4) Welded uptakes shall be so arranged that the weld is directly facing the longitudinal 
centre line of the manhole. 


0. Loco type fireboxes.— (l)The seams shall be welded subject to the depth of the 
flange being such that the welded seams fall between the * and 2" rows of screwed stays 
or between the flange and the adjacent row screwed stay. 


(2) The firehole mouthpiece may be similarly welded when the firebox and shell are 
flanged for the purpose. 


(3) The welding shall comply with regulation 97. 


PART-V 


02. Bar stays.—Bar stays shall not be welded at any part. They shall preferably have plus 
threadsand the ends of the stays being upset or the middle portion being reduced for this 
purpose. Stay bars which have been worked in the fire shall be subsequently annealed. 


03. Longitudinal stays—() Longitudinal and similar solid screwed stays shall be 
efficiently secured with nuts at each end and not merely riveted over. Where they are over 
3657 mm in length, they shall be supported at intervals of 829 mm along its length. 


(2) Where the stay is screwed through both plates, the stay and holes shall have a 
continuous thread and fitted with nuts and washers on the outside. Where the stay 
passes through clearing holes and internal nut and washer shall also be fitted. 
Where the stay is not normal to the surface of the plate the washer shall be shaped 
so as to form a true surface for the nuts or a knuckle joint may be fitted. 


(3) In vertical boilers the stays shall either be screwed into both crown plates or screwed 
into the furnace crown plate and passed through clearing holes in the shell crown 
plate. 


04. Nuts and Washers for Stays.—(l) The washers shall be at least 2'% times the 
diameter of the threaded portion of the stay and not less than 6 mm in thickness. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


(2) The thickness of the external nuts shall be at least equal to the diameter of the 
threaded portion of the stay. Where bar stays pass through clearing holes in end 
plates, internal nuts of a thickness not less than two-thirds of the diameter of the 
threaded portion of the stay shall be fitted. 


05. Jointed stays.—Where jointed longitudinal stay are fitted, they shall, where practicable, 
be fitted with pins having an effective sectional area 25 percent in excess of that of the stay. 
If the pins are slack in the holes, the total slackness shall not be more than .6 mm. The pins 
shall be as close as possible to the shoulder of the eye forging. The shoulder of the forging 
shall be at least 3 mm wide all round, i.e. the diameter at the shoulder shall be not less than 
the diameter of the hole plus 25 mm. 


06. Diagonal bar or rod stays.—The sectional area of diagonal rod or bar stay shall bear 
the same proportion to that of a direct stay as the length of the diagonal stay bears to the 
length of the perpendicular line from the end of the diagonal stay to the surface supported. 
The ends of diagonal stays, shall not be bent, but shall be attached to the plate with bevelled 
washers and nuts or with riveted tee, blocks or angles and shackle pins (referregulation 05 
for eyes and pins). 


PART-VI 


07. Screwed stays.— (|) Screwed stays and the holes for these shall be screwed with a 
continuous thread. 


(2) The screwed threads of the stay shall be clean andfree from checks or imperfections, 
of full depth, correct whitworth form and a good fit in the holes. The middle portion 
shall preferably be turned down to the bottom of the thread. 


(3) The stays shall be screwed with fine threads of not less than / threads per 25 mm. 


(4) The diameter of the stay over the threads shall not be less than 9 mm or twice the 
thickness of the firebox plate whichever is the greater. 


(5) The pitch of the stays at the furnace of vertical boilers shall not exceed 4 times the 
thickness of the furnace plate. 


(6) Where the stays are not fitted with nuts, the ends shall be riveted over to form 
substantial heads.Alternatively stays may be screwed through the shell and firebox 
plates and the projecting ends shall be substantially fillet welded in an approved 
manner. The projection of the end of the stay from the surface of the plate shall be not 
less than one quarter of the diameter of the stay but in no case less than 6 mm. The 
full end of the stay shall be visible on completion of the welding. 


732 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(7) Crown stays of Loco type boilers shall either be fitted with nuts or riveted over on the 
fire side. 


08. Axial drilling.—All screwed stays less than 355 mm long should preferably be drilled 
with a tell-tale hole 5 mm diameter to a depth of 3 mm beyond the inner face of the plate. 
Stays which are obscure on one side shall preferably be made from hollow stay bar. 


09. Stay nuts.—(l) Nuts of screw stays in combustion chambers and firebox shall not be 
less than 9 mm thick for stays up to 38 mm diameter over threads, 22 mm thick for 4 mm 
and 44 mm stays, 25 mm thick for 47 mm and 5 mm stays, and 28 mm thick for stays over 
5/ mm in diameter. 


(2) The nuts shall be made of solid mild steel or of iron which shall be without weld, if 
exposed to flame. 


0. Spacing of end stays-allowance for curves, etc.—For the tops of fireboxes and 
combustion chambers, the distance between the rows of stays nearest to the tube plate or 
fire hole plate or back plate, as the case may be, and the commencement of curvature of 
these plates at their flanges shall not be greater than the horizontal pitch of the stays. 


PART-VII 


4/. Girder stays for firebox and combustion chamber crowns.— (|)Each girder when of 
the normal type, fitted with stay bolts and nuts, shall be of the double plate interconnected 
type of sufficient strength to support its proportion of the load on the crown to support plate 
independently of the crown plate, and the bolts or weld attachments shall have sufficient 
cross-sectional area to carry the applied load. 


(2) The clear waterway between the crown plate and the underside of the girder bars shall 
be as large as practicable but in no case less than 38 mm as in Fig.3/8. 


(3) The ends of the girders shall not rest on the landing of the flat crown plate but shall be 
carefully fitted to bed directly on the bends of the corners of the vertical end or side 
plates. 


(4) The toes of the girder plates shall be solid with the girder platesand not separate 
pieces attached thereto. 


(5) Girders shall be properly attached to the crown plate by bolts or screws. 


(6) Where an all welded firebox is fitted, the girder stays may be welded to the firebox 
prior to stress relieving. The girder stays shall be recessed for waterways as in sub- 
regulation (2) (Fig. 3/6 and Fig. 3/7).Such girders shall be securely welded by an 
approved method to the firebox crown. The method of welding and the proportions of 
attachment shall be to be satisfaction of the Inspecting Authority.

shell and end plate respectively, and shall be designed in accordance with the following.

thickness. 


5. Load on gusset stay.—Each gusset stay supporting the end plate of a boiler shall be 
designed to carry the whole load due to pressure on the area supported by it. 


PART-IX 
/6.Boiler tubes subject to external pressure. —Both plain and stay smoke tubes may be 
made either of wrought iron or steel and may be electric-resistance-welded or seamless. 


[भाग ॥--खण्ड 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


735 


7. Fitting of plain tubes.—(l) Plain tubes shall be expanded at both ends. The 
expanding shall be parallel throughout the full thickness of the tube plate. Plain tubes may 
also be bell-mouthed, beaded, or welded at the gas inlet end. 


(2) Where stay tubes are not fitted, the ends of the tubes shall be beaded over at the fire 
box end and beaded or bell-mouthed at the other end. If bell-mouthed, the tubes shall 
protrude not less than 3 mm beyond the tube plate. 


PART-X 
8. Screw threads of stay tubes.—(l) Stay tubes shall be screwed at both ends with 
continuous threads, and the holes in the tube plates shall be tapped with continuous 
threads. The pitch of the threads shall not be finer than threads per 25 mm. The stay 
tubes shall be expanded by roller expanders and not made right by caulking only. 


(2) Stay tubes may be attached by welding in which case they shall not be adjacent within 
the same tube nest except in local areas, where not more than two adjacent stay tubes 
may be attached by welding. The form of attachment shall be such that there is a 
mechanical hold in addition to the welding, as shown in Fig.3/0. On completion of 
welding the stay tubes shall be lightly re-expanded.

9. Stay tubes.—(l) Stay tubes are tubes having a weld depth equal to the nominal tube 
thickness plus 3 mm. These stay tubes are not required within tube nests except when the 
tube nests comprise tubes which are expanded only. 


(2) If tube nests comprise plain tubes that are expanded and beaded, expanded and 
belled or expanded and welded, welded stay tubes shall be used in boundary rows in 
sufficient numbers to carry the flat plate loadings outside the tube area. 


(3) For plain tubes or stay tubes exposed to flame or gas temperatures exceeding 600°C, 
the ends of welded tubes shall be dressed flush with the welds. If not so exposed, the 
ends of welded tubes shall extend a maximum of 0 mm beyond the weld or, in the 
case of expanded tubes the tubes shall project beyond the tube plate up to a 
maximum of 5 mm. 


(4) Each stay tube shall be designed to carry its due proportion of the load on the plates 
which it supports.

on the thinnest part of the tube does not exceed 7.4 kg/mm’.

20. Thickened ends of stay tubes.—lIf stay tubes are required to have their thickness 
increased at the screwed ends so that the thickness at the bottom of the threads is 
approximately the same as in the body of the tube the thickening shall be attained by 
upsetting and not by welding process, and the tubes shall be annealed after the upsetting. 


2. Load on stay tubes and stay bars.—Stay tubes shall be designed to carry the whole 
load due to pressure on the area to be supported. In each case the area to be calculated is 
as follows: 


(i) For a stay tube within the tube nest the net area to be supported shall be product of 
the horizontal and vertical pitches in mm of the stay tube less the area of the tube 
holes embraced. Where the pitch of the stay tube is irregular the area shall be taken 
as the square of the mean pitch of the stay tubes (i.e. the square of 4 of the sum four 
sides of any quadrilateral bounded by four adjacent stay tubes) less the area of the 
tube holes embraced. 


(ii) For a stay in the boundary row the net area to be supported shall be the area enclosed 
by lines passing midway between it and the adjacent points of support less the area of 
any tubes embraced. The adjacent points of support may be other stay tubes or the 
commencement of curvature of flanging of center line of the circle or rivets securing 
the end plate to the shell angle. 


(iii) In the case of bar stay where there are no stay tubes in the tube nest the area to be 
supported shall extend to the tangential boundary of the tube nest.

PART-XI 


22.Boiler and super heater tubes subject to internal pressure steel tubes.— (|) All 
tubes which are subject to internal pressure of water or steam shall be cold drawn or hot 
finished seamless or electric resistance welded in accordance with Chapter-2. Except as 
provided for in sub-regulation (2)below, they shall be without joint. 


(2) Tubes having an external diameter not exceeding 27 mm may be jointed and such joints 
may be flash welded, machine forge welded arc or gas welded. Tubes above 27 mm 
diameter may also be welded provided they are located outside the furnace. Such welds 
must conform to the requirements of Chapter-7. 


(3) Flash butt welding shall be undertaken as per the qualified procedure. The external fin 
caused by flash butt welding shall be removed subject to a maximum height of 5 percent 
of the tube outside diameter. The required flow area shall be ensured by conducting ball 
test using nearest ball diameter of 75% of the nominal Internal Diameter of the tube size. 


(4) All fusion welded butt joints shall be post weld heat treated as per the requirements 
specified in regulation 23. 


(5) When gas welding is implied the technique followed shall be approved by a Competent 
Person. 


(6) For design metal temperatures and material requirements refer to Table 2// of regulation 
30. 


(7) The technique employed in all field welding of tubes shall be subject to the approval of 
Inspecting Authority or Chief Inspector as the case may be. 
(8) All butt weld of tubes shall be tested as required hereunder: 


(i) Fortubes greater than 78 mm bore, all welds shall be non-destructively tested 
by radiographic or other approved methods. 


(ii) For tubes greater than 02 mm bore and up to and including 78 mm bore, 
ten(0) per cent of the welds by each welder, selected at random with a 
minimum of 2 welds per welder, shall be subjected to non-destructive 
examination by radiographic or other approved method. 


(iii) For tubes 02 mm bore and under, sample welds simulating the production 
welds shall be provided for mechanical testing either at a rate of 2 per cent or 
after each 750 welding hours with a minimum of one sample weld per welder. 


(iv) Alternatively, 5 per cent of the welds made by each welder selected at random, 
with a minimum of one weld per welder, shall be subjected to non-destructive 
examination by radiographic or other approved method. This rate may be 
reduced to 2 per cent by arrangement with the Inspecting Authority after initial 
satisfactory results have been produced. 


738 


THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(v) In the event of any non-destructive test not meeting the requirements, defects 
in the welds represented by that test shall be rectified and the Inspecting 
Authority may call for an increase in the number of non-destructive tests until 
such time as a satisfactory standard is achieved. 


Butt welded joints as indicated in sub-regulation(8) shall be subjected to non- 
destructive examination by radiographic, radioscopy or other approved methods such 
as ultrasonic testing including phased array ultrasonic testing, magnetic particle 
inspection or liquid dye penetrant inspection. When radioscopic examination is to be 
performed in lieu of radiography on welded components, the following requirements 
shall be met, namely:-

shall contain the following:

(e) The nominal thickness to be considered for determining Post Weld Heat Treatment 
and soaking time shall be defined as: 


(i) For full penetration butt welds, the nominal thickness is the thinner of the parts 
being joined. 


(ii) For full penetration corner welds, the nominal thickness is the depth of the weld. 


(iii) For partial penetration groove and material repair welds, the nominal thickness is 
the depth of the weld. The total depth of partial or full penetration groove welds 
made from both sides shall be taken as the sum of the depth of both sides at a 
given location. 


(iv) For fillet welds, the nominal thickness is the weld throat. When a fillet weld is 
used in conjunction with a groove weld, the nominal thickness is either the depth 
of the groove weld or the fillet throat dimension, whichever is greater. 


(v) Except as stipulated in clause (vi) below, the nominal thickness is the depth of 
the groove, if present, through the shell or nozzle or reinforcing pad, or the throat 
of any fillet weld, whichever is greater. 


(vi) When multiple openings form a ligament where the spacing between centres is 
less than twice the average diameter, the nominal thickness of a combination 
groove and fillet weld shall be the sum of the groove depth and fillet weld throat. 


(vii)The thickness of the pressure part at the point of attachment where a non- 
pressure part is welded to a pressure part, in case of butt welds; 


(viii) The thickness of the fillet weld at the point of attachment where a non — 
pressure part is welded to a pressure part, in case of fillet welds.

24. Attachment of Steel Tubes.— () Steel tubes shall be connected to the tube plates by 
one of the following methods:- 


(i) Expanding. 
(ii) Strength welding. 
(iii) Mechanical bolted ball joint. 


(2) Drift or roller expanded tubes shall project through the neck or bearing part in the 
holes by at least a quarter of 25 mm and shall be secured from drawing out by being 
bell mouthed to the extent of 0.8 mm for each 25 mm in diameter plus .6 mm. 


(3) Tubes may be seal welded into fittings or headers for both boilers and super heaters 
after they have been expanded and flared provided the material in the fittings or 
headers does not contain carbon in excess of 0.35 per cent. 


(4) In the case of drifted or roller expanded tubes, the tube holes in the tube plates of 
drums, pockets, or headers shall be formed in such a way that the tubes can be 
effectively tightened in them. Where the tube ends are not normal to the tube plate, 
there shall be a neck or belt of parallel seating of at least {3 mm depth measured in a 
plane normal to the axis of the tube at the holes. 


(5) Where tubes are strength welded direct to the tube plates, the technique followed 
shall be approved by the Inspecting Authority and all welds shall be suitably heat 
treated. In the case of plates below 22 mm thickness, the requirement of stress 
relieving by heat treatment after welding of the tubes may be waived provided the 
weld satisfies the requirements of the maximum hardness and also the requirements 
concerning the impact values of the weld metal. The welding procedure adopted and 
the weld sequence selected shall also be subject to the approval of the Inspecting 
Authority. This provision in applicable to only shop welding of tubes at the 
Manufacturers Works. 


746 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(6) Tubes spacers, supporting clips and lugs may be welded to the tubes. Flash welding 
of studs for supporting refractories, etc, is also permissible. 


(7) The tubes shall be so arranged that they are accessible for cleaning internally and 
externally. 


PART-XIl 


25. Headers, mud boxes, etc. of water tube boilers.—() (a) Headers and mud boxes, 
etc. of water tube Boiler may be of seamless or welded steel or of cast steel complying with 
the requirements of the provisions contained in regulations 49 to 57. Where welded, the 
welding shall be stress relieved, radio graphed or ultrasonically examined and in all respects 
shall be to the satisfaction of the Inspecting Authority as per Table 3/5 of regulation 23. 


(0) Open ends of seamless steel tube headers may be closed by forging or the ends 
may be secured by bolting, screwing or welding in an approved manner. Bolting 
shall not be used where the bolts are exposed to or are swept by gases of 
combustion. 


(c) The method of attachment of the ends shall be subject to the ends shall be subject 
to the approval of the Inspecting Authority. 


(2) Each piece prior to being fitted in place shall be subjected to hydraulic tests to one- 
and-a-half times the design pressure of the boiler into which it is to be fitted. 


(3) (2) The sighting hold doors and header caps shall be substantial and be capable 
of being removed or replaced from time to time without loss of efficiency of 
safety. They may be held in position either by means of bolts or by seal 
welding. 


(b) The bolts by which they are held in place shall be fitted to them in such a way 
as to satisfy the above conditions. 


(c) The doors shall be so designed that they will not blow out in the event of 
breakage of the bolt. 


(d) Circular holes also may be provided in addition to elliptical holes, if provision 
is made to prevent the door bolts from turning, while securing the joint. 


(4) All flanges shall have a fillet with a radius of curvature at least equal to the thickness 
of the necks to which they are attached.

PART-XIIl 


26. Stand pipes and padsetc..—Stand pipes and seating for carrying mountings shall be 
made of wrought, cast of fabricated steel. These shall take the form of short stand pipes, 
pressed steel plate saddles, forged pads or pads cut from round rolled bar as may be most 
convenient and secured to the boiler by welding. Where short stand pipes are used they 
shall be of solid forged, fabricated or cast steel. They shall be carefully bedded to the shell 
before attachment. The jointing faces to which mountings are to be bolted shall be 
machined. Pads shall have sufficient thickness to allow the drilling of stud holes for 
mountings without the inner surface being pierced and the length of the screwed portion of 
the stud in the pad shall be not less than the diameter of the stud. 


27. Design of stand pipes.—The design of the branches and stand-pipe shall be regulated 
in the following manner: 


(i) in order to withstand the maximum allowable working pressure, the minimum thickness 
of branch and stand-pipe shall be determined in accordance with the provisions 
specified in sub-regulation (/) of regulation 244; 


(ii) Compensation requirements for openings in the main pressure parts shall be 
determined in accordance with the provisions of regulation 79; 


(iii) The additional thickness shall be considered to withstand superimposed loading due to 
connecting pipe-work or fittings. 


(iv) The minimum thickness of the branch or standpipe shall be the greatest of the values 
required above and shall not be less than 0.05 0५ plus 3.2 mm where, d, is the 
outside diameter of the branch (in mm); 


Provided that the provisions of the regulations shall not apply to such tube stub 
which have been designated as tubes. 


28. Pressed plate saddles.—Where pressed plate saddles are employed they shall be 
formed to bed closely to the boiler and machined on the face jointing the mounting and on 
the edges. The studs for attachment of mountings, if screwed through the saddle, shall each 
be fitted with a nut on the inside having a thickness equal to the diameter of the stud. Where 
the stud holes do not penetrate through the saddle, the length of the screwed portion of the 
stud in the plate shall not be less than the diameter of the stud. 


29. Seatings for mountings.— (l) For pressures not exceeding 8.7 kg/cm*(g), mountings 
with the screwed ends not exceeding inch S.P.T.(Straight Pipe Threads) may be used; the 
screwed portion of any such mounting being not less than 5 mm. 


(2) |The mountings may be screwed: 


a. Directly into the boiler shell plate, nuts being fitted on the water side, or 


748 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


b. Into steel distance pieces the length of thread engaged being in no case less than 
the bore of the mounting plus 6 mm. 


(8) The distance pieces shall be made from solid mild steel. They shall be screwed into 
the plate and fitted with nuts on the water side. The walls of the distance pieces shall 
be not less than 6 mm thick at the bottom of the thread. 


30. Attachment of mountings.— (l) Mountings may be attached directly to any shell or 
end plate where the plate is of sufficient thickness to allow a suitable surface to be obtained 
for the attachment of the boiler mountings. 


(2) The minimum thickness at the hole in the shell or end plate shall be not less than 
the thickness required for the maximum allowable working pressure considering the 
plate as being unpierced. 


(3) Where the boiler mountings are secured by studs, the studs shall have a full thread 
holding in the plate for at least one diameter. If the stud holes penetrate the whole 
thickness of the plate. The stud shall be screwed right through the plate end be 
fitted with a nut inside having a thickness equal to the diameter of the stud. Where 
bolts are used for securing mountings they shall be screwed right though the plate 
with their heads inside the shell or end plate. 


3. Insufficient thickness of end plates.— (l) In cases where the thickness of the end 
plate is insufficient for this purpose the mountings shall be joined to suitable steel seatings 
as provided in regulation 726. 


(2) The following constructions as to stand pipes attached to shells and end plates shall 
be permissible: 


(i) Where the internal diameter of the stand pipe does not exceed 25 mm, the 
standpipe may be screwed into the plate and fitted with a nut on the 
waterside. 


(ii) Where the internal diameter of the standpipe exceeds 25 mm but does not 
exceed 5/ mm, it may be screwed in and seal-welded. 


(iii) Where the diameter of the standpipe exceeds 5 mm, it may be welded to the 
end plate. 


(3) The foregoing provisions as to the stand pipe shall be regulated by the following 
conditions: 


(i) When stand pipes are screwed, the screwing shall be of Standard Pipe Thread, 


(ii) Where stand pipes, saddles or other forms of seatings are fabricated by fusion 
welding they shall be stress relieved by heat treatment before attachment to the 
boiler, 

(iii) Where the bore of the stand pipe or seating and the hole in the plate does not 
exceed 27 mm plus twice the thickness of the plate, the seating may be welded 
to the plate without subsequent heat treatment of the weld so made. Where the 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


749 


hole in the plate exceeds 27 mm plus twice the thickness of the plate, the plate 
to which seating is attached shall be stress relieved by heat treatment. 


32. Attachment of water and pressure gauges.—Water gauge and pressure gauge 
siphons may be attached direct to the front end plates without the intervention of a pad or 
stand pipe, provided they are flanged and secured by studs. If the studs are screwed 
through the plate, nuts shall be fitted on the inside of the plate. 


33. Mountings on flat places.—Where the flanged mountings are attached direct to a flat 
plate, such mountings shall be provided with a substantial spigot, the full thickness of the 
boiler plate. 


34. Bolts and nuts.—Bolts and nuts shall be machined where they come in contact with 
the flanges, and all holes in saddles and pads shall be drilled. 


Note: In all cases where boiler is lagged the joint of the mountings shall be clear of the 
lagging surface or the lagging kept clear of flange so that the joint can be inspected and, when 
necessary, remade.

36. Compensating rings and frames for openings in shells.— (|) Compensating rings 
and frames for openings in shells shall be of same material as that of shell. The 
compensation provided shall preferably be flanged frames, which shall be fitted in all cases 
where the shell plate exceeds 4 mm thick. Flanged frames shall be weld less and shall be 
flanged or pressed to provide a flat jointing surface for the cover. 


(2) All compensating rings and frames shall be formed to bed closely to the surfaces to 
be connected. Any weld therein shall be on the transverse centre line. 


(3) The flat jointing surfaces of all flanged or pressed frames and all doors or covers 
shall be machined. 


37. Internal doors.—Internal doors shall be of wrought steel in accordance with Chapter-2 
and constructed in accordance with the following:- 


(!) Doors shall be formed to fit closely to the internal joint surface and should be fitted 
with studs, nuts and crossbars; 


(2) Doors for circular opening larger than 250 mm or elliptical/rectangular opening 
larger than 250 mm x 75 mm shall have two studs but for opening of 250 mm x 
770 mm or less only one stud may be fitted. Doors for opening not larger than 23 
mm x 90 mm may have the stud forged integrally with door; 


(3) Doors studs shall be of welding quality steel having a minimum specified tensile 
strength of not less than 36.7 kg/mm* and those for manholes shall be not less than 
30 mmand they shall be fixed in any of the following way:- 


(a) screwed through the plate and fillet welded on inside; 


(0) fillet welded each side of the plate with a leg length of not less than 0 mm; 


(c) attached to the door by an intermediate plate or lugs so that the strength of the 
attachment is not less than the strength of the studs and the studs are prevented 
from turning; or 


(d) provided with an integrated collar and be riveted or screwed onto the door plate 
and be prevented from turning in which case the strength of the attachment shall 
be not less than the strength of the studs;

(4) Door spigot when the door is in the central position shall have a clearance of

(5) The nuts shall be of appropriate material compatible to that of bolts and be placed 
on the seating surface; 


(6) The cross-bars shall be of substantial proportions and of mild or wrought steel.

39. Positions of manhole in shell—Manholes and other openings in cylindrical shells 
shall be placed as far as possible from any seams, preferably towards the back end to the 
boiler top. Wherever practicable, oval openings shall be arranged with the minor axis 
parallel to the longitudinal centre line of the boiler. In no case shall the circumferential length 
of any opening exceed twice the longitudinal width of the opening. 


40. Compensation rings to manholes.—Compensation shall be provided in every case for 
the part cut of a cylindrical shell for a manhole. The strength of the net section of 
compensating ring and also welds securing them to the shell, compared with that part of the 
shell cut out, shall not be less than the efficiency of the longitudinal seam. 


4. Compensation for cutting large holes in shell type boilers —Where holes are cut in 
the cylindrical shell for the purpose of attaching a seating of frame or door, compensation 
shall be provided such that the added sectional area, including parts of the frame within 
07.6 mm of the shell shall be not less than the sectional area of the plate removed which 
shall be the product of the diameter of the opening and the calculated thickness of the plate 
as found by Equation(4/2)._ Where holes are cut in the cylindrical shell for the purpose of 
fixing seating for mountings and the diameter of the holes is greater than 204 times thickness 
of the shell plate plus 70 mm, compensation shall be provided. Where a large opening is cut 
in a cylindrical shell to receive another part of the structure, the sides where cut away shall 
be efficiently cross-stayed or strengthened in some other effective manner.

42. General requirements.—Where applicable the general terms of Chapter- relating to 
Certificates from Makers, Inspecting Authorities, etc., and of Chapter-3 concerning 
construction shall be followed. 


PART-I 


43. Materials of constructionfor fusion welded Boiler Drums.—(l) For plates to be 
used in the construction of fusion welded boilers drums, requirements of Chapter-2 shall 
apply. 


(2) Plates having thicknessof more than 50 mm, before being fabricated, shall be uniformly 
heat treated to produce grain refinement andheat treatment involving quenching in a liquid 
medium is not permitted. 


PART-II 


44. Fusion Welded Drums.—The term 'Fusion Weld’, for the purpose of this Chapter, 
isapplicable to all welded joints made by the metal arc process with covered electrodes or 
other electric arc process, in which the arc stream and the deposited weld metal are shielded 
from atmospheric contamination. 


45. This Chapter shall apply to the single run or heavy run welding process and that welded 

boiler drums manufactured by that process shall conform with all regulations of this Chapter, 
except those in which divergence is necessary solely because of special requirements 
essential for the most efficient utilisation of that processand all regulations governing quality 
of material, construction workmanship andtesting (both non-destructive and otherwise) are 
applicable. 


46. Equipment of workshop.— (l) The welding plant and equipment shallbe of good 
quality and maintained in an efficient working condition. 


(2) The welding apparatus shallbe installed under cover and shall bearranged so that the 
welding work may be carried out in positions free from draughts and adverse weather 
conditions. 


(3) The procedure shall be such that there is regular and systematic supervision of the 
welding works, and the welding operators are subjected to periodic tests for quality of 
workmanship by the works officials. 


(4) Records of these periodic tests shall be kept and madeavailable by works office to the 
Competent Person for scrutiny. 


754 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


47.Testing Laboratory.— 


(.) The works shall be equipped with an efficient testing laboratory which shallinclude 
apparatus suitable for carrying out tensile, bend and impact tests, micro-examination of 
specimens and x-ray examination of the actual joints in pressure vessels. 


(2) The works shallalso be equipped with a suitable heat treating furnace having satisfactory 
means for temperature control, but as an alternative arrangement may be made whereby the 
drums can be heat-treated elsewhere. 


48. Constructional details and preparation for welding— (l) Before starting the 
construction work, the manufacturer shall furnishto Inspecting Authority, a fully dimensioned 
sectional drawing reflecting thereincomplete details of construction of the drumfor approval. 


(2) Fully dimensioned drawings of the proposed welds preparations of the main seams 
drawn to a scale, clearly reflecting therein all the relevant details shall be furnished. 


(3) Sketches showing details of the welds preparations for the attachment of the stand 
pipes, branch pipes and seating and their locations relative to the longitudinal and 
circumferential seams and to other openings shall be furnished. 


49. Preparation of plates —For the purpose of preparation of plates, requirements 
contained underregulation77 shall apply. 


50. Cylindrical Shell of Drums.— 
(.) Each drum shell plate shall be of cylindrical form to the extreme edges of the plate. 


(2) The bending shall be done entirely by machine and local heating or hammering is 
prohibited. 


(3) Where the plates are bent to an internal diameter less than 20 times of the plate 
thickness, they shall be efficiently heat-treated after bending or combined with final post weld 
heat treatment. 


5. Method of making welded joints.—() For the purpose of requisite quality of welding, 
the seams may be welded from both sides of the plate or from one side of the plate with or 
without a backing strip and If a backing strip is used, it shall be removed and the surface so 
exposed shall be dressed. 


(2) Additional runs of metal shall be deposited at the surface of the welded seams so that 
the welded metal at the level of the surfaces of the plate is refined as far as possible. 


(3)Thickness of such additional welding shall not exceed values given in Table 4/lbelow.

(4)The surfaces of the welds which are to be subsequently radiographed shall be sufficiently 
free from coarse ripples, overlap, grooves, abrupt ridges and valleys, so as to avoid stress 
raisers and to permit proper interpretation of radiographs and other Non-Destructive 
Testing(NDT) methods. If there is a question regarding the surface condition of the weld 
when interpreting a radiographic film, the film shall be compared to the actual weld surface 
or provide smooth contours and to be flush with the respective surfaces of the plate before 
radiography examination is done. 


(5) Undercut shall not exceed 0.8mm or 0% of wall thickness, whichever is less and 
undercut shall not encroach on design wall thickness. 

(6) When affixing standpipes, branch pipes, seating, compensating plates, doubling plates or 
manhole frames, not less than two runs of metal shall be deposited at each weld. 


(7) Each run of weld shall be thoroughly cleaned and free from slag that may adversely 
affect the quality of the succeeding runs. 


(8) Welds shall be marked permanently to facilitate their location. 


756 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


52. Type of welded joints—The longitudinal and circumferential seams shall be made 
with butt joints of the single or double U or Vee type. 


53. Number of joints —Where, having regard to the approved design, the dimensions are 
such that the shell cannot be made from a single plate, it shall be made with the minimum 
number of joints and the longitudinal seams in successive rings shall not fall in line, except 
where the rings of the drum are in two halves of unequal thickness. 


54. Position of the tube holes.—(]) Tube holes in welded seams shall be avoided as far 
as possible.Where the holes are unavoidable, they may be machined through welded seams 
after these seams are radiographed. 


(2) In the case of vanadium steels, in addition to radiography, the welded seams shall be 
stress relieved. 


(3) The efficiency of the ligament in the direction of weld shall be multiplied by a weld factor 
not exceeding 0.95 except where the distance from the edge of the tube hole to the edge of 
the weld is greater than 3 mm. 


(4) The edge of the weld shall be considered to be the edge of the weld groove as machined 
in the plate prior to welding. 


Notwithstanding anything in this regulation, efficiency of the ligament in the direction 
of weld shall not be multiplied by a weld factor 0.95 where 00 percent radiography of weld 
joint is done.

56. Mechanical test and test plates of fusion welded seams.—(l) Fusion welded joints 
shall comply with the mechanical tests herein specified. Not less than one set of test plates 
shall be provided to represent the welding of each longitudinal seam and the test plates may 
by attached at each end of the longitudinal seam or the set may be located at one end only. 


(2) Where the drum shell is formed in two or more courses, the staggered longitudinal seam 
shall be regarded as a continuous longitudinal seam provided the welding be effected in 
one reasonably continuous operation and by the same operator or operators. 


(3) Where there are circumferential seams only or where the method of welding the 
circumferential seam differ from that employed for the longitudinal seams, the method of 
providing the test plates shall be decided by the Inspecting authority. 


(4) (a) The test plates shall be of a size sufficient for the preparation of the test pieces 
specified in sub-regulation()of regulation 57and for any repeat test pieces that may be 
required. 

(0) The material for each set of test plates shall be cut from the respective plate or plates 
forming the appropriate seam, and before begin cut shall be stamped by the Competent 
Person. 


(5) When the analysis of the plate is approved by the Inspecting authority and is considered 
sufficiently similar, the test plates may be cut from one drum shell plate only. 


(6) In the case of insufficient material being available on the shell plate to permit the cutting 
of test pieces, these shall be acceptable if they are made from another plate provided it is 
made from the same cast. 

(7) (a) The weld groove in the test plates shall be similar to that adopted for the 
corresponding edges of the longitudinal seam, and the respective fusion faces shall be in 
continuous alignment. 

(0) The test plates shall be reinforced or supported during welding in order to prevent 
under warping. 


758 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(c) The weld metal in the plates and the seam shall be of the same grade of electrode 
and shall be deposited continuously at the same operation. 


(8) The weld in any test plate shall not be repaired unless agreed by the Inspecting Authority 
and the repairs shall be done in such a manner as will ensure that the repaired seam in 
the test plate is still representative of the material in the main seam. 


(9) Where it is desired to straighten test plates which have warped during welding they may 
be straightened at a temperature below the temperature of heat treatment of the drum to 
which they belong. Straightening shall take place before final heat treatment. 


(0)Heat treatment requirements shall comply with regulation 23. 


() If any defects in the weld metal of a test plate are revealed by radiographical 
examination, the position of these shall be clearly marked on the plate and test pieces 


shall be selected from such parts of the test plates as may be decided by the Inspecting 
Authority.

64. Non-Destructive test— (l) Micro and Macro Examination— A specimen, the full 
thickness of the plate and not less than 3 mm wide may be taken from each set of test 
plates by the Inspecting Authority for the purpose of micro and macro examination.Macro- 
etching of a complete cross-section of the weld including the heat effected zone, should 
show satisfactory penetration, fusion and absence of significant inclusions or other defects. 
In case of a doubt as to the condition of the weld as shown by micro-etching, the area 
concerned shall be microscopically examined for defect investigation. 


(2) Radiographical examination—(a) Every portion of the longitudinal and circumferential 
welded joints of the drums shall be subjected to radiographical examination or ultrasonic 
examination. Where ultrasonic examinations isused,it shall be demonstrated to the 
satisfaction of the Inspecting Authority that the equipment and the technique used are 
satisfactory. The manufacturer shall ensure that the operator employed is competent to 
use the equipment, apply the technique and interpret the results of the examination. 
NDE operator and evaluator shall possess qualification as per ASNT SNT-TC-A or ISO 
972 or equivalent. 


(b) The method employed in obtaining the radiographs shall be such as to show clearly 
defects having a magnitude equal to 2 per cent of the thickness of the welded joint. To 
determine whether this result is being obtained and indicator of approved form which 
includes a portion equivalent to not more than 2 per cent of the joint thickness, shall be 
placed in the vicinity of the weld so as to make a record on each radiograph. Each 
section of every weld shall be marked so that the radiographs can be easily correlated 
to the particular part of the joint represented. Radiographic or Ultrasonic testing shall 
be carried out as per written down procedure specifying technique, IQI sensitivity, 
density requirements and acceptance norms in line with established International 
boiler codes subject to acceptance by the Competent person. 


(c)The examination shall be made from the original films and the acceptability of the 
welds shall be rejected or dealt with under regulation 65 and be radiographed again. 


(d) PAUT or TOFD or both in lieu of Radiographic test may be used subject to 
establishing a procedure to include techniques, set ups, calibrations, operator 
qualification, acceptance norms in line with International Codes. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


765 


(3) Magnetic Particle Flaw Detection- Magnetic method of flaw detection shall be employed 
wherever possible for ferritic steel. 


(4) Dye-Penetrate Flaw Detection- Dye penetrants or equivalent method of flaw detection 
shall be employed for Austenitic or other non-magnetic steel. 


(5) All butt welded joints shall be subjected to non-destructive examination by radiographic, 
radioscopy or other approved methods such as ultrasonic testing, magnetic particle 
inspection or liquid dye penetrant inspection. When radioscopic examination is to be 
performed in lieu of radiography on welded components, the following requirements shall 
be met, namely:- 


(a) A written procedure shall be submitted for approval to the Inspecting Authority 
which shall contain the following: 

(i) material and the thickness range;

radioscopic images and system performance quality shall exhibit: 

(i) a thin section contrast sensitivity of 3%;

(iv) lQI sensitivity - 2% of the joint thickness when wire IQI's are to be used,

sensitivity of the system. 

(c) Radioscopes shall be properly marked to co-relate with particular part of joint 
represented. 


(d) The radioscopic examination data shall be recorded and stored on videotape, 
magnetic disk or optical disk or any other electronic storage device at the maker's 
plant for a sufficient period after the date of radioscopic examination as specified 
by the Inspecting Authority, Efficient radioscopic examination record recall shall 
be made available at any time over the record retention period and shall be 
traceable to the test objects. 


(e) When repair has been performed as a result of radioscopic examination, the 
repaired areas shall be re-examined using the same radioscopic technique to 
evaluate the effectiveness of the repair. 


(f) To aid in proper interpretation of the radioscopic examination data, the details of 
the technique used shall accompany the data. As a minimum, the information 
shall include the approved procedure requirements and system performance test 
data. 


766 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


65. General.— (l) (a) Any repair to a weld carried out by the manufacturer shall first be 
agreed to by the Inspecting Authority. 


(b)Where defects occur in distributed positions in a seam, repairs to the extent of 75 per 
cent, of the total length of the seam shall be permitted to replace the defective welding. 


(c)Where defects are located in a single continuous length, the permissible extent of 
repair shall be decided by the Inspecting Authority. 


(2) Where the weld metal in any way fails to comply with the requirements specified, the 
whole of the weld metal may be removed and the seam re-welded provided that; 
(a)the original test plates are similarly treated, or 


(b)New test plates of the same thickness as the joint and of similar quality of material 
are attached to the end of the seam and re-welded with it. 


(c)In either case the plates shall be tested in accordance with regulations 56 to 
64andthe requirement for heat treatment shall be in accordance with regulation 66. 


(3) With regard to the extent of permissible repair and when agreed by the Inspecting 
Authority,a circumferential seam shall be treated in the same manner as a longitudinal 
seam. The Inspecting Authority shall be entitled to call for representative tests for a re- 
welded circumferential seam. 


(4) Defects shall be cut out by chipping of machining or by burning out by the Air Arc Weld 
Process. 


(5) Where a defective part has been cut out, the Inspecting Authority shall be entitled to make 
an examination before re-welding. 


(6) Only metallic arc welding shall be used for repairs. 


(7) All repaired areas shall be subjected to radiographical examination or radioscopic 
examination by the approved techniques. 


(8) The Inspecting Authority shall be entitled to call for specimen representing any welded 
repair, for the purpose of examination and test. 


(9) On completion of all welded repairs, the manufacturers shall, if requested, supply for record 
purposes a detailed diagram showing the positions, length depth and width of all such 
repairs. 


66. Heat treatment.—(]) (a)After completion of the welding of the seams and the welding on 
the stand pipes and including welding repairs but before the hydraulic test, each drum shall 
be heat treated for stress relieving; during this heat treatment the official test plates shall be 
lying inside the drum. 


(b)For heat treatment requirements refer regulation 23. 


(2)Where shell is subjected to a primary stress relieving treatment identical to the final heat 
treatment to be given to the drum, the test plates may be placed inside the shell during 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


767 


the primary treatment and thereafter cut up and tested without waiting for the final 
treatment of the drum. 


(3) Where the shell is not subjected to primary stress relieving treatment or is subject to a 
primary stress relieving treatment which is not identical with the final heat treatment the 
test plates may be placed inside any other drum of comparable dimensions which is to be 
heat treated in accordance with this Chapter. The heat treatment is to take place in the 
furnace in which the drum relating to the test plates will eventually be given its final heat 
treatment. 


(4) Temperature charts shall be submitted to indicate that the test plates and the drum they 
represent have been subjected to identical heating soaking and cooling treatment. 


(5)(a) For the heat treatment, the drum shall be placed in a furnace sufficiently larger to 
accommodate the whole drum. 


(b) The furnace shall have proper means of temperature measurement and control and 
shall be capable of heating the whole of the drum to a uniform temperature. It shall be 
so designed as to prevent direct impingement of flame on the drum. 


(c) Thermocouples shall be attached to the drum at appropriate locations.A temperature 
time diagram of the stress-relieving process shall be provided for a welded shell or drum 
and a similar diagram for other welded pressure part shall be provided where inspecting 
Authority requires it. 


(6) Alternative procedure for the heat treatment of the drum may be submitted to the 
inspecting Authority for approval. 


(7) In special cases it may be permissible to heat treat the test plates separately from the 
drum, provided the inspecting Authority is satisfied with the means adopted to ensure 
that the following factors shall be the same for the drum as for the test plates, namely:- 


(i) Rate of heating 

(ii) Maximum temperature 
(iii) Time held at maximum temperature 
(iv) Conditions of cooling. 


67. Hydraulic test at makers’ works.— () Boiler drum having internal diameter greater 
than 600 mm and other cylindrical component having internal diameters greater than i000 
mm shall be hydraulically tested on completion of manufacture at the makers works in the 
presence of Competent Person to i% times the maximum allowable working pressure 
without indication of weakness and defects. 


(2)All components which are not reasonably accessible for inspection after assembly into 
the boiler or have been tested hydraulically prior to welding at a pressure less than that 
specified in sub-regulation (l)shall be tested hydraulically to % times the maximum 
allowable working pressure before assembly into the boiler. 


(3) Tubular products that have been hydraulically tested to the required pressure prior to 
welding or ultrasonically tested shall not require further hydraulic testing as components 
provided they were joined during assembly by circumferential butt joint which have been 
welded and non-destructively tested as per relevant provisions of these regulations. 


768 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(4) Components other than tubular products shall not require hydraulic testing before 
assembly into the boiler if the completed boiler is tested hydraulically to ¥ times the design 
pressure at site. 


(5) In case of drums, headers which are to be fitted with tubes, the test may be made 
before drilling of tube holes but after attachments of nozzles and similar fittings. 


(6) The test pressure shall be raised gradually under proper control at all times so that it 
never exceeds by more than 6% of the required pressure and maintained for 30 minutes 
whereupon the pressure shall be reduced to maximum allowable working pressure and 
maintained for sufficient time to permit close visual inspection for leakages of the pressure 
parts. 


(7) The temperature of water used as medium of pressure testing shall not be less than 
20°C and more than 50°C. 


(8) (a) In case of drums of ‘composite’ construction and partly reverted and partly welded 
seams or seamless forged drum shell with ends attached by fusion welding. 


(0) The test pressure shall be the same as for fusion welded drums. 


(9) In case the hydraulic test reveal any defects in the welded steam, it shall not be 
repaired unless the Inspecting Authority permits to do so. 


(0) |Oncompletion of agreed repairs to a drum which has previously been stress relieved 
by heat treatment, further heat-treatment, if required by the Inspecting Authority shall be done 
and the drum shall again be subjected to hydraulic test.

73. Intermediate boiler drum supports.—Where a boiler drum is supported at 
Intermediate points in its length at a distance greater than one internal diameter from the end 
of the parallel portion of the drum shell, the shell shall be thickened locally to the supports or 
so designed that when the local stress set up by the supports in the drum shell are added, 
algebraically to those caused by the internal steam pressure and supported loads, the 
maximum resultant stress does not exceed the permissible working stress at the working 
metal temperature.

75. General— (l) The thickness ‘T’ specified in equation (4/0) of regulation i77 is the 
thickness of the end plate after manufacture and is applicable over the whole area of the end 
plate up to the point where, for ends of partially spherical shape, the dishing radius joins the 
corner radius; from this joint a gradual thinning is permissible up to maximum of i0 per cent 
of the thickness ‘T’ at the point where the corner radius joins the straight portion of flanged 
end plate. 


(2) A similar gradual thinning is permissible for end plates of semi-ellipsoidal shape. 


(3) This permissible reduction in thickness applies also to the flange for the manhole 
opening. In no case, however, when the end plate is butt welded to the drum shell, shall the 
thickness of the edge of the flange for connection to the shell be less than the thickness of 
an unpierced seamless shell of the same diameter and material, determined by equation 
(4/2).

CHAPTER-5 
VALVES, GAUGES AND AUXILIARIES 


PART-! 
8. Requisite Mountings, fittings and Auxiliaries. —(])Every boiler shall be provided at 
least with the following, namely: - 


(a) Two safety valves, one of which may be a high steam and low water type safety 
valve and in no case the bore of the seat of the valve should be less than 9 mm. 


(0) Two means of indicating the water level; 
(c) A steam pressure gauge; 

(0) A steam stop valve; 

(e) A feed check valve; 

(f) One feed apparatus; 


Provided that for boilers fired by gaseous, liquid or solid fuels in suspension 
where heating surface exceeds 20 m’,shall be provided with minimum two feed 
apparatus which shall have a combined capacity of not less than the maximum 
continuous rating of the boiler: Provided further that for other boilers where residual 
heat is there even after fuel supply cut-off, two feed apparatus each having a 
capacity of not less than maximum continuous rating of the boiler shall be provided. 
(For boilers in battery see regulation 242); 


(g) A blow-down cock or valve; 
(h) Fusible plugs as provided under Regulation 236; 
(i) An attachment for Competent Person’s test gauge; 


(j) A manhole, where size and construction permit, and such mud holes or sight 
holes as are necessary for effectively cleaning the boiler. 


(2 


— 


In the case of boilers fitted with integral super heaters, an additional safety valve 
shall be fitted at the end of the super heaters outlet header. 


(3) In the case of boilers with no fixed steam and waterline, the fitting of such 
accessories that are manifestly not needed or used, such as water gauges, water 
columns and gauge cocks, may not be insisted upon. 


(4) In the case of a single boiler of the Shell type and not connected in a battery with 
other boilers, the heating surface of which does not exceed 02 m’, two independent 
source of power supply to the two feed apparatus shall not be necessary. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


795 


(5) In the case of miniature boilers coming under Chapter-4, the Steam pressure gauge 
may be connected to the steam space or to a steam connection to the water column 
by a syphon tube or equivalent device that will keep the gauge tube filled with water 
and if brass or bronze composition is used, the minimum size of the syphon tube 
shall be 6 mm standard pipe size; for other materials the minimum inside diameter of 
the pipe or tube shall be 3 mm. 


(6) For Electrode boilers, see regulation 356. 


(7) In case of boilers with reheaters, the reheaters shall be protected with one or more 
relieving devices of 05% capacity (5% of the total capacity shall be located in the 
steam flow path between reheater outlet and first stop valve) to avoid over pressure 
in case of internal failures. 


82. Additional Requirements for Automatic Boilers.—(])Every boiler which is provided 
with the appropriate water level and /or firing control, to allow for automatic working, shall 
comply with the following requirements: 


(a) In the event of failure of automatic control, boiler shall be capable of being 
brought under immediate manual control. 


(0) In those cases where the control and alarm devices are housed in chambers 
external to the boiler, the following shall apply, namely:- 


(i) The boiler shall have provision made for isolating the steam and water 
connections of the chambers from the boilers. Such isolating valves shall be 
capable of being locked in the open position and shall preferably be of the 
parallel slide type but if screw down stop valves are fitted, those on the water 
connection shall be mounted with the spindle horizontal to avoid the possibility of 
an air lock. The steam and water connections of the chambers shall be not less 
than 25 mm bore. In those cases where sequencing control water valves are 
fitted, the steam isolating valve may be omitted; 


(ii) The boiler shall be provided means to test operation of the control or alarm and 
to blow through separately the water connection and the chamber to prevent the 
accumulation of deposits. The means provided for flowing through shall be 
sequencing valves or equivalent devices so arranged that the water connection 
to the boiler cannot be shut off unless the drain connections to the chamber is 
open; 


(iii) The boiler shall have a drain system from the chambers which provides a visual 
indication of flow. Tundishes of adequate size, placed in a prominent position 
shall be used wherever practicable. 


(c)Where the boiler is provided with electrical equipment for water level and firing 
control, it shall have this equipment so designed that any fault in the circuits caused, 


796 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


both in the fuel and air supply, the boiler to be automatically shut off. Positive means 
requiring manual resetting shall be provided to cut off the fuel and air supplies to the 
boilers should there be a failure of electricity supply to water level and / or firing 
control equipment. All electrical conductors and equipment in connection with water 
level and firing controls shall be of adequate size and shall be properly insulated and 
protected against danger including adequate protection against the ingress of 
moisture and the effects of high temperature. 


(d)Where the evaporating capacity of the boiler is greater than 3700 Kg/h, it shall have 
automatic water level alarms and firing controls and can be tested regularly without 
altering the level of water in the boiler. The water level alarms may be incorporated in 
the automatic control system. With a perceptible water level which are arranged for 
automatic working and not intended for continuous supervision, shall be provided 
with an entirely independent and separately operated over-riding control in addition to 
the water level and firing control specified in sub-regulations (2) and (3). The over- 
riding control shall comply with the following requirements: 


(i) Cut off fuel supply to the burners or the fuel and air supply to solid fuel stoker 
and operate an audible alarm when the water level in the boiler falls to a pre- 


determined low water level; 


(ii) Be of the lock-out type and so arranged that control or its electrical circuit has to 
be manually reset before the boiler can be brought back into operation; 


(iii) Be provided with its own entirely independent electrical control circuit. 
(e)Where mounted externally to the boiler, the over-riding control shall - 


(i) be provided with its own chamber; 
(ii) Comply with the requirements of clause (b). 


(2) Automatic water level control shall be as follows:- 
(a) float or displacer operated; or 
(b) operated by electrical probe or thermostat; or 


(c) operated by other approved principle to the satisfaction of the Inspecting Authority. 


The control equipment shall regulate the feed-water supply to the boiler in order 
to effectively maintain the level of water in the boiler between predetermined limits. 


(3) Automatic firing controls shall comply with the following requirements- 


(a) At all times they shall effectively control the supply of fuel and air to the 
combustion equipments. 


(0) They shall shut off the fuel supply to the burners or the fuel and air supply to the 
stoker under the following conditions:- 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] 


भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


797 


(i) Flame failure or pilot flame failure in the cases of gas, oil or pulverised 
fuel fired boilers. This control shall be of the lockout type required to be 
manually reset; 

(ii) Failure to ignite the fuel at the burner within a pre-determined time. The 
control shall be of the lock-out type required to be manually reset; 

(ili) When the water level in a boiler falls below a pre-determined safe level. 
The control shall also cause an audible alarm. 

(iv) Failure of forced or induced draught fans or any automatic flue damper. 

(v) Increase in furnace pressure to a pre-determined value. 


Note: The above provisions shallnot apply to once-through forced circulation boiler.

valves are connected directly to the boiler. In the case of valves not 
connected directly to the boiler this temperature limitation may be increased 
to 260°C. 


PART-III 


84. Castings.—()All castings shall be smooth, sound and free from flaws or other injurious 
defects. Variations in thickness at any part shall be gradual and substantial fillets shall be 
provided. 


(2) The body of a boiler mounting shall be connected to the boiler flange by a strong and 
stiff neck. In no case, the thickness of the neck of bronze mounting shallbe less than 5 
mm for sizes up to and including 9 mm bore or 6 mm size over 9 mm bore. 


85. Packing of Cocks.—()The bodies of all cocks except those for pressure gauges shall 
be packed with any non-asbestos heat resisting material and shall be of substantial 
designand those over 25 mm bore shall have special provision, other than the gland for 
securing the plug. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


799 


(2)Water gauge column cocks may be any non-asbestos heat resisting material packed or 
solid plug type. 


86. Covers and Spindles.—()Valves of 38 mm bore and above directly connected to 
boilers, and other valves of 63 mm bore and over where fitted with a cover shall have such 
cover secured by bolts or studs and the screwed portion of the spindle shall be outside the 
stuffing box. All valves for superheated steam shall be fitted with an external screwed 
spindle. 


(2) (a) Where the covers of valves are secured by studs shall be screwed into the body with 
full thread for a length of at least one diameter. 
(0) The stud holes shall not penetrate into the pressure space of any casting. 


(3) Valves with screwed covers shall be fitted with suitable locking device to prevent 
rotation of the cover. 


87. Direction of Operation. —Valves shall be clearly marked to indicate the direction of 
flow. Valves directly connected to boilers shall be fitted with indicators to clearly show 
whether the valve is closed or open and all valves shall open by anti-clockwise rotation. 


88. Moving Parts.—The valves and spindles shall be efficiently guided and means shall be 
provided in every case to prevent them leaving their guides. The working parts shall have 
sufficient clearance to ensure freedom of movement under all conditions of service. 


89. Flanges.—(l) Flanges shall be in accordance with the tables for the appropriate 
pressure (Appendix-F). 


(2) In the case of safety valves the drilling, thickness and bolting of inlet flanges shall be in 
accordance with tables for the appropriate pressure and material and for the diameter of 
flange adopted. In the case of outlet flanges the pressure taken shall be the pressure on 
the outlet side of the valve. 


(3) For the purpose of determining particulars of flanges for blow down and scum pipe 
fittings, the design pressure of the fittings shall be assumed to be design pressure of the 
boiler. 


(4) All flanges shall be machined on the face, spot faced, or machined at the back, and the 
bolt holes shall be drilled. 


90. Valve Seatings—Where separate seats are fitted, they shall 06 efficiently 
securedandmeans shall be provided in every case to prevent the valves leaving their guides. 


9. Chests and fittings in General.—(]) (a) All chests and fittings shall be smooth, sound 
and free from flaws, cracks or other injurious defects and after completion, the chests shall 
be hydraulically tested at minimum one and half times the maximum allowable working 
pressure of the valve for which they are intended. 


800 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(0) Hydraulic test shall be made with water which may contain a corrosion inhibiter, with 
kerosene or with other suitable liquid provided its viscosity is not greater than that of water at 
a test temperature not above 52°C. 


(2) (a) (i) Valves may be fabricated from seamless steel pipes for pressures not exceeding 

7.6 kg/cm*(g) and temperatures not exceeding 426°C.The welding shallconform to 
regulation 97 and valve chest shall be stress relieved after fabrication. 
(ii) Valves meant for use in pipe work may also be fabricated by welding from seamless 
steel pipes but no restriction as above regarding pressure and temperature shall apply to 
them provided the welding complies with all the relevant requirements of fusion welding 
such as stress relieving and radio-graphic inspection of the weld as prescribed in 
Chapter-4 of these regulations. 


(b) The maximum allowable working pressure of the chests shall be determined by 
equation (7/3), where the term ‘2 fE’ shall be substituted by the term ‘.8 x f. 


(3) The maximum allowable working pressure and the thickness of the bronze and cast Iron 
valve chests shall be determined by the following formulae, subject to the minimum 
thickness as specified in sub-regulation ( 2) ofregulation 84.

PART-IV 


92. Special requirements for safety valves.—Safety valves, ordinary, high lift, and full lift, 
shall be so constructed that breakage of any part shall not obstruct the free and full 
discharge of steam from the boiler. 


93.ordinary Lift Safety Valve— (l) A safety valve in which the valve head lifts 
automatically a distance of at least D/24 with an over-pressure not exceeding 0% of the set 
pressure. 

(2) There shall not be any mechanical stop which would prevent the valve head from being 
lifted a distance of at least D/8. D is the minimum bore of the body of seat. 


94.High Lift Safety Valve.— (|) A safety valve in which the valve head lifts automatically a 
distance of at least D/2 with an over-pressure not exceeding 0% of the set pressure. 

(2) There shall not be any mechanical stop which would prevent the valve head from being 
lifted a distance of at least D/8. D is the minimum bore of the body seat. 


95. Full Lift Safety Valve.— (l) A safety valve in which the valve head lifts automatically a 
distance such that the area of discharge which limits the flow through the valve is between 
00% and 80% of the minimum area at any section at or below the body seat. 

(2) This lift is achieved by a rapid opening within an over pressure not exceeding 5% of the 
set pressure. 


96.Discharge Capacity of Safety Valves.—(l)The rated discharge capacity of a safety 
valve which discharges saturated steam shall be calculated using the following equation;

(3) (a) The Total peak load evaporation of a boiler shall be calculated on the basis of

non-steaming economiser). 
(0) In the case of Waste Heat Boilers, however, when the evaporation per square 
meter of the heating surface is certified by the manufacturers to be less than 30 kg. 
The minimum number of safety valves required may be calculated on the basis of the 
actual maximum evaporation of the boiler. 


97. Over Pressure of Safety Valves.— (|) The safety valves shall be sodesigned that they 
attain rated discharge capacity with the over pressure not greater than that given in 
regulation 93 to 95; provided that the safety valves which have a discharge area less than 
80 per cent of the flow area, the over pressure at which the design lift is attained shall not 
exceed 0 percent of the set pressure. 
(2) For safety valves having discharge area 80 per cent of more of the flow area, the over 
pressure at which the design lift is attained shall not exceed 5 per cent of set pressure. 


98. Pressure Drop (Blow Down).— () The safety valves shall bereset at a pressure at 


least 2.5% below, but not more than 5% below the safety valves set pressure. 


(2) The 5% limit shall be increased to 6% for set pressures up to 25 kg/cm? and 0% for 
valves having a body seat bore less than 32 mm.

805 


99. Mountings of Safety ४४४९७.--()(9)52/69५ valves shall be mounted without any 
intervening valve on pads or branches used for no other purpose. The axis of the valve shall 
be vertical. 

(0) The cross — sectional area of the bore of each pad or branch shall be at least equal to the 
area of the bore at the inlet of the safety valve, or where two or more safety valves are 
mounted on the same pad or branch, at least equal to the sum of the areas of the inlet bores 
of all the safety valves. 


(2) (a) Branches shall be as short as possible so as not to impair proper action of the safety 
valves or impose any undue stress on the branches at their point of attachment to the boiler. 
(6) Nothing shall obstruct free flow to the safety valve. Branches, particularly when full lift 
safety valves are mounted on them, should be radiused at the inlet. 

(c) The inlet and outlet flanges shall be drilled in accordance with the approximate table in 
Appendix-F for the diameters of flanges adopted. 


200. Openings in Shell.—(|) No accessories other than those integral with the Safety Valve 
shall obstruct the openings in the boiler shell. 

(2) Discharging steam shall have direct access to the safety valve without flowing through 
internal pipes. 


20i. Discharge Passage.—(l) (a) The safety valve discharge pipes shall comply with the 

requirements of sub-regulations (2) , (3) and (4) of this regulation. 

(0) The discharge pipe shall be as short and straight as possible and be fitted with open 

drain to prevent accumulation of water in the pipe. Suitable arrangement shall be provided in 

the discharge pipe system so that the discharge can readily be heard by the Boiler 

Attendant. 

(2) Where a waste steam-pipe is fitted the pipe and the passage leading to it shall have a 
cross-sectional area not less than the minimum combined area of the safety valves 
required by regulation 96. 


(3) For full lift valves, the area of waste steam pipe and passage leading to it shall have a 
cross-sectional area not less than twice “A”, or such area above this minimum as maybe 
required for valves having a higher approved constant, where “A”, “E” and “P” are as 
defined in regulation 96. 


(4) (a) The area of the discharge pipe from an economiser safety relief valve shall be at least 
twice the area of the valve seating. 
(b) Where the discharge from several economiser safety relief valves is connected to the 
main discharge pipe, the diameter of the main discharge pipe shall be designed to 
prevent accumulation of pressure due to the formation of steam under the particular 
conditions of temperature and pressure which may be applicable. 


202. Drainage.—(i) For each enclosed safety valve chest, a means of draining shall be 
provided. 

(2) The drain pipe shall be laid with a continuous downward gradient clear of the boiler to a 
place where the discharge is visible and cannot do injury to any person. 


806 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


203. Moving Parts.—() The valves and spindles shall be efficiently guided and means shall 
be provided in every case to prevent their lifting out of their guides. 

(2) The working parts shall have sufficient clearance to ensure freedom of movement under 
all conditions of service. The spindle shall not be fitted with a stuffing box. 


204. Bearings for Levers.—(!) The bearings of the levers of lever valve shall be so 
designed as to allow free working of the valve under all condition of service. 

(2) Where the lever is mounted on pin bearings, the holes in the lever shall be bushed with 
non-corrodible metal, or the pins shall be of non-corrodible metal. 


205. Attachments of Weights and Springs.—(l) In a lever and weight safety valve, the 
weight shall be in one piece and attached to the lever in such a way that the safety valve 
cannot be over loaded. 


(2) (a) In the case of spring loaded safety valves, washers or ferrules shall be fitted under the 
adjusting screws so that the valves cannot be over loaded when under the steam. 
Interference with load on the spring after the safety valve has been adjusted shall be 
prevented by the fitting of a ferrule under the adjusting screw collar, or by using a lock nut 
on the adjusting screw which shall be further safe-guarded by means of a padlock or 
other suitable device. 

(0) Where springs are in tension, links or the suitable stops shall be fitted to prevent the 
spring being extended a greater amount than that corresponding to a valve lift of D/4. 


Where, D = diameter of valve seating. 


206. Easing Gear.—Safety valves shall be so arranged that they can be eased off seats 
when under pressure and the easing lever shall positively lift the valve. 


207.Lift— Safety valves shall be capable of being lifted a distance such that the area of 
the discharge edge shall not be less than the minimum aggregate area “A” in regulation 96. 


208. High and Low Water Alarms.—High and low water alarms shall be adjusted so that 
the alarm is sounded with the water level visible in the gauges. 


209. Final Settings.—Before leaving the maker’s works, each safety valve shall be adjusted 
to blow-off at the specified pressure. 


20. Adjustment of Safety Valve Set Pressure.—The set pressure of a safety valve may 
be adjusted using air or other gas as the test medium provided that the safety valve has 
been subjected previously to hydraulic test in accordance with the requirement of sub- 
regulation(!) of regulation 94. 


2.Change of Safety Valve Set Pressure.—The spring in a safety valve shall not be reset 
for any pressure more than 5% above or below that for which the valve is markedandthe set 
pressure may be changed to the satisfaction of registering authority.

(c) All springs shall be formed hot and suitably hardened and tempered.

23. Dimensions.—(4) For ordinary lift valves, the compression or extension of safety valve 
springs required to load the valves to the set pressure shall not be less than one quarter of 
the diameter of the valve due consideration being given in the case of spring loaded level 
safety valves to the ratio of leverage. 

(2)The proportion of unloaded length to external diameter of the spring shall not exceed 
4:. 

(3) These requirements do not apply to full lift and high lift safety valves.

25. Test.—(l)The permanent set in the spring (defined as the difference between free 
height and height measured ten minutes after the spring has been compressed solid three 
additional times, after pre-setting at room temperature) shall not exceed 0.5% the free 
height. 


(2) Torsion bars shall not show a permanent distortion after being twisted to an angle 
fifty per cent in excess the working angle. 


26. Extension Springs.—Extension springs shall be made from round section wire.
