28. Spacing of Coils.— The space between the coils when the valve is lifted to /4" of its 
diameter, shall be not less than .6 mm for full lift valves and 0.8 mm for ordinary and high 
lift valves. 


29.Finishing of Ends—Compression springs shall have their ends ground flat and smooth 
and at right angles to the axis of the springs over the full circumference so that when placed 
on end on a horizontal plane the springs will stand perpendicular. 


PART-V 


220.Lever valves.—Where the valve is operated by means of a lever, whether hand or 
mechanically controlled, the lever shall be of ample strength and the bearings shall be so 
designed as to allow free working of the valve under all conditions of service. 


22. Steam stop valve.—(l) (a) The stop valve connecting the boiler or super heater to the 
steam—delivery pipe shall be located as near the outlet from the final superheater header as 
is convenient and practicable or in case of boilers without super-heaters as close as 
practicable to the drum. 

(0) Where two or more boilers are connected with a steam receiver or any other vessel, a 
steam stop valve shall be fitted between the boiler and such receiver or vessel. 


(2) (a)Steam stop valves shall be attached direct to the boiler shell or to suitable pads or 
stand blocks and the neck or the valve chest shall be reasonably short and of strong 
construction. 

(0) The steam stop valve may also be attached to a stand pipe, a connecting pipe or the 
super-heater header. 

(c) The attachment may be made by bolted flanges or butt-welded joints. Such butt- welded 
joints shall be suitably stress relieved, where necessary: 


Provided that in the case of a larger boiler in which it is proposed for the purpose of drainage 
or owing to obstruction to connect the steam—pipes to the steam stop valve at a higher level 
than would be obtained under this regulation, a vertical stand pipe not exceeding 5 
diameters in height will be permitted between the stop valve and the boiler. Such stand pipes 
shall be of strong construction and of wrought iron, mild steel, or cast steel. The flanges of 
wrought or mild steel pipes shall be welded to the pipes, and there shall be no branch on the 
stand pipe for any other connection: 


8l2 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


Provided also that in the case of large boiler in which it is desired to fit a tee piece for 
the purpose of providing a branch connection between the stop valve and the boiler, such a 
tee piece may be so fitted, the tee piece shall be of strong construction, of wrought iron, mild 
steel, or cast steel and shall not exceed 2'2 diameters in height and a stop valve shall be 
fitted direct to each tee piece branch. 


(3) When two or more boilers are connected to a common steam main and there are no 
combined stop and isolating valves fitted to them an automatic isolating valve shall be 
compulsory. In the case of boilers fitted with welded pipes, fitting of an independent 
automatic isolating valve shall be compulsory. 


PART -VI 


222.Blow-down cock or valve and pipes.— (l) The blow-down cock or valve shall be of 
substantial construction. 

(2) The waste pipe attached to the cock or valve shall not be bound fast in arch or brick work 
and shall discharge at a point where there is no danger of injury to any person. 

(3) These pipes shall not be connected to a pipe common to another boiler. 

(4) The continuous blow-downs may, however be connected to a common header 
discharging freely to an adequately vented tank or sump. 

(5) The headers shall be of sufficiently large cross- section and the blow- off tank shall be 
provided with a vent pipe free from valves and of sufficient size to prevent accumulation of 
pressure. If, however, the tank is intended for collecting flash steam, a safety valve of 
adequate capacity shall be provided. 

(6) The tank shall be so located that all parts will be accessible for inspection. 


223 Blow-Down mountings.—(|) Each boiler shall be fitted with a suitable blow-down valve 
or cock placed at, or as near as practicable, to the lowest point of the boiler. 


(2) (a) For locomotive, vertical and marine type boilers, the valve or cock shall be attached 
direct to the boiler or to a suitable pad or stand pipe. 
(b) For water tube boilers the valve or cock shall be outside the brick work with a 
substantial steel pipe between it and the mud box. 


(3) For Cornish and Lancashire boilers, the cocks or valve may be attached to a cast steel 
elbow pipe of substantial section bolted to a suitable stand pipe or pad welded to the boiler. 
But cast iron elbow pipes shall not be permitted. 


224.Blow-Down Valve or Cock.—(|) Each valve or cock shall be fitted with a device which 

shall clearlyindicate its open and closed positions, and any key or similar device for 

operating the valve or cock shall be such that it cannot be removed unless the valve or cock 

is fully closed. 

(2) The locking feather shall be secured by welding. 

(3) Cocks fitted with taper plugs shall be of the bolted cover type with separate packing 
glands. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


843 


PART -४॥ 


225.Water Gauges.—(l)Every boiler shall have two means of indicating the water in it outof 
which one shall be conventional gauge glass: 


Provided that in the case of boiler drums below 9 cm diameter where there is difficulty 
in fitting two water gauges, two test cocks and a glass water gauge shall be fitted. 


(2) (a) The lowest visible part of the glass of the water gauge and lower test cocks shall 
be fixed at safe working level. 
(0) For locomotive type and vertical boilers this shall not be less than 50 mm above the 
highest part of the firebox roof plate. Minimum length of the visible portion of the gauge 
glasses shall be 200 mm. 
(c) The length may be increased depending upon the capacity of the boiler by the 
Inspecting Authority. 


(3) (a) Glass water gauges shall be so placed as to be easily seen and reached by the 
boiler attendant. 
(0) The fittings of glass water gauges and test cocks shall be of substantial make with 
large passage ways through them to facilitate cleaning. 
(c) The gauge cocks when open shall have their handles in a vertical direction and each 
handle at its junction with the plug shall be plainly marked with a deep line to indicate the 
direction of the passage way through the plug. 
(d) When detachable handle are provided arrangement shall be made to prevent 
incorrect fitting of the handles. 


226. Drains.—A drain cock or valve with a suitable discharge pipe shall be fitted to each 
water gauge. 


227. Protectors.— (/) Where tubular glass water gauges are fitted, substantial protectors 
shall be provided. 
(2) The glass shall be suitably treated to prevent splintering. 


228. Glass Size.— Tubular water gauge glasses shall be not less than 38 mm and not more 
than 79 mm outside diameter. 


229. Safety Devices— Water gauge glass mountings shall be fitted with self-closing 
devices in the bottom arms and it is recommended that a similar device may be fitted in the 
top arm. 


230. Gauge Columns.— Where the gauges are mounted on a column, there shall be no 
connecting passage between the top and bottom arms of the column unless valves or cocks 
are fitted between the columns and the boiler. 


23. Isolating Cocks.— Where isolating cocks or valves connecting water gauge pipes to 
the boiler are fitted, they shall be not less than 25 mm bore and of the bolted cover type with 
separate packing gland. 


8l4 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


PART -VIII 


232. Pressure Gauges Dials— (l) For pressure upto35 kg/cm* (g), pressure gauge dials 
shall be graduated in kg/cm*(g) from zero to twice the pressure as nearly as may be 
practicable. 


(2) For pressure exceeding 35 kg/cm*(g),the range of the graduation shall be from zero to 
one and a half times the maximum allowable working pressure, as nearly as may be 
practicable, but in no case shall the maximum graduation on the gauge be less than 70 
kg/cm? (g). 


(3) The scale on the dial shall be clearly and permanently marked in kg/cm? (g). 


(4) The maximum allowable working pressure shall be marked in red on the dial of each 
pressure gauge. 


(5) (a) Where the gauge is compensated for a head of water between the gauge and the 
boiler connection, the amount of such compensation shall be marked on the dial. 
Pressure gauge shall be calibrated within an accuracy of + percent. 

(0) Boiler pressure gauges shall not be less than 50 mm in diameter. 


(6) The travel of the pointer of the dial gauge shall not exceed 325°. 


233. Connections.—All pressure gauges shall be fitted with a syphon pipe and a cock or 
valve integral with, or adjacent to, the gauge in such manner that the gauge may be shut off 
and removed whilst the boiler is under steam. 


234. Gauge Cocks.—The handles of the gauge cocks shall be parallel to the pipes in which 
they are located when the cocks are open and marks shall be cut on the shank of the cock 
indicating open position. 


235.Test Connections- Competent Person’s Pressure Gauge Attachment.— ()Every 
boiler shall be fitted with a valve or cock carrying in a vertical position a receiving screw for 
attachment of the Competent Person’s pressure gauge. 


(2) The receiving socket shall be tapped for M/20 x .5 metric threads and shall be fitted with 
an easily removable cap. 


PART -IX 


236. Fusible Plugs.—(|)Fusible plugs shall be of sufficient height and fitted in such a 
position as to give early protection to all parts of the boiler liable to damage by the direct 
application of furnace heat in the event of shortness of water. 


Note: For example - In Lancashire boilers the fusible plugs shall be in the crowns of the 
furnaces from 305 mm to 457 mm in front of the brick work fire bridge. 


(2) (a) On boilers having wet back reversing chamber, a minimum of two fusible plugs 
shall be fitted; one on the crown of the reversing chamber and the other on one of the tube 
plates. On boilers not having wet back reversing chamber, at least one fusible plug shall be 
provided on the front end tube plate. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


85 


(b) The plug shall be fitted in such a way that in the event of fusion of the plug, the pressure 
inside the boiler shall push the pellets out. 


237.Type.— (3) Fusible plugs shall consist of an outer body with a central conical passage. 


(2) The smallest part to be not greater than 3 mm for plugs suitable for pressures up to 7 
kg/cm*(g) and not greater than 0 mm for plugs for pressures exceeding 7 kg/cm’ (g). 


(3) The passage shall be closed by a plug secured by an annual lining of fusible alloy so that 
the plug may drop clear if the lining melts. 


(4) The portion of the body carrying the fusible metal shall preferably be detachable from the 
base to allow of easy replacement without removing the whole fitting from the boiler. 


238. Material—() The non-fusible portions of the plug shall be of bronze except where the 
nature of the boiler water precludes the use of non-ferrous material. 


(2) The fusible metal shall be ofan alloy melting readily at a temperature not less than 66°C 
in excess of the saturated steam temperature at the design pressure of the boiler. 


239. Attachment to Boiler.— () Wherever practicable, fusible plugs shall be screwed into 
the boiler plates from the water side. 


(2) The screwed portion shall have threads of Whitworth form not more than / per 25 mm. 
PART -X 
240.Feed Valves.— (|) Feed check valves shall be of the non-return type. 


(2) Where the valve is not of screw-down non-return type, a separate screw-down valve 
shall be provided. 

(3) The discharge from the feed check valve or from the internal feed pipe (if provided) 
shall be above low water level and in the case of Lancashire and Cornish boilers, shall 
be at least 52 cm beyond the fire bridge: 


Provided that the aforesaid restriction regarding the position of feed discharge level 
shall not apply in the case of water tube boilers. 


24. Operating Position.—Feed check valves or regulating valves shall be so arranged as 
to enable them to be satisfactorily operated from the boiler floor. 


242. Requirements as to Feed Apparatus in certain cases.—In the case of a battery of 
boilers connected to a common feed range, the requirements ofregulationi8 in respect of 
the number of feed apparatus shall be considered to have been fulfilled provided a total 
supply of feed water, not less than the combined maximum continuous rating of all active 
boilers can be maintained even if any one of the sources of power supply fails.

CHAPTER -7 


PIPES AND FITTINGS 


249. Pipes.—(l)(a) Steam-pipes may be ofcarbon steel, cast steel, alloy steel and nickel 
alloys. 

(0) Pipes may be solid drawn (cold or hot finished), butt welded or electric resistance 
welded. 


(2) Where, material used is in conformity with the code of the country of manufacture 
and in accordance with provisions of these regulations, the permissible stress figures 
specified in the code at different temperatures may be accepted in lieu of figures 
computed from the data required to be furnished under regulation 256 in any of the 
following cases, namely:- 


(a)Where a certificate is furnished from the Inspecting Authority to the effect that the 
steel complies with requirements of the steel grade (to be specified by the 
Inspecting Authority) and that the permissible stress for the working condition as 
allowed for in the code of the country of manufacture falls within the permissible 
limits under theseregulations. 


(b)Where the basis upon which these stresses have been arrived at is made 
available and such basis is not found as to give rise to stresses higher than those 
permissible under the regulations. 


(c) Where pipes have to be fabricated by longitudinal fusion butt electric arc welding of 
plates rolled to shape, the limits provided for butt welded pipes in Table 7/4 under 
regulation 255 shall not apply. 

(d) The requirements other than those relating to the minimum thickness of shell for 
fusion butt welding provided in Chapter-2 shall be applicable to such pipes. 


(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in Chapter-7, the hydraulic test for pipes in 
maker's premises may be dispensed with by the Inspecting Authority: 


Provided that these pipes have been fully tested by non-destructive 
examination by radiographic or ultrasonic techniques: 


Provided further that in the case of pipes having internal diameter 000 mm 
and more, the plates used for the manufacture of pipes and the long seam welds of 
pipes are fully tested by non-destructive examination like ultrasonic or radiographic 
testing and the soundness of pipes both in the parent material and in the weld is 
established in the maker's premises; and the whole component of the pipes, after 
completion of any further fabrication and erection at site, are hydraulically tested at a 
pressure not less than .5 times the maximum allowable working pressure of the 
piping system: 


Provided also that in the event of detection of any defect after conducting 
hydraulic test of these pipes at site, it shall be the responsibility of the manufacturer

heat treatment.

(6) Hot finished seamless pipes may, however, be made of Bessemer Steel.

254. Method of manufacture, heat treatment and marking.— (l) On completion of any 
work which involves heating, whether for hot bending of the pipe or for any other similar 
purpose, the pipe shall be carefully annealed. 


(2) (a) The cold drawn seamless carbon steel pipes and welded carbon steel pipes shall 
be supplied in normalised condition. 


826 


THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY 


(0) Hot finished seamless carbon steel pipes shall be supplied in hot finished 
condition or in normalised condition at the option of the manufacturer. 


(c) The seamless alloy steel pipe either cold finished or hot finished and welded 
pipes shall be supplied in normalised and tempered condition. 


(d) By agreement between the users and the manufacturer, the pipes may be 
delivered in a condition other than normalised and tempered condition in which case 
they shall be suitable for subsequent manipulation and the user shall be informed of 
the heat-treatment necessary to give required properties. 


(3) (a) (i) Pipe bending and forming (reducing or swaging) operation shall be done by any 


hot or cold method and to any radius which shall result in a surface free from cracks, 
buckles or other defects as determined by the method of inspection specified in the 
design. 

(ii) A post bending or post forming heat treatment for carbon steel material is required 
with a nominal wall thickness in excess of 9 mm unless the bending or forming 
operation are performed and completed at normalizing temperatures, where no further 
heat treatment is required. 

(iii) The heat treatment where required, shall be normalised or stress relieved, as the 
case may be. 


(0) A post bending or post forming heat treatment shall be required for all ferritic alloy 
steel material with nominal pipe size 00 mm and larger or with a nominal thickness 3 
mm or greater. 


(c) (i) If hot bending or forming is performed the material shall receive normalize and 
temper or tempering heat-treatment as required by the design. 
(ii) For cold operation, tempering heat-treatment shall be applied. 


(4) Marking shall be carried out in accordance with regulation 329.

PART-II 


258. Flanges of carbon steel pipes.—(!)The material for carbon steel flanges, where 
forged, cast or cut from the plates (excluding branches forged integral with the pipes) shall 
be made of steel produced by an Open Hearth or Electric process or any of the Oxygen 
processes. 


832 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(2) Carbon steel flanges shall not be used for temperatures exceeding 454°C and 
such flanges shall be made without a weld and free from lamination or other 
defects secured by welding. 


(3) Blank flanges shall be of mild steel or cast steel and shall be not less in thickness 
than the flanges to which they are attached. The material shall comply with the 
requirements specified in relevant regulations of chapter-2 or Chapter-4 of these 
regulations. 


259. Flanges of alloy steel pipes.— (i) (a) The material for alloy steel flanges where 
forged, cast or cut from plates (excluding branches forged integral with the pipes), 
shall be made from the steel produced by an Open Hearth or Electric process. 

(o)Flanges shall be made without a weld and shall be free from lamination or other defects. 
(c) The material of alloy steel flanges shall comply the provisions of regulation 30. 

(d) The material for flanges shall be similar to that of the pipes to which they are to 
be attached. 

(e) The flanges are to be so designed that the total stress induced in them does not 
exceed the maximum permissible stress as per criteria mentioned inregulation 70. 


(2) Blank flanges of alloy steel shall be not less in thickness that the flanges to which 
they are to be attached and the material shall be similar to that of the flanges. 


260.Non-ferrous flanges.— (l) The material for non-ferrous flanges shall be of bronze. 
(2)The chemical composition shall comply with the requirements of clause (iv) of sub- 


regulation() of regulation’83. 

(3) When flanges are attached to copper pipes by brazing, they shall be secured in 
such additional way like forming a conical bore in the flange so that the resistance to 
withdrawal from the flange does not depend wholly on the brazing. 


26. Screwed on flanges.— (|) Where flanges are secured by screwing, the screw thread 
on the pipes and in the flanges shall be arranged to end at a point just inside the back of 
boss of the flange and after the flange has been screwed on, the pipe shall be expanded into 
the flange by a roller expander. 

(2) Such screwed and expanded flanges may be used for steam for a maximum allowable 
working pressure of 3.5 kg/cm? (g) and maximum temperature of 399 °C and for feed for a 
maximum allowable working pressure of 42 kg/cm? (g). 


262. Loose flanges.— (|)(a)Loose flanges may be used where the joints are made by metal 
faces integral with ends of the pipes and alternatively these joints may be welded or seal 
welded. 

(0) The loose flanges shall conform to the table given in Appendix-F. 


(2) Where the joint is formed by integral flanges, after machining these shall be not 
less in thickness than the designed thickness of the pipe as calculated by Equation (7/2)

Note: 


All dimensions shown in the figures of types / to 7 relate to finished sizes. 
The design conditions for each type are as follows: 
Types 4, 2 and 3 flanges for all maximum allowable working pressure and 
temperature conditions. 
Types 4 and 5 flanges for all pressure conditions up to and including 42 kg/cm? (g) 
and design temperature not exceeding 399°C. 
Types 6 and 7 flanges for all pressure conditions up to and including 7.6 kg/cm? (g) 
and temperature not exceeding 399°C except that Bossed flanges of type 6 shall not 
be used on pipes over 304 mm_ in nominal bore, nor Bossed flanges of type 7 on 
pipes 52 mm in nominal bore. 
Type 8 flanges for all maximum allowable working pressure and temperature 
conditions and this type shall be used only for pipes up to and including 5 mm 
nominal bore. These flanges shall not be used where severe erosion or corrosion is 
expected to occur. 


(3) Type 7,2,3,4 and 5 Carbon Steel types flanges welded on by the metal 


arc process shall have the welds stress relieved where the design depth of the weld 
recess is greater than 20 mm and all welds joining flanges to alloy steel pipes shall 
be stress relieved. 


(4) Where type 4 flanges are attached by oxy-acetylene welding, the welds shall be 
normalised in accordance with the following requirements: 


(a) Welds in mild steel pipes shall be normalised by heating the metal to a 


temperature between 900° and 950°C, the temperature then being maintained for not 


834 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


less than two minutes for pipes up to and including 02 mm bore, and for not less 
than five minutes for pipes over 02 mm bore. 

(0) Welds in pipes made from the alloy steel shall be normalised by heating 
the metal to a temperature between 925° and 975°C, the temperature then being 
maintained for not less than two minutes for pipes up to and including 02 mm bore, 
and for not less than five minutes for pipes over 02 mm bore. 

(c) The higher temperatures of between 950° and 975°C, shall be used for 
alloy steels having a carbon content up to and including 0.{2 percent and the lower 
temperatures of between 925° and 950°C shall be used for alloy steels having a 
carbon content of more than 0.2 percent. 

(d) After normalising the joint shall be covered with a suitable muff or 
asbestos cloth to ensure slow and even cooling. 

(e) The normalising of welds in pipes up to 02 mm bore may be carried out 
with welding flames the temperature being judged with the aid of a colour card, or 
measured by means of one or more thermo-couples or an optical pyrometer. 

(f) The normalising of welds in pipes over 02 mm bore shall preferably be 
carried out in a portable pipe normalising furnace or muffle, the temperature being 
measured by means of one or more thermo-couples or an optical pyrometer. 

(g) The width of the zone to be heat treated to the specified temperature shall 
extend at least 3 mm on either side of the weld reinforcement. 


(5) The procedure to be observed in the stress relieving of welds shall be in accordance 
with regulation 23 and stress relieving shall be carried out by any of the following 
methods:- 


(a) (i) Local heating using a portable muffle furnace, induction coils or other 
suitable appliances and due care shall be taken to apply heat uniformly over 
the area to be treated. 

(ii) The use of procedures not providing adequate control such as manual 
operated gas torches are not permissible. 

(iii) The temperature shall be measured by the thermo-couples pinned, welded 
or otherwise su _ itably attached to the surface of the pipe and where necessary, 
protection from flame impingement shall be taken. 


(0) The temperature of the joint during heating in a stationary industrial furnace 
shall be measured by thermo-couples appropriately placed within the furnace 
as to give a true measure of the joint temperature. 


264. Standard flanges.—The size and thickness of flanges and the number and size of their 
bolts shall be as shown in Appendix-F. 


265. Joints.— (l) Theseregulations provide for ordinary bolted flange joints and special 
types of joints may be used, subject to the approval of the Inspecting Authority or Chief 
Inspector, as the case may be. 


(2) Welded butt joints of pipes or socket welded joints for pipes, valves and fitting shall 
be made by arc welding process and post weld heat treated effectively as per 
regulation 23.

(a) (i) Local heating using a portable muffle induction coils, or other suitable heating

(ii) Due care shall be taken to apply heat uniformly over the area to be treated. 

(iii) The use of procedures not providing adequate control such as manual operated 
gas torches are not permissible. 

(iv) The temperature shall be maintained symmetrically over peripheral band of metal 
of a minimum width of three times the width of the butt welded preparation. 

(v) The temperature shall be measured by thermo-couples pinned, welded or 
otherwise suitably attached to the surface of the pipe and, where necessary, 
protected from flame impingement.

Tests on completed welds on pipelines.— (l) For tests on completed welds on 
pipelines, pipelines shall be divided into followingtwo classes, namely:- 


(a) Class-l: Pipelines for service conditions in which any one of the following 
limitsare exceeded. 


(i) Design temperature 2/8°C 
(ii) Maximum allowable working Pressure 7.6 kg/cm?(g) 
(iii) | Feed water pressure 24.6 kg/cm? (g) 


(0) Class Il: Pipelines for service conditions in which none of the foregoing limits is 
exceeded. 


(2) For identification of welds,the welders’ identification mark shall be stamped 
without indentation, or stencilled adjacent to each completed weld. 


Tests for Class | pipelines—(l) Where the completed pipelines are not tested by 
the application of hydraulic pressure, the welds shall be subjected to the following 
inspection procedure, namely:- 


(a) (i) For piping of over 02 mm bore, all butt-welds shall be subjected to 
non-destructive examination by radiographic or other approved methods. 
(ii) The entire circumference of the first five welds made by each welder 
shall be non-destructively examined and If these are found to be 
satisfactory and Competent Person is satisfied with the welding 
techniques, methods of control and supervision employed, relaxation in 


836 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


the extent of non-destructive examination may be considered, but this 
relaxation shall in no case permit the non-destructive examination of less 
than one-third of the circumference of each of remaining welds made by 
the welder concerned. 


(0) For piping off02 mm bore and under, but not less than 38 mmbore, five 
percent of the butt-welds made by each welder with a minimum of two 
welds per welder, selected at random shall be subjected to non- 
destructive examination by either radiographic or other approved methods 
or may be cut out for visual examination and bend tests. 


(c) For piping of less than 38 mm bore, special tests are not normally required 
but two percent of the welds by each welder on a pipeline may be cut out 
from the pipe-line for visual examination and bend tests. 


(2) Where the completed pipelines are tested by the application of hydraulic 
pressure, the welds shall be subjected to the following inspection procedure, 
namely:- 


(a) For piping ofover 02 mm bore, ten percent of the welds made by each 
welder on a pipeline with a minimum of two welds per welder, selected at 
random, shall be subjected to non-destructive examination by 
radiographic or other approved methods. 

(0) For piping of 02 mm bore and under, but not less than 38 mm bore, two 
per cent of the welds made but each welder on a pipeline with a minimum 
of one weld per welder, selected at random, shall be subjected to non- 
destructive examination by radiographic or other approved methods or 
may be cut out for visual examination and bend tests. 


(c) For piping of less than 38 mm bore, special tests are not normally 
required,but two percent of the welds by each welder on a pipeline may be 
cut from the pipeline for visual examination and bend tests. 


268. Tests for Class Il pipelines.—(])AIl pipelines under this classification shall 
be subjected to hydraulic test on completion of erection. 


(2) (a) On completion of the first ten production welds made by each welder, one 
of the welds shall be cut out for test purposes or alternatively, the welder 
shall prepare a test specimen made up of two similar lengths of piping 
welded in a position as closely representative of a selected production weld 
as is practicable. (b) The test specimen shall be subjected to visual 
examination and bend tests. 


(3) Two percent of the remainder of the welds made by each welder shall be 
selected at random and cut out for test purpose, or, alternatively the welders 
shall prepare a test specimen made up of two similar lengths of piping 
welded in a position as closely representative of a selected production weld 
as far as practicable and the test specimen shall be subjected to visual 
examination and bend tests.

(a) For piping of over 02 mm bore, five per cent of the welds made by each

random shall be subjected to a non-destructive examination by 
radiographic or other approved methods. 


(b) For piping of {02 mm bore and under, one per cent of the welds made 
by each welder on a pipeline with a minimum of one weld per welder, 
selected at random shall be subjected to non-destructive examination 
by radiographic or other approved technique. 


269.Re-tests.— (l) If any test specimen is unsatisfactory, two further weld specimen for 
re-test shall be selected from the production welds and subjected to tests. 
(2) In the events of failure of any of the re-test specimens, the production welds 
carried out by this welder subsequent to the previous tests shall be subject of special 
consideration. 


270. Socket weld joints.— (|) Socket weld joints may be used with carbon and low alloy 
steel pipes not exceeding 60.3 mm. outside diameter. 
(2) Such welds shall not be used where fatigue, severe erosion or severe corrosion is

(3) The maximum allowable working pressure of the socket weld fittings shall be 
determined in accordance with equation (7//) (regulation 256). 
(4) The thickness of the socket weld fittings shall not be less than '%4 times the 
nominal thickness of pipeandthe material shall be compatible with the associated 
piping.

product.

274.Steel butt Welded fittings.— () (a) Branches, bosses and drain pockets welded to the 
pipes shall conform to the requirements of regulations 48 to 52. 
(b) Branches shall not be welded to any main at an angle of less than 60°. 


(2) (a) If the thickness of the main or branches of a single or multiple branch piece is less 
than given by the Equation(7/6),external reinforcement shall be provided. 
(b) Such reinforcement may take the form of multiple radial plates of ‘horse shoe’ 
form or the form of collars or other reinforcement, approved by the Inspecting 
Authority or Chief Inspector as the case may be, applied to or around the junction 
between the branch and the main. 


842 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)]

branch is attached to a pipe, the opening of each branch shall be projected 
perpendicularly on the axis of the main and the distance between each pair of these 
projection measured. If the distance so measured between two branches is less than 
the sum of their bores, the two branches are deemed to affect each other; if this 
distance is equal to or greater than the sum of their bores, the two branches are 
deemed not to affect each other and in calculating the reinforcement required, each 
branch is to be considered in turn together with all the branches by which it is 
affected.

275. Blow-down pipes — (l) Blow-down pipes which can be subjected to full boiler 
pressure shall be considered as saturated steam-pipes at that pressure. 


(2) Blow-down pipes which cannot be subjected to full boiler pressure shall be 
considered as saturated steam-pipes at half the design pressure of the boiler. 


276. Valves chests — (l) Chests of stop-valves, isolating valves, reducing valves, steam 
traps, etc., forming parts of wrought steel main steam piping when for use with saturated 
steam up to a gauge pressure of /kg/cm? (g)or a temperature of 204°C may be made of 
cast iron, cast steel or wrought steel in accordance with the requirements of regulation 794. 


(2) When superheated steam is used above 204°C or when pressures are above 
4kg/cm? gauge, such chests shall be made of cast or wrought steel or other approved 
material in accordance with the requirements of regulation 94. 


PART-VI 


277. Materials in the construction of steam receivers, separators, catch waters , 
accumulators and similar vessels.—(|)Material for plates, bars and sections used in the 
construction of steam receivers, separators, catch waters, accumulators and similar Vessels 
shall comply in all respects with the requirements of relevant regulations of Chapters-2 and 
4, depending upon the mode of construction. 


(2) Branches, bosses and drain pockets may be solid forged, fabricated by fusion 
welding, machined from solid bars or made from tubes. 


(3) Materials for flanges shall comply with the appropriate provisions of regulation 
258. 


[भाग ॥--खण्ड 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 855 


(4) Forgings shall comply with the requirements of regulations58 to 62 


(5) Steel castings for shells or pressure parts of shell shall comply with regulations 
5/ to 57. 


278. Construction and workmanship.—(l)Shell ends formed separately from the shell may 
be dished or flat or the ends of the shell may be forged down and closed by manhole doors 
or by plugs or branches welded in. 


(2) (a) (i) Each dished end shall be made from one rolled plate. 
(ii) If this is impracticable, owing to the large diameter, the dished end plate may 
be made from two plates fusion butt welded together and in such cases, the line 
of weld shall be parallel to the horizontal axis of the vessels and the weld shall be 
radiographed after forming. 
(iii) The shape of dished end shall conform to the requirements of regulation 774. 
(iv) Dishing end peripheral flanging shall be done by machine. 
(v) Cold flanging shall not be adopted. 
(vi) All plates which have been dished, flanged or locally heated shall afterwards 
be efficiently heat treated for the purpose of relieving internal stresses, unless 
during the last stage of manufacture, they have been uniformly heated throughout 
to a suitable temperature. 
(vii) Care shall be taken to see that the flanges are cylindrical, of good surface 
and free from local irregularities. 


(0) Where flats are pressed in dished ends for the attachment of connections, 
they shall be formed with an ample radius at the junctions of the flat and curved 
surfaces and shall be free from sharp corners and tool marks. 


(c) Dished ends shall be attached to the cylindrical part of the shell by one of the 

following methods: 

(i) Welding with butt Joints of the Single or Double U or V Type;where the 
internal diameter of the shell is 60 mm or over, the joints shall in all cases, 
be welded from both sides of the plate. 

(ii) Where the internal diameter of the shell is less than 60 mm the joints may 
be welded from one side only, when efficient welding from inside is 
considered impracticable. 


(iii) In the construction of unfired boilers when the dished ends do not form part of 
the heating surface, cold spun dished ends conforming to IS: 2825 may be 
used. 


(3) (a) Flat ends shall be of forged steel or plate steel and shall be welded to the 
cylindrical part of the shell or bolted to flanges which shall be attached to the 
cylindrical part of the shell in accordance with regulation 263.

of the shell plate whereverpracticable andwhere welding is done from one side 
only, care shall be taken to ensure full penetration using backing strips.

279. Access to Shells.— (|) At least one manhole shall be provided to allow access for 
thorough cleaning and inspection, except that where the shell is too small to permit 
entry, cleaning and inspection openings of sufficient size and number shall be 
provided. (2) When there is an elliptical opening in the cylindrical part of the shell, the 
minor axis shell, wherever practicable be parallel to the longitudinal axis of the shell. 


280.Compensating rings to openings and doors.—The material, construction and 
workmanship of compensating rings and doors shall comply with the relevant 
provisions of Chapters 2, 3 and 2. 


28. Branches and other connections.—(|) (a) Connections to shell shall be made by 
means of branches, pressed plate saddles, forged pads or bosses or where the 
thickness of the shell is sufficient to allow suitable surface to be obtained, connections 
may be attached directly to the shell, provided that the minimum thickness at the hole in 
the shell is not less than the thickness required for the maximum allowable working 
pressure and temperature considering the shell as being unpierced and that the diameter 
of the hole does not exceed the maximum diameter of an uncompensated hole as 
defined in regulation 47 and 79. 

(b) Studs for securing such connections shall have a full thread holding in the shell for a 
length of at least one diameter and the stud holes shall not penetrate the whole 
thickness of the shell. 

(c) All holes for bolts and studs in branches, saddles and forged pads shall be drilled. 

(d) Where such connections are secured by welding alone, a minimum of two runs of 
metal shall be deposited at each weld, except for seal welds. 

(e) Each run of weld metal shall be thoroughly cleaned and free from slag before the 
next run is deposited. 

(f) The final finish of the welds shall be such that change of section from shell to branch 
is gradual and free from sharp notches. 

(g) Where the diameter of the shell is 60 mm and over, welding shall be from both 
sides of the plate. 

(0) Where the internal diameter of the shell is less than 60 mm, external and internal 
welds shall be applied unless it is considered that efficient welding from both sides is 
impracticable. 

(i) This does not apply to the methods of attachment shown in Fig.7/40 and 7/4/ in which 
the welding shall always be from both sides.

(2)(a) Branches of not more than 38 mm nominal bore may be screwed into the shell with a 
taper thread and seal welded, provided that the thickness of the shell is sufficient to allow 
for a length of thread equal to the diameter of the branch. 

(b) Where the thickness of the shell is not sufficient for the purpose, a boss may be 
welded on so that the total thickness of the boss and shell is at least equal to the required 
length of thread. 

(c) Methods of attachment of such bosses are shown in Figs. 7/65 to 7/69. 


(3) (a)Branches, pressed plate saddles, forged pads of bossesshall be secured to the shell 
by one of the following methods,- 


(i) Welding; 
(ii) Screwing and Seal Welding. 


(0) 0) Methods of attachment secured by welding are shown in Figs. 7/40 to 7/64 of this 
chapter. 
(ii) Branches may be provided with flanges for ordinary bolted joints. Joints of 
special type may also be used. 
(iii) Flanges for ordinary bolted joints shall be in accordance with the appropriate 
table of Appendix-F and shall be forged solid with the branches or attached in 
accordance with regulation 263. 
(iv) They shall be machined on the jointing and bolt bearing surfaces. 


(c) () Where pressed plate saddles are used, they shall be formed to bed closely to the 
shell and shall be machined on the face adjoining the connection and machined or 
flame cut by machine on the edges. 

(ii) The studs for the attachment of the connection, if screwed through the saddle, 
shall each be fitted with a nut on the inside. 

(iit) Where the stud holes do not penetrate through the saddle, the length of the 
screwed portion of the stud in the plate shall be not less than the diameter of the 
stud. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


867 


(0) The join faces of all pads shall be machined. 


(e) 0) The pads shall be sufficiently thick to allow the drilling of stud holes for 
connections without the inner surface being pierced. 
(ii) The length of the screwed portion of the stud in the pad shall be not less than the 
diameter of the stud. 
(iii) Method of attachment of pads secured by welding are shown in Fig. 7/70 to 7/76 
of this chapter but where pads of the type shown in Fig. 7/7Oare used, they shall be 
formed to bed closely to the shell. 


(f) 0) Tapped bosses of not more than 38 mm standard pipe welded to the shell, may 
be used for maximum allowable working pressure not exceeding 4 kg/cm? (g) and 
design temperatures not exceeding 343°C. 

(ii) Such bosses shall have taper threads. 
(iii) Methods of attachment of bosses secured by welding are shown in Fig. 7/65, 
7/69 of this chapter 


(9) 0) All welded attachments other than flange connections shall be by the metal arc 
process and the electrodes used shall comply with the requirements ofregulations 7 
to 76. 
(ii) Where tack welds are used, they shall be sound and unless cut out, shall be 
carefully fused into the main runs. 


(h) All parts secured by welding shall be effectively heat treated after completion of all 
welding and before hydraulic test. 


282.Shell joints .— (l)Fusion Welded Shellsshall be classified as follows: 


(a) Class | - No limit to scantlings. 
(0) Class Il - When none of the following limits exceeds:— 


(i) maximum allowable working pressure- 35 kg/cm? (g) 

(ii) product of maximum allowable working pressure and internal diameter in 
centimeters — 3750. 

(iii) design temperature — 343°C. 


(c) Class Ill - When none of the following limits exceeds:— 


(i) maximum allowable working pressure -7.4 kg/cm? (g) 

(ii) product of maximum allowable working pressure and internal diameter in 
centimeters — 940. 

(iii) design temperature — 77°C. 


(2) Fusion welds, preparation of seams, the method of formation of cylindrical shells 
including heat treatment after bending, method of making welded seams, types of 
welded joints, test plates and circularity of shells, all shall conform to the 
requirements of Chapter -4, except for the following, namely;- 


(a) (4) Whenever practicable, seams shall be welded from both sides of the plate. 


868 


THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


Additional runs of metal shall be deposited at both surfaces of the welded seams to 
build up to a thickness 0 per cent greater than thickness of the plate. 

(ii) The surfaces of welds wherever carried out on both sides shall be ground smooth 
and flush with the respective surfaces of the plates. 

(iii) Where the seam is welded from one side only, these provisions shall apply to the 
exposed of the surface weld. 


(0) Tests for Class | fusion welded seams shall comply with the requirements of the 
relevant regulations of Chapter -4. 


(c) Tests for Class Il fusion welded seams shall comply with the requirements of 
those of Chapter-/2, except that an additional provision for one micro and macro 
examination shall be made. 


(d) Tests for Class III fusion welded seams shall comply with the requirements of 


Chapter -72. 


(e) Class | and Class II shells shall be effectively stress-relieved by heat treatment 
when the wall thickness exceeds 20 mm or the carbon content exceeds 0.25% or the 
pipes are made of alloy steel.

286. Bronze screwed and socketed joints and mountings and fittings of bronze.— 

() Mountings and fittings of bronze up to 76 mm diameter may be attached directly to steel 
pipes by screwing, when the pressures and temperatures do not exceed 8.5 kg/cm? (g) and 
225°C respectively; where tapered threads are employed, such joints may be used for 
pressures not exceeding 7.6 kg/cm’ (g). 

(2) Bronze fittings above 76 mm diameter shall be of flanged construction. 


287. Reducing valve.—Where a reducing valve is installed in a pipe line, the pipe line and 
accessories on the low pressure side of the reducing valve shall be protected by a suitable 
safety valve or valves so adjusted as to permit the steam to escape as soon as the 
maximum allowable working pressure is exceeded or by a Suitable appliance for cutting off 
automatically the supply of steam as soon as the maximum allowable working pressure is 
exceeded.

289. Pipe work supports.— (l) All pipe work shall be adequately supported in order to 
permit free movement for expansion and contraction, and the amount of such movement 
shall be proportioned throughout the whole of any main by the provision of anchors at 
suitable points. 

(2) Where pipes may be subject to vertical movement, spring supports designed to carry the 
load under all conditions shall be provided. 

(3) Points of supports shall, as far as practicable, be arranged adjacent to the pipe joints. 

(4) Slings are in general preferable to roller supports and the latter shall be used only where 
necessary. 

(5) All pipe supports shall as far as practicable, be of mild steel and pipe anchors either of 
mild steel or cast steel. 


290. Drainage.— (|) (a) In the case of steam mains, attention shall be paid to the adequate 
provision of drainage points in the form of drain pockets. 

(b) Drainage points connected to stream-traps, shall be provided wherever water can collect 
under working conditions. 

(c) Hand drains shall be provided at all points at which water can collect in any portion of the 
steam main, by valve leakage or other means, when shut down, or when warning up prior to 
use. 


(2) Wherever practicable, a suitable gradient shall be provided in the pipe work to ensure 
the passage of condensed water in the direction of flow of steam towards the drainage 
points. 


[भाग ॥--खण्ड 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 877 


(3) It is recommended that a bypass shall be fitted at each steam trap. 


(4) Where the volume of water deposited is likely to be of serious proportions, separator 
shall be installed. 

(5) Each separator shall be furnished with a steam trap which shall be connected to it by 
means of a three-way cock, one end of which is connected to a manually operated 
drain. 


29.Freedom from rust and other foreign matter.—All pipes, valves and fittings shall be 
thoroughly cleaned as far as possible of rust and other foreign matter before erection and 
pipe lines shall be blown through with steam or air before being put into service. 


292. Test Pressures.—(l) Each completed pipe and fitting shall be tested by hydraulic 
pressure as per Chapter-2. 


(2) (a) Pipes and fittings with flanges for steam pressures exceeding 7 kg/cm? (g) shall be 
tested with blank flanges bolted or clamped on. 
(b) All other pipes, if straight, may be tested between the heads of an ordinary hydraulic 
pipes testing machine. 


(3) (a) The piping system shall, after erection, be subjected to a hydrostatic test pressure. 
(b) The hydrostatic test pressure at any point in the piping system shall not be less than 
.5 times the design pressure but shall not exceed the maximum allowable test pressure of 
any non-isolated components such as vessels, pumps or valves. 
(०) At no time during the hydrostatic tests, any part of the piping system shallbe subjected 
to a stress greater than 90 per cent of its yield strength (0.2 per cent off set) at test 
temperature. 


Notwithstanding anything contained in this sub-section, for boiler external piping and 
non-boiler external piping which are open to atmosphere such as vent and drain pipes, the 
hydraulic test for the portions of such pipes located beyond the last isolation valve may be 
dispensed with provided the weld joints in the pipe under reference are tested 00% by 
approved non-destructive examination and found satisfactory. 


(4) Special arrangement shall be made, according to circumstances, for testing bends and 
other fittings which are not flanged. 


(5) Hydraulic testing of butt welded and socket welded joints shall be conducted either at 
makers work or at user’s premises on completion of fabrication of pipes by the Inspecting 
Authority. 


(6) (a) Hydrostatic testing of fabricated pipes having attachments of flanges, fittings, butt joints, 
branch joints and weldolets shall be done at manufacturer's works or alternatively at site at 
.5 times the maximum allowable working pressure. 

(b) Where hydraulic testing of fabricated pipe joints is not carried out at manufacturer’s 
works, dye-penetrant test shall be carried out on the welded joints along with five per cent 
radiography of such joints.

(4)Provision shall be made for effective disconnection of all steam and hot water

(5)No blank flange or plug shall be inserted between a safety valve chest and the boiler 
generally and where it is permitted by the Competent Person, the blank flange or plug

hour and over, and using treated feed water to the satisfaction of the Competent Person. 


(7) For boilers used for electric power generation, the inspection shall be carried out as per 
the provisions of Appendix-H. 


(8) (a) For Waste Heat Boilers (Fired and Unfired) used exclusively in continuous process 
plants, the inspection shall be carried out as per the provisions of Appendix-l. 
(0) The boilers used in corrosive environment such as sulphuric acid plants shall not be 


covered under the provisions of Appendix-l. 


(9) In the case of forced flow and forced circulation types of boilers, proper circulation in 
every section of the circuit shall be ensured by the flow of water. 


296. Hydraulic test of boilers.— (व) Every boiler shall be hydraulically tested in the 
presence of an Inspector. 


(2) Boiler working at a pressureof 50 kg/cm? (g) or more, and used exclusively for electric 
power generation need not be hydraulically tested for issue of certificate every year, 
provided the inspection of such boiler is carried out as per the provisions of sub- 
regulation (7) of regulation 295. 


(3)Waste Heat Boilers (Fired and Unfired) used exclusively in continuous process plants 
need not be hydraulically tested for issue of certificate every year, provided the 
inspection of such boilers is carried out as per the provisions of sub-regulation (8) of 
regulation 295. 


297. Preparation for hydraulic tests.— () The chest of all mountings subject to steam 
pressure shall be in place and shut tight or blank flanged. 


(2) The safety valves shall be invariably removed and the chest opening blank flanged. 
(3) The attachment for the Competent Person’s pressure gauge shall be in order. 
(4) (a) All doors shall be properly jointed and tightened up. 


(0) The boiler shall be completely filled with waterwith care being taken to allow all air 
to escape and, if possible, a preliminary test not exceeding the design pressure of the 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


boiler shall be taken before the Competent Person’s visit, to test the tightness of the 
joints. 


(5) When a boiler is hydraulically tested for the first time, it shall be entirely cleared of 
lagging or brick work; at subsequent tests the lagging or brick work, or portions 
thereof, shall be removed, if required by the Competent Person, provided the 
Competent Person may, at his discretion, allow the lagging and brick work to remain 
in situ, in case of boilers where the covered parts have been fabricated and tested 
before erection in position. 


298. Procedure of hydraulic tests.— () (a) Subject to the provisions of sub-regulation 
()of regulation300, every sub-critical boiler shall be hydraulically tested after erection at site 
in presence of the Competent Person to 7.25 times the design pressure as certified by the 
Inspecting Authority in Form-|(Part-B) or Form-l(Part-C) as the case may be, to be stamped 
on the boiler, as free from any indication of weakness or defects and every Super critical 
boiler, with no fixed steam and waterline, having pressure parts designed for different 
pressure levels along the path of water-steam flow, shall be hydraulically tested after 
erection at site in presence of the Competent Person to a pressure of not less than .5 times 
the design pressure at the super heater outlet but not less than .25 times the design 
pressure of any part of the boiler as certified by the Inspecting Authority in Form-|(Part-B) or 
Form-|(Part-C) as the case may be, to be stamped on the boiler, as free from any indication 
of weakness or defects. 


(0) If all components of the boiler in the manufacturer’s premises have not been tested 
hydraulically as per regulation 67, the test, on completion, shall be taken to 7.5 times 
the design pressure. 


(c) The temperature of the water used as medium of pressure testing shall not be less 
than 20°C and greater than 50°C. 


(d) The test pressure shall be raised gradually under proper control at all times so that it 

never exceeds by more than 6% of the required pressure and maintained for 30 minutes 

whereupon the pressure shall be reduced to maximum allowable working pressure and 

maintained for sufficient time to permit close visual inspection for leakage of pressure 

parts. 

(e) The hydraulic test at site for the components meant for renovation or retrofit or 
spares shall be carried out at .25 times of the design pressure and these 
components need not be hydraulically tested at manufacturer's premises. 


(2) The boiler shall satisfactorily withstand such pressure without appreciable leakage or 
undue deflection or distortion of its parts for at least ten consecutive minutes. If the 
test if not satisfactory, the design pressure allowable by calculation shall be suitably 
reduced, unless the owner desires to make such alterations as will enable the boiler 
to withstand the hydraulic testsatisfactorily, in which case the boiler shall again be 
examined after the alterations have been made, the pressure recalculated, if 
necessary and the boiler tested to satisfaction of the Competent Person. 


882 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(3)At the first hydraulic test of a boiler prior to the issue of an original certificate,deflection 
measurements shall be made before, during and after test of each furnace length, fire- 
box and flat end or other plates. 


(4)After application of the hydraulic test, the Competent Person shall carefully examine 
the boiler inside and outside and satisfy himself that it has satisfactorily withstood the 
test. 


(5)(a) In caseany part of the boiler show undue deflection or indication of permanent set 
during the progress of the test, the pressure shall be released immediately such 
indications are observed. 

(0) The maximum allowable working pressure for the part shall be 40 per cent of the 
test pressure applied when the point of permanent set was reached. This procedure 
shall apply to any boiler at any test. 


(6)Hydraulic tests of boilers at subsequent examination shall be at .25 times the design 
pressure of the boiler. 


(7)When the internal construction or size of a boiler does not permit the Competent 
Person to get inside it for examining all its parts closely, he shall see it tested by 
hydraulic pressure to 7.5 times the design pressure at each inspection or the grant or 
renewal of a certificate. 


(8)Water tube locomotive type boilerand all tubular boilers shall be hydraulically tested at 
each inspection for the grant or renewal of a certificate, unless such test is waived 
under the orders of the Chief Inspector. 


(9)The Competent Person may if he considers it necessary, apply a hydraulic test to any 
boiler at any inspection. 


(0) Except in the case of vertical boilers having heating surface ofless than 
8.5m*portable and vehicular boilers, which do not require re-erection or building in 
brick work, the hydraulic tests of all boilers shall be conducted only after the erection of 
the boiler in situ and all boilers shall after re-erection in a position different from that in 
which were last examined by hydraulically tested. 


() A hydraulic test shall also be taken granting an increased pressure certificate and 
after repairing a boiler. However, in the case of minor repairs to the water tube boilers 
where non-destructive testing(NDT) has been carried out, hydraulic testing may be 
dispensed with provided non-destructive testing is carried out by an approved method. 


(2) When carrying out hydraulic test, Competent Person shall ensure that the pressure 
gauges have valid calibration. 


299. Steam tests.— (l) Every boiler before registration and every boiler of which the design 
pressure has been altered shall, before the issue of an original or renewal certificate for 
such boiler, be tested under steam to the satisfaction of the Inspector. Inspector shall send 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


883 


notice to the owner for the date fixed for the steam test and on completion of the test the 
Inspector shall enter all relevant details in the memorandum of inspection books. 


(2) At the time of test, the safety valves shall be left free and capable of being adjusted to the 
approved design pressure. 


(3) After adjustment of the valves to the correct blowing pressure, the boiler shall be tried 
under full steam and firing with the feed water shut off and the stop-valve closed, and the 
Inspector shall note the accumulation of pressure and other details of the test as 
accumulation of pressure and other details of the test as well as the loading and 
adjustment of the safety valves. 


(a) In the case of sub-critical water tube boiler or boilers fitted with super heater, the 


— 


feed water connection and stop valve need not be shut off and if the total valve 
area is lifted and found to be adequate by calculations, the requirement of the 
accumulation test may be assumed to have been satisfied if the valves are or 
have been found so adjusted that at least one safety valve on boiler shall be set 
at or below design pressure and remaining safety valves can be set up to three 
per-cent above the design pressure: 


Provided that all valves shall be lifted so that all steam which can be 
generated by the boiler can be discharged with a pressure rise not exceeding ten 
per-cent of the design pressure; 


In the case of super critical boiler or boilers, with no fixed steam and waterline, 
having pressure parts designed for different pressure levels along with the path of 
water-steam flow, safety valves shall be set up to ten per-cent above the 
maximum allowable working pressure: 


Provided that all the valves shall be lifted so that all steam which can be 
generated by the boiler can be discharged with a pressure rise not exceeding 
thirteen percent of the individual component maximum allowable working 
pressure, provided the boiler is having automatic burner management system 
and Master Fuel Trip (MFT) on main steam pressure. High lifting of safety valves 
can be tested by hydraulically actuated methods. 


(4) Before the safety valve test, the Inspector shall satisfy himself that the water gauges 
are in working order and that the feed apparatus is capable of supplying the boiler 
with sufficient water. 


(5) Where as per rules, a person-in-charge of a boiler holding certificate of competency 
is not required, the Inspector may, when he thinks fit, satisfy himself by questioning 
or by practical test, whether the person-in-charge of the boiler understands the use 
and purpose of the water gauges, the pressure gauge, the safety valves, the feed 
water-supply and blow down. 


884 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(6) When witnessing safety valves test, Inspector shall ensure that the pressure gauges 
have valid calibration. 


(7) No steam gauge shall be used without a syphon filled with water between it and the 
boiler. 


(8) When the accumulation of pressure at a steam test exceeds ten per cent of the 
design pressure the area of the safety valves shall be considered insufficient, and a 
certificate shall be refused until the safety valve area is increased. 


(9) An Inspector may, when visiting a factory for any purpose, verify the correctness of 
the safety valve and pressure gauge of any boiler under steam by comparison with 
his standard pressure gauge. 


*Note: A steam test is primarily intended for ascertaining that the safety valves are sufficient to relieve 
boilers effectively of excess steam and operate at the time when the maximum allowable working 
pressure is reached. 


300. Procedure for Registration— (l) On receipt of an application for registration under 
sub-section (/) of Section 2 of the Act, along with certificates and drawings as provided in 
regulation-8, the Inspector shall, when the boiler has been properly prepared for 
examination proceed to inspect it with a view to satisfy himself that the boiler has not 
suffered any damage during its transit from the place of manufacture to the site of erection 
and if he is satisfied with the correctness of the maker’s certificate and other particulars 
relating to the material and construction as mentioned under clause (c) of sub-section (4) of 
section 9 of the Act and regulation 7, take due account of the workmanship and details of 
the construction of each part; 


(2) Subject to any discretionary power exercised by the Chief Inspector, he may accept the

302. Measurement of Heating Surface.— (l) For the purpose of regulating the area of the 
safety valves and the amount of registration and inspection fees, the heating surface of a 
boiler shall be the total surface of all plates and tubes exposed to heat on one side and in 
contact with water on the other measured on the water side or the fire side, whichever is 
larger. 


(2) (a) For Lancashire and Cornish boilers, the total heating surface shall include the 
wetted surface of the furnaces between the end plates, the fire surface of cross tubes 
where fitted, and the part of the external shell below the side flue covers. In estimating the 
areas, furnaces shall be considered as plain cylinders andthe area of their wetted surface 
shall be taken as their mean external circumference X the length of the boiler between end 
plates. For the shell, the width of that part of the circumference below the flue covers shall 
be taken as = 2D, and this width multiplied by the length between end plates, shall be 
taken as the area of shell heating surface. 

(0) The part of the surface of the back end plate exposed to heat shall be omitted from 

the calculation. 


Example — The formula for the total heating surface of a Lancashire boiler having 
plain furnaces without cross tubes is as follows: -

Heating Surface in square meter = 2 L (3.44 6 + 0). “L” is the length of the boiler 
between end plates in meter, “d” is the mean external diameter of the furnaces in 
meter and “D” is the internal diameter of the largest belt of shell in meter. 


(3) (a) For steam and water drums of water tube boilers, the heating surface of the drum 
shall be taken as half the external mean circumference multiplied by the clear length of 
drum between the outer brick walls or centers of cross boxes, as the case may be. 

(0) The heating surface of the tubes shall be taken as the external surface of the tubes 

between the tube plates or heaters. 

(c) The heating surface of the heater shall be omitted from the calculation. 


(4) (a) For marine boilers of the fire-tube type, the heating surface shall include the 
wetted surface of the furnaces between the tube plates (considered in the same way as for 
Lancashire boilers), the wetted surface of the combustion chambers (less the area of the 
tube holes) and the wetted surface of the tubes between tube plates. 

(0) The parts of the front tube plate exposed to heat shall be omitted from the calculation. 


(5) (a) For locomotive type boilers, the heating surface shall include the wetted surface 
of the fire-box above the foundation ring (less the area of the tube holes and the fire hole 
and ring) and the wetted surface of the tubes between the tube plates. 

(0) The smoke box tube plate shall be omitted from the calculation. 


(6) For vertical boilers of ordinary type; the heating surface shall include the wetted 
surface of the fire-box above the foundation ring (less the area of fire hole and ring and 
tube holes if any) and the surface of any cross or other tubes and uptake below the lowest 
water level shown in the gauge glass.

306. Memorandum of Inspection Book .-- (l) A Memorandum of Inspection Book shall be 
prepared for each boiler in Form-Xland the Inspector shall enter all particulars in ink and 
dimensions of the boilers with the particulars of hydraulic test and steam test and his 
inspection notes in this book; 


(2) At subsequent inspection, Competent Person shall enter the dates of the Inspections, 
hydraulic tests and steam tests, when such are made with their notes thereon; 


(3) the Inspector or Competent Person, as the case may be, shall also enter in the 
Memorandum of Inspection Book, the general condition of the boiler and of repairs, to 
what extent boilers have been cleared of brick work, a report of all casual visits for 
inspection of repairs, for inspection of main steam pipes, and reports on accidents; 


(4) (a) On submission of the Memorandum Book to the Chief Inspector, he will in the 
case of newly registered boilers, check all particulars and calculations and approve 
the design pressure that is to be permitted. 

(b) In the case of old boilers, the Chief Inspector shall examine the Inspector’s notes 
of inspection and proposals made for repairs or reduction of pressure. 

(c) A pressure once approved for the boiler shall not be altered without the written 
authority of the Chief Inspector. 

(d)The Memorandum of Inspection Book shall be kept clean and up-to-date and the 
Inspection Book except when actually required by the Competent Person, shall be 
kept in the office of the Chief Inspector. 


307. Registration book.— () A registration book or copy of memorandum of inspection 
book containing all the particulars required for registration shall be maintained in the office 
of the Chief Inspector in Form-Xland any orders passed by him regarding the boiler shall 
be entered in the registration book under his initials. 


(2) The Chief Inspector shall also see that the note of subsequent inspections entered in 
the Memorandum of Inspection Book are copied in the Registration book. 


308. Maintenance of records.— (l) The Inspecting Authority shall maintain the records 
pertaining to the boiler or the economiser, as the case may be, including all the certificates 
provided in Form-|(Part-B), Form-|(Part-C),Form-IV(Part-A), Form-IV(Part-B), Form-IV(Part- 
C), Form-IV(Part-D), Form-V(Part-A) and Form-XVI and the copies of the approved drawings 
for a period of at least three years after registration of the boiler and thereafter these 
records may be sent to the owner of the boiler by the Inspecting Authority. 


(2) The owner of a boiler or economiser shall maintain the records pertaining to the boiler or 
economiser as the case may be, including the certificates provided in Form-l(Part-B), 
Form-|(Part-C), Form-IV(Part-B), Form-IV(Part-C), Form-V(Part-A), and Form-XV and 
the copies of the approved drawing for the entire life of the boiler or economiser as the 
case may be.

(3) In the event of any transfer of the ownership, the records mentioned above shall be

(4) The manufacturer of boiler or economiser or steam pipe shall maintain the record
