309. Transfer of memorandum of inspection book and registration book.—On transfer 
of a boiler from one state to another, the memorandum of inspection book and the 
registration book shall, on the request of Chief Inspector of the state to which the boiler has 
been transferred, be forwarded to that officer who shall take over their custody and maintain 
them. 


30. Grant of Certificate — (l) A certificate for the use of a boiler shall be granted in Form- 
XIl. 

(2) In the certificate, the design pressure at which the boiler shall be worked, the load to be 
placed on the safety valves or the thickness of the washers or ferrules required as safeguard 
against overloading and the date and pressure of the last hydraulic test of the boiler shall be 
entered. 

(3) The Inspector's remarks shall be as brief as possible. 


3i. Procedure for inspection of installed boilers.—() (a)It is essential to have every part 
of the boiler that is accessible, open and properly prepared for examination, internally and 
externally. 

(b)All boilers have openings through which an examination may be made and for which 
operation are closed; all such parts shall be opened whether for access to water surfaces, or 
heater surfaces. 

(c)In cooling a boiler down for inspection or repairs, the water should not be withdrawn until 
the setting is sufficiently cooled to avoid damage to the boiler and when possible allowed to 
cool down naturally. 

(d)It is not necessary, in order to comply with ordinary prudence, to remove insulation 
material, masonry, or fixed parts of the boiler, unless defects or deterioration peculiar to 
certain types of in accessible parts of boilers are suspected and where there is moisture or 
vapour showing through the covering should be removed at once and a complete 
investigation made. 

(e)Particular attention shall be paid to the external parts of boilers in the way of seating 
blocks, especially when the situation is damp. Saddle tanks and engine fittings of locomotive 
type boilers shall be removed to facilitate the inspection of the parts underneath at the first 
inspection, and at any reasonable period afterwards, if the Competent Person cannot 
otherwise satisfy himself as to the condition of those parts. 

(f)Upon sufficient visible evidence or suspicion due to age or other causes, every effort shall 
be made to discover the true condition, even to the removal of insulating material, masonry 
or fixed parts of a boiler. Sometimes drilling or cutting away of parts is justifiable and 
necessary to positively determine this condition. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


893 


(2) The Competent Person shall, whenever the size permits, go inside it and make a 


(4) 


(5) 


— 


thorough inspection of all its internal parts. Before doing so, he shall, satisfy himself that 
proper provision has been made for disconnecting the boiler from any other boiler under 
steam. In case he find that proper provision for disconnection has not been made or that 
the boiler has not been properly cleaned, or scaled, or that is unreasonably hot, he shall 
decline to proceed with the inspection and shall report the facts to the Inspecting 
Authority or Chief Inspector as the case may be,for orders. When a boiler is of such a 
size or its construction is such that the Competent Person cannot go inside it, there 
should be sufficient sight holes or hand holes provided to enable him to see the principal 
internal parts; if any important part of a boiler is so constructed that the Competent 
Person cannot examine it, he should report the facts to the Inspecting Authority or Chief 
Inspector as the case may be, for orders. 


In the case of forced circulation and forced flow boilers which are not accessible to close 
visual inspection, the Competent Person shall, besides thorough examination, ensure by 
the flow of water that proper circulation is maintained through all sections of the water 
circuits. 


(a)Upon entering a boiler, the Competent Person shall examine all surfaces of the 
exposed metal to observe the action caused by the use of water, oil scale solvents, or 
other substances which may have intentionally or unintentionally gone in with the feed 
water. Any evidence of oil is dangerous and immediate steps shall be taken to prevent 
any further entrance of oil into the boiler. 

(b)Oil or scale in the tubes of water-tube boilers or on plates over the fire of any boiler is 
particularly bad, often causing them to rupture. 


A given amount of corrosion along or immediately adjacent to a seam is more serious 
than a similar amount of corrosion in the solid plate away from the seams. Grooving 
along longitudinal seams is especially significant as grooving or cracks are likely to occur 
when the material is highly stressed. Severe corrosion is likely to occur at points where 
the circulation of the water is poor and such places shall be examined most carefully for 
evidences of corrosive action. 


If the Competent Person decides that a boiler in one or more of its parts is no longer fit 
for the pressure approved for it, he shall without delay report his proposal for reducing 
the pressure to the Chief Inspector and at the same time submit his calculation for the 
wasted parts for check and approval of pressure. 


(7) With regard to the pitting and wasting of shell plates, the Competent Person shall bear in 


mind that thickness of shell plates mayreduce to an appreciable extent and still be 
stronger than longitudinal seams. 


(8) (a)All flanging shall be thoroughly inspected and particularly the flanges of circular and 


plates that are not stayed. 

(b)Internal grooving in the fillet of such heads and external grooving in the outer surfaces 
of heads concave to pressure is very common since there is slight movement in the 
heads of this character which produces this kind of defect. Some types of boilers have 
what is known as the OG or reversed flange construction in some of their parts that may 
be inaccessible to the eye, but the condition shall be determined by the insertion of a 
mirror which at a proper angle will reflect back to the eye the condition of such a place, 
or any other feasible manner. 


894 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(9) (a)All stays, whether diagonal or through, shall be examined to note that they are in even 
tension. 
(0) All fastened ends shall be examined to note whether cracks exist where the stays are 
punched or drilled or rivets or bolts and, if not found in proper tension, the Competent 
Person shall recommend their proper adjustment. 


(0) (a)The manhole and other reinforcing plates, as well as nozzles or other connection 
flanged or screwed into a boiler, shall be examined internally as well as externally to see 
that they are not cracked or deformed, and wherever possible observation shall be made 
for the inside of the boiler, as to the thoroughness with which its pipe connections are 
made to the boiler. 

(b)All openings to external attachments, such as water column connections, openings in 
dry pipes and opening to safety valves, shall be noted to see that they are free from 
obstructions. 


(42)(a)Particular attention shall be given to the plate or tube surface exposed to the fire. The 
Competent Person shall observe whether any part of the boiler has become deformed 
during, operation by bulging or blistering; bulging is a distortion of the entire thickness of 
the plate or tube where it takes place, while the blistering is a lamination or separation of 
the plate due to foreign material being embedded in the ingot before the plate is rolled. 
(b)If bulges or blisters are of such size as would seriously weaken the plate or tube and 
especially when the leakage is noted coming from those defects, the boiler shall be 
discontinued from service until the defective part or parts have received proper repairs. 
(c)Careful observation shall be made to detect leakage from any portion of the boiler 
structures, particularly in the vicinity of seams and tube ends. 

(d)Fire tubes sometimes blister but rarely collapse, the Competent Person shall look 
through the tubes for such defects and if they are found with a sufficient degree of 
distortion they shall be removed. 


(2)(a)Lap joint boilers are apt to crack where the plates lap in the longitudinal or straight 
seam; if there is any evidence of leakage or other distress at this point, it shall be 
thoroughly investigated and, if necessary rivets removed or the plate slotted in order to 
determine whether cracks exist in the seam. Any cracks noted in shell plates are usually 
dangerous except fire cracks that run from the edge of the plate into the rivet holes of 
girth seams. 

(b)A limited number of such fire cracks is not usually a very serious matter. 


(43) The Competent Person shall test stay bolts by tapping one end of each bolt with a 
hammer and when practicable a hammer or other heavy tool shall be held on the 
opposite end to make the test more effective. 


(4) — (a) (i)Tubes in horizontal fire tube boilers deteriorate more rapidly at the ends toward 
the fire, and they shall be carefully tapped with a light hammer on their outer surface to 
ascertain whether there has been serious reduction in thickness. 

(ii) The tubes of vertical tubular boilers are more susceptible to deterioration at the upper 
open ends when exposed to the products of combustion without water protection. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 895 


(iii) They shall be reached as far as possible either through the hand holes if any, or 
inspected at the ends. 


(b) (i) The surfaces shall be carefully examined to detect bulges or cracks, or any 
evidences or defective welds. 

(ii)Where there is a strong draft, the tubes may become thinned by corrosion 

produced by the impingement or particles of fuel and ash, or the improper use of soot 

blowers. 

(iii)A leak from a tube frequently causes serious corrosive action on a number of 

tubes in its immediate vicinity. 


(c) (i)Where short tubes or nipples are employed in joining drums or headers, 
there is a tendency for waste products of the furnace to lodge in the junction points 
and such deposits are likely to cause corrosion if moisture is present. 

(ii)All such places shall be thoroughly cleaned and examined. 


(5)(i)The ligaments between tube holes in the heads of all types of fire-tube boilers and in 
shells of water-tube boilers shall be examined. 
(ii)If leakage is noted, it may denote a broken ligament. 


(46) Steam pockets on surfaces are sometimes found in new or replacement work, and 
wherever, this is possible or likely, the Competent Person shall make observation and, if 
any are found, recommend the necessary changes. 


(7)(a)(i)The steam and water pipes, including connections to the water column, shall be 
examined for leaks, and if any are found, it shall be determined whether they are the 
result of excessive strains due to expansion and contraction, or other causes. 

(ii) The general arrangement of the piping in regard to the provisions, for expansion and 
drainage, as well as adequate support at the proper points, shall be carefully noted. 

(iii) The location of the various stop valves shall be observed to see that water will not be 
pocketed when the valves are closed and thereby establish cause for water-hammer 
action. 


(o)The arrangement of connections between individual boilers and the main steam pipes 
shall be especially noted to see that any change of position of the boiler due to setting or 
other causes, will not produce an undue strain on the piping. 


(c) It shall be ascertained whether all pipe connections to the boiler possess the proper 
strength in their fastenings, whether tapped into the boiler, a fitting, or flange riveted to 
the boiler. 


(d)(i)The Competent Person shall determine whether there is provision for the 
expansion and contraction of such piping, and that there is no undue vibration tending to 
crystalize the parts subjected to it. 

(ii) This includes all steam and water pipe and special attention shall be given to the blow 
off pipes with their connections and fittings, because the expansion and contraction due 
to rapid change in temperature and water-hammer action create a great strain upon the 
entire blow off system, which is more pronounced when a number of blow off pipes are 
joined in one common discharge. 


896 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(iii) The freedom of the blow off connection on each boiler shall be tested whenever 
possible by opening the valve for a few seconds, at which time it can be determined 
whether there is excessive vibration. Blow off pipes should be free from external 
dampness to prevent corrosion. 


(8)(a)(i)The piping to the water column shall be carefully noted to see that there is no 
chance of water being pocketed in the piping forming the steam connection to the water 
column. The steam-pipe shall preferably drain towards to the water column. 

(ii) The water pipe connection to the water column must drain towards the boiler. 


(0) (i) The relative position of the water column to the fire surfaces of the boiler shall be 
observed to determine whether the column is placed in accordance with the regulations. 
The attachments shall be examined to determine their operating condition. 


(9)(a)In Water-Tube boilers, it shall be noted, as far as possible, whether or not the proper 
baffling is in place. 
(0) In many types of boilers, the absence of baffling often causes high temperatures on 
portions of the boiler structure which are not intended to be exposed to such 
temperatures, from which a dangerous condition may result. The location of combustion 
arches with respect to tube surfaces shall be carefully noted. These are sometimes 
arranged so as to cause the flame to impinge on a particular part of a boiler and 
produces overheating of the material and consequent danger of the rupture of the part. 


(20) Localisation of heat brought about by improper or defective burner or stoker installation 
or operation creating a blow pipe effect upon the boiler, shall be condemned. 


(2)Where boilers are suspended, the supports and setting shall be carefully examined 
specially at points where the boiler structure comes near the setting walls or floor. Often 
accumulation of ash and soot will bind the boiler structure at such points and produce 
excessive strains on the structure owing to the expansion of the parts under operating 
conditions. 


(22)(a) As the safety valves are the most important attachments on the boiler, they shall be 
inspected with the utmost caution. There shall be no accumulations of rust, scale, or 
other foreign substances located in the casings so as to interfere with the free operation 
of valves. The setting and freedom of the safety valves shall be tested preferably by 
raising the steam pressure to the blow-in-off point, or if this cannot be done, the valves 
shall be tested by means of the try levers to ascertain if they are free. Where the steam 
discharged from a safety valve is led through a pipe the Competent Person shall 
determine at the time the valve is operating whether or not the drain, opening in the 
discharge pipe is free and in accordance with the Regulations. 


(b)If the Competent Person deems it necessary, in order to determine the freedom of 
discharge from a safety valve, the discharge connections shall be removed. Under no 
circumstances a stop valveshall be permitted between a boiler and its safety valve. 


(23)The steam gauges on all boilers shall be removed and the Competent Person shall test 
them and compare their readings with a standard test gauge. The readings of the steam 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 897 


gauges shall be observed and compared when making an inspection with steam on the 
boiler, where several boilers are in service connected to a common steam main. The 
location of the steam gauges shall be noted to see whether or not it is exposed to high 
temperature either externally, as would be the case if placed close to the smoke flue or 
other high heated part of the boiler or setting, or exposed to heat internally due to lack of 
protection of the gauge spring with a proper syphon or trap to prevent steam from 
coming in contact with the spring. The Competent Person shall see that the provisions 
are made for blowing out the pipe leading to the steam gauge. 


32. Calculation of wasted shell. —(7)When any part is wasted and the Competent Person 
is doubtful of its fitness for the pressure, he shall cause one or more small holes to be bored 
and from them ascertain the average thickness of the parts from which he can satisfy himself 
by calculation, in accordance with the formula applicable to the part.He shall enter such 
gauging and calculations in the Memorandum of Inspection Book. 


(2) In making calculations for a wasted part of a boiler shell, e.g., along the line of 
seating blocks of a Lancashire boiler, the Competent Person shall use the following 


formula:

36. Repairs to boiler and steam pipes.—(l) Major repairs or replacements such as 
tubes, coils, headers, drums, fusion welded patches to shells, fireboxes and end plates of 
boilers and extensive building up of wasted parts of boilers permitted under these 
regulations, the renewal of furnaces and end plates, parts of shell, fireboxes, girders and 
steam-pipes, etc., shall only be entrusted to a firm who is recognised as a repairer under 
these regulations. 


(2) Any firm seeking recognition shall apply in ‘Form-XIIl'to the Chief Inspector of Boilers of 
the State in which the recognition is sought along with the fee specified in table 8/9. 


(3) A firm seeking recognition as a repairer shall meet the following requirements depending 
upon the class of boilers, namely: — 


(a) For Class | boiler repairer, the owner of the firm himself shall have a degree in 
mechanical or Production or Power Plant or Metallurgical engineering or the firm 
shall have on its rolls a permanently employed engineer having a degree in 
mechanical or Production or Power Plant or Metallurgical engineering and the 
said owner or the permanently employed engineer shall also have an experience 
of at least five years in an organisation engaged in fabrication, erection, repair or 
maintenance and quality control of boilers; and the firm shall also have qualified 
and permanently employed welders as per the provisions of these regulations; 


(b) For Class II boiler repairer,the owner of the firm himself shall have a diploma in 
mechanical engineering or the firm shall have on its rolls a permanently 
employed engineer having a diploma in mechanical engineering and the said 
owner or the permanently employed engineer shall also have an experience of at 
least three years in an organisation engaged in fabrication, erection, repair or 
maintenance and quality control of boilers; and the firm shall also have qualified 
and permanently employed welders as per the provisions of these regulations; 


(c) For Class Ill boiler repairer, the owner of the firm himself or a person permanently 
employed with the firm shall have a minimum three years’ experience in repair, 
maintenance, operation, erection or inspection of boiler and the firm shall also 
have qualified and permanently employed welders as per the provisions of these 
regulations; 


(d) For Special class boiler repairer, the owner of the firm himself shall have a 
degree in mechanical or welding engineering along with specialised experience 
in welding technology for a minimum period of three years or the firm shall have 
on its rolls a permanently employed engineer having a degree in mechanical or 
welding engineering along with specialised experience in welding technology for 
a minimum period of three years, and have permanently employed welders as 
per the provisions of these regulations who should also have valid certificate for 
carrying out Tungsten Inert Gas welding; 


(e)(i) Where the power stations, fertilizer plants, chemical and petrochemical plants or 
refineries apply for repair of their own boilers, they shall have al (i) Where the power 
stations, fertilizer plants, chemical and petrochemical plants or refineries apply for repair 
of their own boilers, they shall have all the facilities in-house and may apply to the Chief 


904 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


Inspector of Boilers of the State for permission to repair their own boilers in accordance 
with these regulations; 


(ii) On receipt of the application for permission to repair to a boiler, the Chief 
Inspector of Boilers of the State shall reply to the request within a period of 
two days of the receipt of the application. 


(4) The Chief Inspector shall scrutinise and evaluate the application along with the 
replies to the questionnaire and after satisfying himself that the following 
requirements are fulfilled, shall recognise the firm as a repairer within a period of 
thirty days, in the category applied for, namely: — 


(a) that the firm possesses rectifier or generator, grinder, general tools and 
tackles, dye-penetrant kit, expander and measuring instruments; 


(0) that the electric arc or oxy-acetylene welding sets and all other tools and plant 
in his possession for carrying out repairs are suitable for the work undertaken; 


(c) that the quality of material used conforms to the specifications prescribed in 
these regulations; 


(d)that the supervisory and operational staff employed by the firm possesses the 
necessary training and experience for the work undertaken; 


(e) that all welders employed by the firm possess certificates issued as required 
under Chapter-3 of these regulations; 


(f) Standard of work should be of high order and comply with all the 
requirements and test that may be specified by the Chief Inspector. 


(5) The recognition of the firm as a repairer shall be for a period of two years and 
thereafter it shall apply for renewal of its recognition at least two months before the 
expiry of said period. 


(6) A repairer recognised in one State shall be eligible to work in any other State by 
getting his recognition endorsed from the Chief Inspector or Director of Boilers of the 
concerned State on making payment of fee as prescribed in this regulation. 


(7) In case the repairer is found indulging in violating the provisions of the Act or 
regulations, the firm shall be blacklisted under intimation to Chief Inspector or 
Director of Boilers of all the States and Union territories and Secretary, Central 
Boilers Board, and renewal shall not be done in any case.

37. Procedure for repairs.—()The repair work shall be carried out under the supervision 
of Inspector or Competent Person and when the fireboxes and smoke tubes of locomotive 
tube boilers are withdrawn, the internal parts, which are otherwise inaccessible to close 
inspection, shall be inspected by the Inspector or Competent Person, as the case may be. 


(2) Repair to boilers shells shall be carried out by patching or by removing a strip of worn or 
damaged plate and inserting the new strip with covering straps over the longitudinal butt 
ends, the strength of the riveted joints shall be not less than that of the longitudinal joints 
of the shell. 


(3)(a) Patches for fire exposed plates shall be fitted metal to metal without joint of any 
description; 


(b) The affected part shall be cut out, leaving the corners of the hole well-rounded. 
(c) Patches shall be secured, wherever possible, properly spaced rivets with a width of 
plate at least equal to the diameter of rivet between the edge of the rivet hole and the 


edge of the plate. 


(d) Where riveting is impracticable, the plate shall be secured by welt fitting countersunk 
headed screw pins. 


(4) The thickness of a patch plate shall not be less than the original thickness of the plate 
which it is used to patch. 


(5)Bulged or distorted furnaces or circular section may, if the bulge or distortion is not too 
great, be pressed back to shape. 


(6)Circular furnaces of horizontal boilers that have become distorted may be suitably 
reinforced. 


906 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(7)(a) Anti-collapse rings shall be substantial section either of single or double angles 
bolted back to back with screw stays not less than 22 mm in diameter and about 78 
mm in pitch passed though flat of angle and screwed into the furnace, the ends being 
rounded over on the fire side and fitted with nuts at the other. 


(0) The stay bolts shall be fitted with ferrules not less than 25 mm in depth between 
furnace and angle ring. 


(8) Welding shall not be accepted for the repair of any part of a boiler for which welding is 
forbidden for a new boiler under these regulations and boiler shells shall not be repaired 
by welding beyond the filling up of a small isolated corroded or pitted part or the making 
up of wasted edges of openings. 


(9) Cracks or grooving in dished or flat end plates of cylindrical shells or in the bends of 
furnace flanges in a circumferential direction may be weed out and welded. 


(0) Wasted parts of circular furnaces and fireboxes and fire exposed flat plates as in 
rectangular fireboxes and combustion chambers may be cut out and be replaced by new 
pieces welded in or they may be built-up by welding. 


() Longitudinal cracks in circular furnaces and fireboxes and cracks in rectangular 
fireboxes and combustion chambers may be welded. 


(72) No stay bar shall be welded. 


(3) Smoke tubes may be butt-welded either by fusion welding, flush welding or oxy- 
acetylene welding, and these may be tested hydraulically at the discretion of the 
Inspecting Authority. 


3i8. Procedure for welding during repairs. The repairer shall satisfy the inspecting 
Authority :- 


() That the electric arc or oxy-acetylene welding sets and all other tools and 
plant in his possession for carrying out repairs are suitable for the work 
undertaken. 


(2) That the quality of material used conforms to the specification that are 
prescribed. 


(3) That the supervisory and operational staff employed by him possess the 
necessary training and experience for the work under taken. 


(4) That all welders employed by him possess certificates issued as required 
under Chapter-3 of these Regulations. 

(5) Standard of work shall be of high order and comply with all the 
requirements and test that may be prescribed by the Chief Inspector. 


39. Riveting and other repairs.—The repairer shall satisfy the Chief Inspector:-

(!) That he possesses the necessary equipment and tools and engages trained 
and experienced workmen and staff for the work underwork taken. 


(2) Standard of work shall be of a high order and comply with all the

material used shall be boiler quality. 


320. Miscellaneous provisions for repairs.— () (a)Therepairs shall be supervised, so 
far as his other duties permit by the Competent Person. 
(b) When the fire boxes and smoke tubes of locomotive tube boilers are withdrawn, the 
opportunity shall be taken to inspect the internal parts which are otherwise 
inaccessible to close inspection. 


(2) Repairs to boiler shells shall be effected either by patching or by removing a strips of 
worn or damaged plate and inserting the new strip with covering straps over the 
longitudinal butt ends, the strength of the riveted joints shallbenot less than that of the 
longitudinal joints of the shell. 


(3) (a) Patches for fire exposed plates shall be fitted metal to metal without joint of any 

description. The affected part shall be cut out, leaving the corners of the hole 
rounded. 
(b)Patches shall be secured, wherever possible, properly spaced rivets with a width 
of plate at least equal to the diameter or rivet between the edge of the rivet hole and 
the edge of the plate. (c)Where riveting is impracticable, the plate shall be secured 
by welt fitting countersunk headed screw pins. 


(4) The thickness of a patch plate shall not be less than the original thickness of the 
plate which it is used to patch. 


(5) Bulged or distorted furnaces of circular section may, if the bulge of distortion is not 
too great, be pressed back to shape. 


(6) Circular furnaces horizontal boilers that have become distorted may be suitably 
reinforced. 


(7) Anti-collapse rings shall be of substantial section either of single or double angles 
bolted back to back with screw stays not less than 22 mm in diameter and about 78 
mm in pitch passes through flat of angle and screwed into the furnace, the ends 
being rounded over on the fire side and fitted with nuts at the other. The stay bolts 
shall be fitted with ferrules not less than 25 mm in depth between furnace and angle 
ring. 


(8) Welding shall not be accepted for the repairs of any part of a boiler for which welding 
is forbidden for a new boiler under these Regulations. Boiler shells shall not be 
repaired by welding beyond the filling up of a small isolated corroded or pitted or the 
making up of wasted edges of openings. 


908 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(9) Cracks or grooving in dished or flat end plate of cylindrical shells or in the bends of 
furnace flanges in circumferential direction may be weed out and welded. 


(0) Wasted parts of circular furnaces and fire boxes and fire exposed flat plates 
as in rectangular fire boxes and combustion chambers may be cut out and be 
replaced by new pieces welded in or they may be built up by welding. Longitudinal 
cracks in circular furnaces and fire-boxes and cracks in rectangular fire-boxes and 
combustion chambers may be welded. 


(7) No Stay bar shall be welded. 


(2) For the purposes of these Regulations renewed part shall be deemed to be 
parts of a new boiler intended for use at the pressure at which the boiler under 
renewal is used. 


(3)ForButt Welding of Smoke Tubes,Smoke tubes may be butt welded either by fusion

32.Submission of manufacturing drawings and the particulars of boilers in 
advance.— (|) In the case of land boilers and boiler components including spares made in 
India for use in the States, the manufacturing drawings and the particulars of materials, 
design and construction of boilers shall be submitted by the makers of the boilers or boiler 
components or spares, as the case may be to the Inspecting Authority of the State, where 
the principal parts of the boilers will be manufactured, for examination and approval before 
commencement of the manufacture of boilers. 


(2) In the case of boilers and boiler components including spares made outside India for 
use in the State, the manufacturing drawings and particulars of the material, design and 
construction, of boilers shall be submitted initially to the Inspecting Authority in the 
country of manufacture for examination and approval. 


(3) The manufacturing drawings and the particulars of materials, design and construction in 
the case of fired boilers of steam generating capacity 00 Tons/hour and above and that 
of Waste heat boiler of 20 Tons/hour and above including boiler components and spares 
thereof shall then be submitted to the Technical Adviser (Boilers) for selection of latest 
materials with high strengths and use in high temperature and pressure, for the safety. 
Thereafter, the manufacturing drawings and the particulars of materials, design and 
construction approved by the Inspecting Authority shall be sent to the Chief Inspector of 
Boilers of the State where the boiler will be installed and used, for final examination and 
approval before commencement of manufacture so as to avoid questions arising at the 
time of erection and registration of the boiler. 


(4) The manufacturing drawings and the particulars of materials, design and construction in 
the case of fired boilers of steam generating capacity less than 00 Tons/hour and that 
of Waste heat boiler of less than 20 Tons/hour including boiler components and spares 
thereof approved by the Inspecting Authority shall be submitted to the Chief Inspector of 
Boilers of the State where the boiler will be installed and used, for final examination and

322. Inspection of pipes.— () Pipes shall be inspected and hydraulically tested before 
use in place, in test pressure to be that prescribed in the standard conditions for steam 
pipes. A certificate from the Inspecting Authority in Form-|lV(Part-B), stating that this has 
been done by him may be accepted. If the Competent Person is satisfied with the test, the 
pipes may be erected in position. The Chief Inspector shall intimate his approval to the 
owner regarding the suitability of the pipe line for use at the pressure and temperature to be 
specified. 


(2)At subsequent inspection of the boiler or at any other time, the Competent Person may 
make an external inspection of the steam-pipes and for this purpose may require a part of 
the lagging at the flanges to be removed, and the pipe made bare. If as a result of this 
inspection the Competent Person is of opinion that the pipes or any positions of then are 
in an unsatisfactory condition he shall report the matter to the Chief Inspector, who may 
require the whole of the lagging to be removed and may require any pipe or pipes to be 
hydraulically tested. The test pressure at such hydraulic test shall be not less than one 
and half times, the design pressure of the boiler or the maximum allowable working 
pressure of pipe as the case may be. 


(3)(a) A memorandum of Inspection Book shall be prepared in respect of steam pipe and 
fittings in Form-XIV. In this book, the Inspector shall enter in ink, all particulars and 
dimensions of the steam pipe and fitting with calculations for the various parts in detail, 
particulars of hydraulic test and his inspection notes. 


(b) At subsequent inspection, the Competent Person shall enter the date of the 
inspection and hydraulic test together with notes thereon. 


(c) The Competent Person shall also enter in the Memorandum of Inspection Book 
remarks regarding the general condition of the steam pipes and fittings, and repairs, 
replacements of alterations, if any, and the extent to which the steam pipes have 
been cleaned of lagging and covering so that the book provides a useful record of the 
steam-pipes and fittings for the information and guidance of Competent Person at subsequent 
inspection. 


(d) In the event of an accident to a pipe line or its fittings, necessary remarks shall also 
be entered in the book. 


(e) The Memorandum Book shall be submitted to the Chief Inspector, who will check all 
particulars and calculations and approve the maximum allowable working pressure 
and temperature that are to be permitted for the various parts of the pipe line and 
fittings. The pressure and temperature once approved for the particular steam pipe 
line shall not be altered except on a written authority from the Chief Inspector. 


323. Submission of plans of steam-pipes.— (l) Plans of steam pipes including mountings 
and fittings shall be submitted with the prescribed fee to the Inspecting Authority before 
construction and to the Chief Inspector at the time of registration of the boiler for his decision 
whether the pipes and their arrangement comply with the regulations.

327. Fees for inspection of components of valves——The fees for inspection of 
components of valves shall be charged as under: 


() 50% of the inspection fees of the valves shall be charged by the chief inspector of the 


state where the components of the valves, are manufactured, for inspection of the 
components manufactured in a State other than the State where the valves are 
assembled and remaining 50% of the inspection fees shall be charged by the chief 
inspector of the state, where the valves are assembled, for inspection of assembled, 
and final inspection of the valves. 


(2) Where the inspection, so far as the material testing is concerned, has been carried 


out by a “well Known Foundry” or “Well Known Forge” full inspection fees shall be 
charged by the chief inspector of the state where the valves have been assembled 
and finally tested. 


Where the components of the valves are inspected and tested in the same 
manufacturing work where the valves are assembled and finally tested, full inspection 
fees shall be charged by the chief inspector of the state where the manufacturing 
work is located. 


In case, in a state, components are manufactured by one firm and finally fitting and 
assembly of the valves are made by another, both the firms shall pay inspection fees 
on 50: 50 basis.

CHAPTER-9 


SAFETY OF PERSONS INSIDE BOILERS 


333.Safety of persons working inside boilers— (l) The owner or person in 


charge shall not compel or allow any person to go inside a steam boiler for 
any purpose whatsoever unless the boiler is effectively disconnected from 
any steam or hot water communication with any other boiler,in the manner 
provided in this regulation. 


(a) Effective disconnection shall be made either by the removal of the boiler 
stop valve or of a length of piping from all steam and hot water connection 
with any other boiler, vessel or pipe containing steam or hot water by the 
insertion of substantial blank flanges between the boiler stop valves and 
piping. 

(0) The shutting of a stop valve, stop cock or automatic isolating valve shall 
not be deemed to compliance with this regulation. 

(c) In the case of welded pipe work, however, if a vent pipe of not less than 
50 mm internal diameter (bore) is fitted between the main stop valve and the 
intermediate stop valve on the steam main and between the feed check 
valve and intermediate check valve on the feed line, this regulation shall be 
considered to have been complied with, provided such vent pipes are fitted 
with bolted-on blank flanges and the flanges are removed so as to effectively 
discharge any leakage steam or water to the atmosphere which the valves 
on either side of it have been closed. 


(3)The owner of a boiler to which this regulation is applicable shall obtain the 


(4) 


approval of the Chief Inspector in writing to the method of disconnection 
which he proposes to use and shall be responsible for ensuring that the 
method so approved is followed in practice. 


When electric light is used for work inside a boiler shell or drum or any 
confined space within a boiler, the voltage shall not exceed 24 volts and the 
owner of the boiler shall provide a hand lamp with lamp-guard, keyless 
socket, insulated handle and extension cord of approved type. 


Where power is used for working any equipment inside a boiler the metallic 
portion of the equipment shall be effectively earthed.

CHAPTER-0 
ELECTRODE BOILERS 


PART-4 


334. Application.—This Chapter applies to electrode steam boilers for all voltages for any 
working pressure and for temperatures not exceeding 343°C and electrode boilers shall only 
be of the following construction: 


(a) Fusion welded steel boilers; 
(0) Seamless shell steel boilers. 


335. General requirements.—Wherever applicable, the provisions of Chapter-| relating to 
certificates from makers, Inspecting Authorities etc., and of Chapter-3 relating to construction 
shall be followed. 


336. Materials—The material specifications for structural parts of electrode boilers shall 
comply with Chapter-2, as regards the process of manufacture, chemical composition, mode 
of manufacture and test, and the certificates for the steel plates, provided that the ultimate 
tensile stress and elongation of materials shall be between the following limits: - 


(a) For fusion welded construction, as mentioned in Chapter-2. 


(0) For seamless construction as mentioned in regulation 250 and for seamless carbon 
steel pipes as mentioned in Table 7/3 of regulation 253.

PART-3 
TESTS FOR CLASS | FUSION WELDED SEAMS 


338. Selection of test pieces.—(l) From the test plate of plates on each longitudinal seam, 
test pieces shall be selected for the following test, the specimens being cut out as shown in 
Fig. 0/7 of this regulation and stamped by the Competent Person for identification: 

(a) One Tensile test specimen for the welded seam; 

(b) Two bend test specimens; 

(c) One nick break test specimen 


(2) The remainder of each set of test plates shall be retained for any retest required and 
any specimen for retest shall be cut from the same set of test plates as the original 
specimen.

(3) Surface of tensile and bend specimens corresponding with the outside and inside 
of the shell shall be only lightly dressed so that the rolled surface of the parent metal is not 
wholly removed, except that where the rolled surfaces of the abutting plates are not level 
with one another, one plate may be machined at each face of the weld provided the depth of 
metal removed does not exceed 0.8 mm. 


339. Tensile Test.— (a) The specimen shall be cut out transversely to the welded seam (see 
Fig. 0/7 of regulation 338) and shall be of the full thickness of the plate at the welded seam 
and the breadth “W” shall be as large as the testing machine will reasonably allow, provided 
the effective cross-sectional areas is not less than 322.5 sq.mm (see Fig. 0/8 below). 


(0) The ultimate tensile stress of the welded seam specimen shall be not less than the lower 
limit specified for the plate (see under regulation 37).

340. Bend Test.— (|) (a) Two bend tests shall be made for welded seams. 


(0) One specimen shall be tested with the outer surface or the weld in tension, and the other 
with the inner surface in tension. 


(c) The specimen shall be rectangular in section and shall be cut out transversely to the weld 
so as to have a width of not less than %% times the thickness of the plate. 


(d) The sharp corners of the specimens shall be rounded to a radius not exceeding ten 
percent of the thickness of the specimen. 


(2) (a) Where the plate thickness does not exceed 32 mm, the thickness of the 
specimen shall be equal to the full thickness of the test plate. 


(0) Where the plate thickness exceeds 32 mm, the thickness of the specimen shall 
be at least 32 mm. 


(c) The specimen to be tested with the outer surface of the weld in tension shall be 
prepared by cutting to waste the metal local to the inner surface of the weld, so that the 
desired specimen thickness is obtained. 


(3) (a) The specimen to be tested with the inner surface in tension shall be prepared 
by cutting to waste the metal local to the outer surface of the weld so that the desired metal 
thickness is obtained. 


(0) Where the thickness of the plate permits, both specimen being located in the 
plate one above the other. 


(c) Each specimen shall be mounted with the weld midway between the support, set 
apart at a distance of not more than 5.2 times the thickness of the specimen and pushed 
through the supports with a former having a diameter equal to three times the thickness of 
the specimen (see Fig. 4/6 of regulation 60 of chapter 4). 


922 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(4) (a) On completion of the test, no crack or defect at the outer surface of the 
specimen shall be greater than 7.5 mm, measured across the specimen or 3 mm measured 
along the length of the specimen. 


(0) Premature failure at corners of the specimen shall not be considered cause for 
rejection (see Fig. 4/6, specimen A). 


३34. Nick Break Test— (a) The specimen shall be rectangular in section and cut 
transversely to the well so as to have a width not less than one-half times its thickness. 


(0) The slot shall be cut in one side of the specimen through the center of the weld and 
perpendicular to the outer face of the vessel. 


(c) The specimen shall then be broken in the weld and the fracture shall reveal a sound 
homogeneous-weld, substantially free from slag inclusions, porosity and coarse crystallinity. 


342. Retests— In caseany of the tests fail, two retests shall be made on specimens cut 
from the same plate and both retests shall meet the specified requirements. 


343. Specimens after Tests.—lf required by the inspecting Authority, the specimens after 
test shall be forwarded for examination.

treatment and the heat heat-treatment shall be in accordance with regulation 23.

STANDARD CONDITIONS FOR THE DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION OF 
ECONOMISERS, FEED PIPES, FEED HEATERS AND OTHER SIMILAR

PART-4 


ECONOMISERS 
357. Application of standard condition and exceptions thereto.— (l) An economiser 
shall not be registered under sub-section (5) of section 72 of the Act and a certificate shall 
not be issued under sub-section (6) of that section with reference to an economiser unless 
the standard conditions in respect of material design and construction, which are specified in 
this chapter are satisfied in respect of such economiser. 


(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub regulation (), the chief Inspector may, 
subject to the provisions of regulation 359, register an economiser and order the issue of a 
certificate authorising the use thereof, although the standard conditions are not fully satisfied 
in respect of such economiser. 


358. General requirements.— (l) All cast iron and steel headers and parts used in the 
assembly of an economiser shall conform to the requirements of this Chapter in respect of 
material specification and test workmanship and structural requirements. 


(2) All economisers shall beconstructed under the supervision of an Inspecting Authority 
and shall be so certified by that authority. 


(3) A certificate from the Inspection Authority in Form--XV_ certifying that material was 
tested and the economizers built under their supervision shall be furnished to the 
chief inspector before or with the first application for registration. 


(4) In advance or along with application for registration, the following shall be furnished:- 
(a) A certificate of manufacture and test in Form-XVIsigned by the maker or by a 
responsible representative of the Maker, containing the description of the 
economiser, particulars of the materials used in its construction and the dimensions 
of the several parts with the declaration that the limits oftensile breaking strength 

and tests comply with the standard conditions. 
(b) A certificate from the maker of the material stating the tensile breaking strength and 


the elongation provided that if the maker and manufacturer be the same, the 
manufacturer's precise statements showing the above information shall be 
accepted. 
(5) To suit owners’ convenience, wherever possible it is recommended that economiser 
be installed in two or more sections. 


359. Modification of formula—Where no certificate is produced, the maximum allowable 
working pressure as found by formula will be reduced by 0%. However, when the 
workmanship is doubtful in any way and the chief Inspector is not satisfied that any of the 


930 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


foregoing conditions would be sufficient to meet the circumstances, he may at his discretion 
reduce the maximum allowable working pressure by such percentage as he deems fit. 


360. Maker’s certificate for steel economisers.—The maker shall furnish a certificate to 
the Competent Person in the following form: 


We hereby certify that the material described below has been made by the Open Hearth 
or an Electric process acid/basic and has been satisfactorily tested in the presence of 
the Competent Person in accordance with the standard Tests.

(3) Maximum allowable working pressure shall be the highest pressure at which the 
economiser relief valves are to be set. 


(4) The above test pressure shall be held for a minimum period of ten minutes. 


362. Workmanship and manufacture.—All materials used in the construction of pressure 
parts shall be tested and shall conform to the following requirements:- 


(i) The workmanship shall be of highest standard. All castings shall be well finished, free 
from defects, porous places and blow holes, and true to dimensions without warping. 


[भाग ॥--खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


Where chaplets are used, there shall be satisfactory fusion with the metal and 
chaplets shall be properly tinned with metalfree from lead. 


(ii) The screw threads of all bolts shall be of whitworth forms. 


(iii) Wherevernecessary,all component parts shall be manufactured to limit gauges to 
secure interchangeability throughout.

368. Joint bolts and studs for cast iron economisers.—(i) The maximum allowable

(2) The use of studs tapped into cast iron shall be permissible where;

369. Economiser water outlet temperature.—The design condition shall be such that the 
maximum outlet water temperature of the economiser shall be at least 22°C below the 
saturated steam temperature in the boiler drum: 


Provided that this requirement shall not apply to economizers used on low pressure 
water heating system working at pressure less than 36.5 m head of water.

370. Construction offubes.— () The tubes shall be manufactured as perregulation 722. 

(2)Suitable provision shall be made for supporting horizontal tubes at one or more interval 
in their length to relieve bending stresses and these supports as well as the end connections 
shall permit free expansion.

37. Maximum allowable working pressureof tubes.—The maximum allowable working 


pressure of the tubes shall be calculated as per sub-regulation (/) of regulation 244, but the 
working metal temperature shall be taken as the maximum water temperature for which the 
part of the elements is designed plus °C. 


372.Construction ofheaders.—(i)The headers shall be constructed in accordance with 
regulation 25. 
(2) Branches shall be secured by one of the following methods, namely: - 


(a) Expanded, belled and welded. 

(0) Strength welded with additional securing means. 

(c) Full depth strength weld. 

(d) Branches less than 5 mm bore may be screwed and seal welded. 


(3) Open ends of forged seamless steel tube headers may be closed by forging, or the 
ends may be secured by bolting, screwing, or welding in an approved manner. 


373. Maximum allowable working pressure of headers.—()The maximum allowable 
working pressure of rectangular headers shall be calculated as per regulation 246. 


(2) The maximum allowable working pressure of cylindrical headersshall be calculated 
as per regulations 69 and 70. 


374. Attachment of tubes to headers.—(i)Tubes shall be connected to the tube plates by 
one of the following methods, namely:- 


(a) Expanding with bell mounting or seal welding. 
(0) Strength welding. 


(c) Mechanical bolted joint. 


(2) Roller expanded tubes shall project through the neck or bearing part in the holes by 
at least 6 mm and shall be secured from drawing out by being bell mouthed to the 
extent of 0.8 mm for each 25 mm in diameter plus .6 mm. 


(3) (a) Tubes expanded into headers may be seal-welded inside or outside the header. 
(0) Where a seal weld is provided inside the header, the tube end projection and bell 
mouthed specified in sub-regulation (2) is not required. 


(4) In the case of roller expanded tubes the tube holes in the headers shall be formed in 
such a way that the tubes can be effectively tightened in them, there shall be a neck 
or belt of parallel seating of at least 3 mm. 


(5) Where the tubes are strength welded direct to the headers, the technique followed 
shall be approved by the Inspecting Authority and all welds shall be suitably heat 
treated. 


936 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(6) Bolted joints shall be designed as per regulation 375. 
(7) Tubes spacers supporting clips and lugs may be welded to the tubes. 


(8) The tubes shall be so arranged that they are accessible for cleaning internally and 
externally.

PART-6 


376.Valves and mountings.— () All economisers shall be provided with thermometers for 
measuring water temperature adjacent to the inlet and outlet connections. 


(2) (a)A valve which shall prevent increase of pressure beyond a predetermined limit shall 
be fitted to every economiser and the design shall provide against unauthorized 
interference with the loading. Economisers with pressure parts of cast iron and arranged 
in groups of tiers connected by circulating piping shall have a relief valve fixed on each 
group or tier. Relief valves shall have a minimum orifice diameter of 9 mm. 


(b)The relief valve capacity shall be calculated on the basis of economiser thermal 
capacity. 


(3) Pressure gaugefor indicating the pressure in the economiser shall be constructed as per 
regulation 232. 


(4) Air release valvesshall be provided for the release of air at all points where air 
accumulation may occur. 


(5) Blow off drain valvesshall be provided for complete drainage of water in the economiser. 


938 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(6) Economiser provided with means for heating the incoming feed by mixing it with hot 
water from the economiser outlet,shall have a non-return valve in the hot water return 
line. 


(7)In every case, a reserve flue shall be provided for by passing the flue gases when no 
water is being fed to the boiler through the economiser where it is not integral with boiler. 


(8) To relieve the economisers of excessive pressure accumulation due to internal explosion 
doors preferably of horizontally hinged ‘self-sealing’ type shall be fitted. 


(9) All valves and mountings shall satisfactorily withstand a hydraulic test to the same 
pressure as will be applied to the economiser during its registration. 


(0)Alternative means of feeding the boiler other than through the economiser shall be 
provided. 


() A non-returnvalve shall be provided in the hot feed line between the economiser and the 
boiler to prevent the discharge of steam or water from the boiler into the economiser. 


PART-7 
FEED PIPES 


377.Maximum allowable working pressure for feed piping .—The maximum allowable 
working pressure shall be the maximum pressure generated in overcoming friction and other 
losses in the feed piping under ordinary working conditions, or the maximum pressure which 
can be generated by the boiler feed pumps unless special provision is made to prevent that 
pressure being communicated to the pipe line. 


Note: For boilers operating at design pressure 00 kg/cm? (g) and above feed water discharge 
piping for feed water system without economizer inlet isolating valve can be designed based 
on boiler design pressure with provision of mechanical relief device or a three way valve for 
bypassing H.P Heater, to prevent Boiler Feed Pump (BFP) shut off pressure being 
communicated to the piping system and with such a feed water system, boiler shall be hydro 
tested up to the last isolation valve in the feed water line. 


378. Steel feed pipes.—Steel feed pipes shall be in accordance with chapter -7. 


379. Feed Heaters and similar vessels fitted to feed pipes.—()(a) If welded construction, 
such vessels shall comply with the requirements of Chapter-2, provided that radiographic 
examination of welds may be waived for pressure not exceeding 7.5 kg/cm? (g). 


(0) For parts of vessels of composite construction, the requirements of the appropriate 
regulations of the above Chapters shall be complied with as may be applicable to each such 
part.

PART-8

380. Preparation for inspection.— () (a)At each inspection, the economiser shall be 
emptied and thoroughly cleaned internally and externally and in the flues. 


(0) All mountings shall be opened up and all caps, doors and blank flanges removed to 
permit adequate inspection. 


(2)The owner of an economiser to which this regulation is applicable shall obtain the 
approval of the chief inspector in writing to the method of disconnection which he proposes 
to use and shall be responsible for ensuring that the method so approved is followed in 
practice. 


38i. Procedure for registration.— (l) On receipt of an application for registration,the 
Inspector after the economiser has been prepared for examination,shall take full particulars 
of the design and ascertain the maximum allowable working pressure allowed by the 
regulations.

and submit it to the Chief Inspector.

above, is contained in the regulations, the Chief Inspector shall at his discretion 
determine the fitness of the part.

which it may be worked, the Inspector shall witness the hydraulic test as per 
regulation 383 and may issue a provisional order in Form-XVII. 


942 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(6)If the requirements of provisional order under sub-regulation(5)are not fulfilled, fresh 
provisional 0085 shall be issued subject to a maximum period of twenty four 
months from the date of issue of first provisional order, without any subsequent 
inspection and payment of fee. 


382. Procedure at subsequent Inspection.— (l) (a)After economiser has been cleaned,the 
Competent Person shall make a thorough examination so far as its construction permits. 


(0) The external condition of the tubes shall be carefully noted for wasting especially at the 
feed inlet end and all accessible tubes shall be calibered. 


(c) The internal surfaces of cast iron tubes shallbe closely observed for graphitic wasting as 
far as it is possible and in the event of any tube failure,these shallbe broken up for scrutiny 
so that the general internal condition of the other tubes may be estimated. 


(2) Where tubes or other parts are wasted, the strength shall be re-calculated. 


(3) The scraper gear shallbe examined to note if any parts are missing, if the length of 
travel is adequate and if the scrapers are correctly adjusted. 


(4) All cap bolts shall be inspectedand also the condition and position of the dampers 
and baffles. 

(5) The record of each inspection and calculations shall be entered in the Memorandum 
of Inspection Book. 


383. Procedure for Hydraulic Test.—(l)Every economiser for registration shall be 
hydraulically tested in the presence of Inspector to /2 times the maximum allowable working 
pressure. Hydraulic tests of economisers at subsequent examination when required by the 
Competent Person,shallbe made after the inspection. 

(2) The test pressure to be applied to economisers at subsequent examinations shall be 
from 7.25 to .5 times the maximum allowable working pressure of the economisers. During 
the test, all parts externally and in the flues shall be noted for leakage. 


384. Memorandum of Inspection Book — (l) A Memorandum of Inspection Book shall be 
prepared for each economiser in Form-XVIII and the Inspector shall enter all particulars in 
ink and dimensions of the economisers with the particulars of hydraulic test and his 
inspection notes in this book; 


(2) At subsequent inspection, Competent Person shall enter the dates of the 
Inspections, hydraulic tests when such are made with their notes pertaining to the 
condition of the various parts; 


(3) the Inspector or Competent Person, as the case may be, shall also enter in the 
Memorandum of Inspection Book, the general condition of the economiser and of 
repairs; 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


943 


(4) (a) On submission of the Memorandum Book to the Chief Inspector, he will in the 
case of newly registered economisers, check all particulars and calculations and 
approve the design pressure that is to be permitted. 

(b) In the case of old economisers, the Chief Inspector shall examine the Inspector’s 
notes of inspection and proposals made for repairs. 

(c) A pressure once approved for the economiser shall not be altered without the 
written authority of the Chief Inspector. 

(d)The Memorandum of Inspection Book shall be kept clean and up-to-date and the 
Inspection Book except when actually required by the Competent Person, shall be 
kept in the office of the Chief Inspector. 


385. Registration book.— (l) A registration book or copy of memorandum of inspection 
book for economiser containing all the particulars required for registration shall be 
maintained in the office of the Chief Inspector in Form-XVIII and any orders passed by him 
regarding the economiser shall be entered in the registration book under his initials. 


(2) The Chief Inspector shall also see that the note of subsequent inspections entered in the 
Memorandum of Inspection Book are copied in the Registration book. 


386.Transfer of memorandum of inspection book and registration book - On transfer of 
an economiser from one state to another, the memorandum of inspection and registration 
book shall, on the request of the Chief Inspector of the State to which the economiser has 
been transferred, be forwarded to that Officer who shall take over their custody and maintain 
them as prescribed. 


387. Grant of certificate.—A certificate for the use of an economiser shall be granted in 
Form-XIX. 


388. Casual visits— (l) The Inspector shall notethat the economiser is working 
satisfactorily, the relief valves are correctly adjusted, the scraper gear is operating and the 
external brick work is free from cracks. 


(2) He shall also ascertain that the maker’s instructions for working are being strictly 
followed by the owner. 


Note: It is recommended that the feed inlet temperature to the economiser shall not be less 
than 38°C, to prevent sweating and consequent external corrosion of the tube and bottom 
headers. 


389. Economiser rating.—The rating shall be equivalent to the area of the heating surface 
in square meters which shall be computed from the tubes and the headers. 


390. Registration fee.—An application for registration of Economiser shall be accompanied 
by appropriate fee as specified in regulation 304. 


39. Fee for renewal of certificate-——An application for renewal of certificate of registration 
of economiser shall be accompanied by appropriate fee as specified in regulation 305.

stamped for identification with that number in a prominent place.

393. Inspection of feed pipes.—(l) (a)Feed pipes shall be inspected and hydraulically 
tested before erection in place, and the hydraulic test pressure shall be not less than twice 
the maximum allowable working pressure of the economiser. 

(0) A certificate from the recognized maker or Inspecting Authority certifyingthat this has 
been done may be accepted. 

(c)If the Inspector or Competent Person, as the case may be, is satisfied with the test, the 
pipes may be erected. 

(d) Neither separate certificate for feed pipes shall be issued, nor separate fee shallbe 
charged for their inspection. 

(e) The engraving shall be done within a period of two months from the date of receipt of the 
registry number. 


(2) At subsequent inspection or at any other time, the Competent Person may make an 
external inspection of feed pipes and if found in an unsatisfactory condition, he shall report 
the matter to the Chieflnspector who may require the pipes to be hydraulically tested. 


394. Submission of plans of feed pipes.—(l)The fees for the scrutiny of plans and 
particulars of the material, design and construction of feed pipes, before commencement of 
manufacture of the feed pipes, shall be at the rate of Rs. 200 for 30 metres of piping or part 
thereof. 


(2) The fees for scrutiny of plans and particulars of the material, design and construction 
of any such fittings like feed water heater shall be charged at Rs. 2500 per fitting.

SHELL TYPE BOILERS OF WELDED CONSTRUCTION 


PART-I 
395.Application— (l) These regulations shall apply to all boilers of fusion welded 
construction other than Water Tube boilers and Electrode boilers referred to in Chapters-4 
and 0 respectively. 


(2) Where the design of the boiler is of composite construction viz. combination of Fire 
tube and Water Tube, it shall comply with the relevant regulations governing that particular 
type of construction. 


396. General requirements.—Wherever applicable, the general requirements of Chapter- 
relating to certificates from Makers, Inspecting Authorities, and the like and of Chapter-3 
concerning construction, shall be followed. 


397. Equipment of workshop.— (l) The welding plant and equipment shall be of good 
quality and maintained in an efficient working condition. The welding apparatus shallbe 
installed under cover and arranged so that welding work may be carried out in positions free 
from draughts and adverse weather conditions. The procedure shallbe such that there is 
regular and systematic supervision of the welding works, and the welding operators shall be 
subjected to periodic tests for quality of workmanship by the works officials. Records of 
these tests shall be kept and shallbe madeavailable to the Competent Person for scrutiny. 


(2)The works shallbe equipped with welding plant equipment and quality control 
personnel. However, the equipment for destructive, non-destructive testing and heat 
treatment are not necessary. The manufacturer can tie-up for these facilities outside and a 
letter from the party with whom he makes a tie-up shallbe made available to the Chief 
Inspector of Boilers or the Inspecting Authority or his representative andshallbe allowed to 
inspect the material of the party in the laboratory during the test. 


398.Materials of construction.—Plates, sections and bars used in the construction of these 
boilers shall comply with the requirements of Chapter-2in all respects. However, where the 
tensile strength exceeds 49.6 kg/mm”, the full details of the welding technique including pre- 
heating and post-heating, and the plate preparation to be used, shall be submitted to 
Inspecting Authority for approval before commencement of manufacture. 


399. Welding consumables.—Where welding consumables are used , they shall comply 
with the requirements of regulations 7! to 76, save in the case of the weld metal as 
deposited, where the tensile strength shall not be less than the lower limit specified for the 
plate. 


400. Plain and Stay Tubes.— (l) Tubes shall comply with the provisions of regulations 
30,47 and 48. 


(2) Seamless steel cross-tubes anduptake tubesshall come with regulations 99 and 
00respectively. 


946 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


40i. Construction and workmanship. The manufacturer shall provide Inspecting 
Authority with a fully dimensioned sectional drawing showing the construction of the boiler in 
full detail for approval before putting the work in hand.Full details including dimensions of 
plates preparation for the longitudinal and circumferential seams shall also be shown on the 
drawing.Fully dimensioned sketches showing in details the attachment for stand-pipes, 
branch pipes and seatings, the position of these attachments relative to the longitudinal and 
circumferential seams and other opening shall also be given in the drawing. 


402. Preparation of plates.—For preparation of plates, requirements of regulation 77 shall 
apply.When plates of different thickness are aligned, the welding shall be matched to the 
lower thickness plate and tolerance as required for thinner plate. (refer Figure 2/). 


403. Stress relieving. —Requirements of regulation 78 shall apply. 
404. Cylindrical shells —Requirements of regulation 80 shall apply.

internal diameter. 

(2)The profile as measured on the outside of the boiler by means of a gauge of the 
designed form of the exterior of the boiler, having a length equal to one quarter of the 
internal diameter, shall not depart from the designed form by more than the percentage

(5) In the construction of unfired boilers when the dished ends do not form a part of the

407. Internal flues.— () Sections of internal flues shall each be made from one plate, which 
shall be rolled while cold to circular form. The longitudinal seam shall be fusion butt-welded 
by the metal arc process. 


(2) The maximum permissible variation in diameter of any cross-section shall not exceed 
6 mm or half of the thickness of the plate, whichever is greater. 


(3) The longitudinal welds shall be placed at lower part of the furnace and shall break 
joint in successive sections at least by 50 mm. This requirement shall not be 
applicable if successive sections are separated by tube plate or end plate or bowling 
hoops. 


(4) Where flue sections are flanged for circumferential joints, the flanging shall be carried 
out at one heat by suitable machinery. 


(5) Edges of all flue flanges shall be machined or flame-cut by machine (see regulation 
402). 


(6) Flanged circumferential seams shall be soarranged that they do not fall in line with 
those of the adjacent flue or with circumferential seams of the shell. 


948 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(7) The minimum mean internal diameter of furnaces shall not be less than those given 
in Figure 72/23 depending on the net heat input. 


(8) Where furnace flue is made up of plain or corrugated sections or both, they may be 
connected to each other by fusion butt welded circumferential seams. 


(9) (a) Plain furnaces shall not exceed 3 meter in length except in the case of reverse 
flame boilers, which are considered to be inherently flexible or as provided in clause 
(d). In all other cases flexibility shall be provided in the furnace by means of 
corrugations or blowing hoops or stepping of a minimum of 50 mm in the diameter of 
the furnace. (see figures 2/24 to 2/28. 


(b)If corrugations are used to provide flexibility, at least one-third of the furnace 
length shall be corrugated. 
(c)Breathing spaces as perregulation 483shall be provided for boilers made as per 
this clause. 


(d)Notwithstanding the provisions of clauses (a) and (b), plain furnaces longer 
than 3 meter are allowed to be used in a boiler when the length between boiler 
end plates do not exceed 6.5 meters provided that breathing spaces used in 
this case are in accordance with regulation 484 . 


(0) Where a complete flue is constructed of short plain sections, the ends of each 
adjoining section shall either be swaged out to a radius to provide an adequate point 
of support and longitudinal flexibility and butt-welded together or be butt-welded to 
each side of a bowling hoop. The dimensions shall comply with Figures 2/34, 
72/320r/2/33. 


(i) Stress relieving by heat-treatment shall be carried out when the construction of a flue 
involves the use of a circumferential weld such stress relieving being carried out on 


the completion of all welding in accordance with regulation 453. 


(2) The forms of flue connections to end plates shall be as shown in Figures 2/4, 
72/5, 2/6, 2/77 and 72//8 or be in any other form of welding groovesubject to the 
approval of the Inspecting Authority. 


408. Uptakes.— (l) The uptakes shall be formed from seamless or electric resistance 
welded or fusion butt-welded pipes by electric arc process. The tolerances on these pipes 
shall comply with the requirements of regulation 25. The uptakes shall be fusion butt 
welded to the upward flange of the opening of the furnace crown plate in accordance with 
Figures 2/3 and i2/4. The depth of the flange of the firebox crown plate opening from the 
commencement of the curvature of flange shall be not less than twice the plate thickness 
with a minimum of 25 mm. Unless the whole boiler is to be subsequently stress relieved, the 
uptake and firebox crown plate shall be effectively stress relieved after welding. Where the 
firebox crown plate is also fusion welded to the body of the firebox as in Figure 2/6, the 
firebox complete with uptake shall be effectively stress relieved by heat treatment on 
completion of all welding.

PART-2 
Fireboxes and Combustion chambers 


40.Furnace of vertical boilers.— (|) The furnaces of vertical boilers may be constructed in 
one or more lengthwise sections, each section being rolled from one plate to a full circle. In 
such cases, the component sections may be jointed circumferentially by electric butt- 
welding. The welding shall be stress relieved in accordance with regulation 432. 


(2) In the case of vertical boilers where tube plates form part of the firebox, the tube 
plate portion may be constructed in two vertical sections and the welding of the vertical 
seams when welded shall be stress relieved. 


(3)The maximum permissible variation in diameter, at any cross-section shall not 
exceed 6 mm for fireboxes up to 900 mm in diameter, or 0 mm for fireboxes over 900 mm 
in diameter, or half the thickness of the plate whichever is the greater. 


(4)Circular fireboxes shall preferably be tapered. A taper of 38 mm in diameter per 300 
mm of height is recommended. The water space at the bottom between the firebox and the 
shell shall be not less than 50 mm for boilers up to and including 760 mm in diameter and 
shall be not less than 63 mm for boilers over 760 mm in diameter. 


(5)The method of welding shall be in accordance with regulation 432. 


(6)Flats formed in the firebox for the insertion of water tubes shall have an ample radius 
at the junction of the flat and the curved surfaces and shall be free from sharp corners or tool 
marks. The plate shall not be unduly thinned. 


(7)Ogee flanging whether integral with the firebox or made as separate ring shall 
preferably be formed in one heat by suitable machinery and shall be allowed to cool 
gradually to avoid internal stresses. 


(8)Rings of fire holes mouthpieces or foundation rings shall be made of mild steel. ‘2’ 
sections shall not be used for foundations rings. 


(9)Attachment of fireboxes to cylindrical shells shall be in accordance with Figures 
2/34, 2/35, 2/36 or 2/37. 


(0) The method of attachment of fire holes mouthpieces shall be in accordance with 
Figures 2/40 or 72/4). 


950 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


4.Hemispherical Fireboxes.—() Hemispherical fireboxes shall be pressed to form by 
machine in progressive stages without thinning and shall be annealed on completion. 
(2) Methods of attachment of firebox to the shell be in accordance with Figures 
2/34, 2/35, 2/36 or 2/37. 
(3)The method of attachment of fire-hole mouthpieces and throat pieces shall be in 
accordance with Figures 2/40, or 2/47, 2/43 or 2/44. 


42.Loco-type fireboxes.— () Loco-type firebox wrapper plate sides shall preferably be 
tapered. The water space at the bottom between the fire-box and the shell shall be not less 
than 63 mm. 


(2) Where the firebox tube plate or fire-hole plate is flanged for connection to the wrapper 
plate, the weld shall be located between the commencement of curvature of the flange 
and first row of screwed stays. 


(3) Rings for fire-holemouthpieces of foundation rings shall be made of materials as 
specified in chapter -2. 


(4) Z-sections shall not be used for foundation rings. The attachment of the firebox to the 
outer casing shall be in accordance with Figures 2/37), or 2/30, or 2/3. 


(5) The method of attachment of fire hole mouthpieces shall be in accordance with 
Figures 72/40 or, where the outer casing and the firebox plate are flanged towards the water 
side to form the fire hole, a ring of screwed stays located at not more than half the average 
pitch of the stays distant from the commencement of the curvature of the flanging shall be 
provided (see Figure 72/45. 


43.Water-cooled combustion chambers.—(l) The attachment of the combustion 
chambers—tube plates and back plates to the wrapper plate shall be in accordance with 
Figures 2/79, 72/20, 2/2, 2/22 and where the tube plate is flanged for connection to the 
wrapper plate the weld shall be located between the commencement of curvature of the 
flange and first row of screwed stays. 


(2) The method of attachment of furnace of the flue tubes shall be in accordance with Figures 
72/(52/6 or 2/I7 and access openings shall be in accordance with Figures 72/40 or 
2/46. 


PART-3 
44. Bar stays and firebox stays.— (|) Each bar stay or firebox stay shall be made from a 
solid rolled bar without weld in its length, except where it is attached to the plate it supports. 


(2) Bar stays which have been worked in the fire shall be subsequently annealed. 


(3) It is preferred that when the stay is in position in the boiler, its axis shall be normal to 
the plate it supports, but where this cannot be so arranged, then, if the stay is fitted 
with nuts, bevelled washers shall be provided between the nuts and the plate. 


(4) Stays shall be secured to the plates they support by one of the following methodsas 
given in regulations 4/5 to 48.

45.847 stays.— (/)Plain bars, passing through clearing holes in the plates and welded

(2) Plain bars passing through clearing holes in the plates and fitted with washers on the

Note: Clearing hole for the purpose of this regulation mean a machined

46.Firebox Stays.— (|) (a) Screwed stays, screwed through the plates and riveted over at 
each end to form substantial heads, or fitted with nuts, or the projecting ends fillet-welded as 
indicated in Figures 2/47 and 2/48. 


(0) It is recommended that where the stays are screwed, this shall be with a fine thread 
and the stays and holes shall be screwed with a continuous thread. 


(c)The stays shall be screwed with fine threads of not less than / threads per 25 mm. 


(d)The screw threads on the stays shall be clean, free from checks or imperfections, of 
full depth, or a correct standard form and a good fit in the holes.The middle portion 
shall preferably be turned down to the bottom of the thread. 


(2) Plain stays shall be strength welded to the plates (see Figure 72/49 and 2/50). 


NOTE: This form of attachment is also suitable for plain bar stays. 


(3) All screwed stays less than 350 mm long shall preferably be drilled with a tell-tale hole 
of5 mm diameter to a depth of 3 mm beyond the inner face of the plate. Stays which 
are obscure on one side shallpreferably be made from hollow stay bar. 


47. Girder stays for firebox and combustion chamber crowns.— (|)Where girder stays 
are attached with stay bolts and nuts, they shall be bedded to the corners or ends of side 
plates. 


(2)The attachment of girder stays welded directly to the crown plates shall comply 
with Figures 2/60, 2/6/, 72/62, 2/63 or 2/64. Such girders shall be welded to the crown 
plate prior to stress-relieving. 


(3) Each girder shall be of sufficient strength to support its due proportion of the 
load on the crown plate independently of the crown plate, and the bolts or weld attachments 
shall have sufficient cross-sectional area to carry the applied load. 


(4) The waterways between the underside of the girder and the crown plate shall 
be as large as practicable, but in no case less than 38 mm deep.

420. Manhole frames, mouthpieces and doors.— (l) Manhole frames, mouth-pieces,

type,shall be formed to bed closely to the shell and provide a flat joining surface to the door. 
Alternatively, raised circular mouth-pieces may be fitted externally and where of the flanged 
type shall be bedded closely to the shell. 


(2) Wherever practicable, the frame shall be attached to the inside of the shell 
with the shorter axis parallel to the longitudinal centre line of the boiler. In all 
cases where the shell thickness exceeds 4 mm,oval frames or circular 
mouth-pieces shall be fitted. 


(3) Oval frames and externally raised circular mouthpieces shall be either: 


(a) Formed in one piece without weld, or 


(0) Formed from a suitable rolled section and forge-welded, or fabricated by fusion
