PART-5 


422. Seatings for mountings.—For requirements of seatings for mountings, refer regulation 
729.For requirements of attachment of mountings, refer regulation 730. 


423.Stand Pipes.—Where stand pipes are used, the flanges shall be machined or flame-cut 
by machine on the edges. The bolting flanges shall be machined on the jointing and 
bolting surfaces. 


424.Saddles.— Where saddles are used, the edges of the flanges shall be machined or 
flame-cut by machine. The joining surfaces shall be machined. The studs for the attachment 
of the mountings, if screwed through the saddle, shall be fitted on the inside with nuts of full 
thickness.Where the stud holes do not penetrate through the saddles the length of the 
screwed portion of the stud in the plate shall be not less than the diameter of the stud. 


425.Pads.—Where pads are used, the joining surfaces shall be machined. The pads shall 
have sufficient thickness to allow drilling of the stud holes for mountings without inner 
surface being pierced and the length of the screwed portion of the stud in the pad shall be 
not less than the diameter of the stud. 


426.Attachment of standpipes.—()The following constructions as tostandpipes attached 
to shells and end plates shall be permissible:- 


(i) When the internal diameter of the standpipe does not exceed 25 mm the standpipe 
may be screwed into the plate with a nut on the waterside. 


954 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(ii) Where the internal diameter of the standpipe exceeds 25 mm but does not exceed 50 
mm, it may be screwed in and seal welded. 


(iii) Where the diameter of the standpipe exceeds 50 mm, it may be welded to the end 
plate. 


(2) The provisions in sub-regulation(!) as to the standpipe attachment shall be regulated 
by the following conditions- 


(i) When standpipes are screwed, the screwing shall be of standard pipe thread. 


(ii) Standpipes shall be attached by one of the methods shown in Figures 2/04, 
72/(05,(2/06,42/07, 72/08, 72/09, 72/0, 72/44, 2/442, 2/i3 and 
72/8 or by any other method approved by the Inspecting Authority. 


(iii) Where the standpipes are fabricated by fusion-welding, they shall be stress 
relieved by heat-treatment before attachment to the boiler, unless the whole 
boiler is subject to heat-treatment on completion. 


(iv) Where the bore of the standpipe does not exceed 27 mm or the diameter of 
the opening in the shell does not exceed 27 mm plus twice the thickness of 
the plate to which it is attached, the standpipe may be welded to the plate 
without subsequent heat-treatment of the welds made. If these limits are 
exceeded, the whole plate to which the standpipe is attached shall be stress 
relieved by heat-treatment on completion of welding. 


427.Attachment of pads.—(l) Pads welded to the shell or end plate shall be welded 
internally and externally. 


(2)Methods of attachment of pads shall be as shown in Figures 2/5, 72//6 or 72/7. 
Where the bore of the seating does not exceed 27 mm or the diameter of the opening in the 
shell does not exceed 27 mm plus twice the thickness of the plate to which it is attached, 
the pad may be welded to the plate without subsequent heat-treatment of the welds so 
made. If these limits are exceeded the whole plate to which the pad is attached shall be 
stress relieved by heat-treatment on completion of welding. 


428.Attachment of water and pressure gauges.— Water gauges and pressure gauge 
siphons may be attached direct to the front end plate without the intervention of a pad or 
standpipe, provided they are flanged and secured by studs. If the studs are screwed through 
the plate, nuts of full thickness shall be fitted on the inside of the plate. 


429.Bolts and Nuts.—All holes for bolts and studs shall be drilled and bolts and nuts shall 
be machined where in contact with the flanges.

PART-6 
430. Compensating plates —Compensating plates shall be of same material as that of shell 
and before attachment, shall bed closely to the plates to which they are to be connected. 
Any weld therein shall be on the transverse centre line. 


43. Definition of the term ‘fusion weld’.— (l) For the purpose of this chapter, the term 
‘fusion weld’ is applicable to all welded seams made by the metal arc process with covered 
electrodes or by any other electric arc process in which the arc stream and the deposited 
weld metal are shielded from atmospheric contamination. 


(2) The relevant provisions of this chapter shall also apply to the single run or heavy 
run welding process and that welded boilers manufactured by that process shall comply with 
all regulations of this chapter excepting those in which divergence is necessary solely 
because of special requirements essential for the most efficient utilisation of that process. 
Thus all regulation governing quality of material construction workmanship, and testing (both 
non-destructive and otherwise) are applicable. 


(3) Where welded shells conforming to the regulations of this chapter are made by single 
or heavy run process,it shall be understood that regulations 43,432 and 433 do not apply 
in their entirety. The method of making the welds shall be approved by the Inspecting 
Authority. 


432. Methods of welding.— (l) The seams shall be fusion welded from both sides of the 
plates. The main welding may be on either side of the plate, whichever itis most convenient 
to the manufacturer. Before the second side of the plate is welded, the weld metal at the 
bottom of the first side shall be removed by grinding, chipping, machining or other approved 
method. 


(2) Provided the requisite quality of welding is achieved, the seams may be welded 
from both sides of the plate or from one side of the plate. Before the second side of the plate 
is welded, the metal at the bottom of the first side shall be removed by grinding, chipping, 
machining or other approved method. 


(3) Additional runs of metal shall be deposited at both surfaces of the welded 
seams to ensure that the weld metal at the level of the surfaces of the plate is refined as far 
as possible. 


(4) Thickness of such additional welding shall not exceed values given in following table.

radiographs andother Non-Destructive Test (NDT) methods. If there is a 
question regarding the surface condition of the weld when interpreting a 
radiographic film, the film shall be compared to the actual weld surface or 
provide smooth contours and to be flush with the respective surfaces of the 
plate before radiography examination is done.

or manhole frames, not less than two runs or metal shall be deposited at each weld. 


(0) Each run of weld metal shall be thoroughly cleaned and freed from slag before the 
next run is deposited. 


433. Types of welded shell seams.—The longitudinal and intermediate circumferential 
seams shall be made with butt joints of the single or double U or V type (see Figures 2/3, 
2/4, 2/5, and 2/6) or of any other type approved by the Inspecting Authority. End 
circumferential seams shall be in accordance with Figures 72/7, 2/8, 2/9, 2/0, 2/ or 


72/(2 or with any other form approved by the Inspecting Authority. 


434. Repairs to welded seams.— (|) Any repair to a weld carried out by the manufacturer 


shall first be agreed to by the Competent person. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


957 


(2) (a)Where defects are distributed over the whole length of the seam,the total length of 
the portions which may be cut from any one longitudinal or circumferential seam to 
remove all defects shall not exceed 5 percent of the total length of the seam. 


(b) When, however, the defects are all located in a single continuous length 
which may be cut out to remove all defects shall not exceed 0 percent of the total 
length of the seam. 


(3) Defect shall be cut out by chipping, machining or other approved methods. 


(4) In the case of Class | boilers, all repaired areas shall be subjected to radiographic 
examination. 


435.Tests on welded seams of shell.—() Test plates to represent all welded seams shall 
be attached at each end of each longitudinal seam. These shall be of a size sufficient for the 
preparation of the test pieces specified. In the case of shell plates, the test plate may be 
located at one end only (see Figure 2/58). Where the shell is formed in two or more rings, 
the staggered longitudinal seam shall be regarded as a continuous longitudinal seam 
provided the welding be effected in one reasonably continuous operation and by the same 
operator or operators. The material for the test plates shall be cut from the respective plate 
or plates forming the appropriate seam. 


(2) In the case of insufficient material being available on the shell plate to permit the cutting 
of test pieces, these shall be acceptable if they are made from another plate,provided it is 
made from the same cast. The test plates shall be stamped by the Inspecting Authority 
before being cut. 


(3) The weld groove in the test plates shall be similar to that adopted for the 
corresponding edges of the longitudinal seam, and the respective fusion faces shall be in 
continuous alignment. The test plates may be reinforced or supported during welding so that 
any relative displacement due to warping during welding does not exceed 5°. The weld 
metal in the test plates and the seam shall be deposited continuously at the same operation. 


(4) The weld in any test plate shall not be repaired. If any defects are revealed in the 
weld metal of a test plate the position of this shall be clearly marked on the plate and the test 
pieces shall be selected from such parts of the test plates as may be decided by the 
Competent Person. 


(5) Test plates warped during welding by not more than 5° may be straightened before 
heat-treatment. For the heat-treatment of the test plates (see regulation 453). 


(6) Where there are circumferential seams only or where the method of welding the 
circumferential seams differ from that employed for the longitudinal seams, the test plates 
shall be provided.

437. Tensile tests.— (|) Welded joint; the dimensions of the reduced tensile section shall be as 
shown in Figure i2/73. The width of the reduced section shall be at least 25 mm. 


(2)If the thickness of the plate does not exceed 30 mm, the thickness of the specimen shall be 
equal to the plate thickness and the plate surface of the specimen shall be machined to take 
away the surface irregularities of the plate and the weld. 


(3) If the plate thickness exceeds 30 mm, the tensile test shall be carried out on several 
reduced section specimens, each having a thickness of at least 30 mm and width at the 
effective cross-section of at least 25 mm. These specimens shall be taken out of the test 
piece in such a way that the tensile test covers the whole thickness of the weld joints as 
shown in Figure 2/74. The tensile strength shall not be less than the lower limit specified for 
the plate. 


(4) The dimensions of the all weld metal tensile test specimen shall be those given in Figure 
2/77. The diameter shall be the maximum possible consistent with the cross section of the 
weld but in no case more than 20 mm, the gauge length shall be equal to five times the 
diameter. The tensile strength shall not be less than the lower limit specified for the plate. 
The elongation shall not be less than 20% on a gauge length of five times the diameter of 
the specimen or 5.65 times the square root of the cross-sectional area of the specimen, and 
the reduction in area not less than 35 percent. 


438.Cold bend tests.— (|) Two bend tests shall be madeas given in this regulation. 

(2) One specimen shall be tested with the outer surface of the weld in tension and the other 
with the inner surface in tension. The specimen shall be rectangular in section and shall be 
cut out transversely to the weld so as to have a width not less than one-and-a half times the 
thickness of the plates. The sharp corners of the specimens shall be rounded to a radius not 
exceeding 0% of the thickness of the specimen. 

(3) Where the plate thickness does not exceed 32 mm, the thickness of the specimen shall be 
equal to the full thickness of the test plate. Where the plate thickness exceeds 32 mm, the

specimen shall in all cases have a thickness of at least 32 mm. The specimen to be tested

440.Macro and micro examinations.—() A specimen of the full thickness of the plate and not

(2) Micro-etching of a complete cross-section of the weld including the heat affected zone shall 
show Satisfactory penetration, fusion and absence of significant inclusions or other defects.In 
case thereis any doubt as to the condition of the weld as shown by macro-etching, the area

44.Additional tests before rejection—()ln case any of the test specimens taken in 
accordance with regulations 435 to 443fail to meet the specified requirements, retests shall 
be allowed for each specimen that fails as follows: 


(2) Where any result of the tensile test is not less than 90% of the specified figures, one retest 
shall be made. Where any result falls below 90%, two retests shall be made. 


(3) Where a bend specimen fails to meet the specified requirements, two retests shall be 
made. 


(4) If an impact test fails to meet the specified requirements, two retests shall be taken from the 
test plate, one on each side of the final specimen and separate from it by not more than 5 
mm. 


(5) If it be found there is insufficient metal to permit the preparation of specimens for retests 
from the remainder of the test plate from which the original specimen was taken, the 
specimen for retest may be cut from the test plate relating to the opposite end of the same 
longitudinal seam. 


(6) In case any of the additional tests fail to meet the specified requirements, the welded seams 
represented by these tests shall be rejected.

443. Radiographic examinations.— () Every portion of the longitudinal and circumferential 
butt-welded seams of the shell of the boiler shall be subjected to radiographic or ultrasonic 
examination. Each Longitudinal and circumferential butt welded seams of Furnace, Reversal 
chamber, Access tube and drop pipes shall be subjected to 0% radiographic 
examination.The percentage of welds to be examined shall include each intersection of 
longitudinal and circumferential seams.Where ultrasonic examination is used, it shall be 
demonstrated to the satisfaction of the Inspecting Authority that the equipment and the 
technique used are satisfactory. The manufacturer shall ensure that the operator employed 
is competent to use the equipment, apply the technique and interpret the results of the 
examination. 


(2) The methods employed in obtaining the radiographs shall be such as to show clearly 
differences equal to 2% of the thickness at the welded joints. To determine whether this 
result is being attained, an indicator of approved form which includes a portion equivalent to 
not more than2% of the joint thickness shall be placed in the vicinity of the weld so as to 
make a record on each radiograph. Each section of every weld shall be marked so that the 
radiographs can be easily correlatedto the particular part of the seam represented. 


(3) The examination shall be made from the original films and the acceptability of the welds shall 
be decided by the Inspecting Authority. The welds deemed unsatisfactory shall be rejected 
or dealt with under the condition of regulation 434 and can be radiographed again. The films 
shall be retained by the manufacturer for minimum three years for reference. 


Notes: (i) Magnetic Particle Flaw Detection, Magnetic methods of flaw detection shall be employed 
wherever possible for ferrite steel. 


(2) Dye-Penetrate Flaw Detection; Dye-penetrant or equivalent methods of flaw detection 
shall be employed for Austenitic or other non-magnetic steel. 


(3)All butt-welded joints shall be subjected to non-destructive examination by radiographic, 
radioscopy or other approved methods such as ultrasonic testing, magnetic particle 
inspection or liquid dye penetrant inspection. When radioscopic examination is to be 
performed in lieu of radiography on welded components, the following requirements shall be

2/74:specimen B). The tensile strength of the welded joint specimen shall not be less 
than the lower limit specified for the plate. 


446.Cold bend tests.— (|) Two bend tests shall be madeas given in this regulation. 


(2) One specimen shall be tested with outer surface of the weld in tension, and the other 
with the inner surface in tension. The specimens shall be rectangular in section and 
shall be cut out transversely to the weld so as to have a width not less than one-and- 
a-half times the thickness of the plate. The sharp corners of the specimens shall be 
rounded to a radius not exceeding 0 percent of the thickness of the specimen. 


(3)The specimen to be tested with the outer surface of the weld in tension shall be 
prepared by cutting to waste the metal local to the inner surface of the weld, so that 
the desired specimen thickness is obtained (see A, Figure 2/78). The specimen to be 
tested with inner surface in tension shall be prepared by cutting to waste the metal 
local to the outer surface of the weld so that the desired specimen thickness is 
obtained (see 3, Figure i2/78). Where the thickness of the plate permits, both 
specimens may be cut from the same piece of plate, the specimens being located in 
the plate one above the other (See C, Figure 2/78). 


(4) Each specimen shall be mounted with the weld midway between the supports set 
apart at a distance of not more than 5.2 times the thickness of the specimen and pushed 
through the supports with a former having a diameter equal to three times the thickness 
of the specimen. 


(5) On completion of the test, no crack or defect at the outer surface of the specimen 
shall be greater than 7.6 mm measured across the specimen, or 3 mm measured along 
the length of the specimen. Premature failure at corners of the specimen shall not be 
considered cause for rejection. 


447.Nick-break specimen .— (l) This specimen shall have a width not less than one and a 
half times its thickness and the slot shall be cut in each side of the specimen through the 
centre of the weld and perpendicular to the outer face of the boiler. 

(2) The specimen shall then be broken in the weld and the fracture shall reveal a sound 
homogenous weld substantially free from slag inclusions, porosity and coarse crystallinity. 


448.Additional tests beforerejection.— In case any of the test specimens fails, two retests 
shall be made and both shall meet the specified requirements. 


449.Specimen after tests.—lf required, specimens after tests shall be at the disposal of the 
Inspecting Authority for examination. 


450.Radiographic or ultrasonic examination.—Each longitudinal and circumferential seams 
in class II boiler (including shell to end plate) shall be subjected to spot radiographic or 
ultrasonic examination.

482. Breathing space.—Breathing spaces as provided in regulations 483,484 or 485shall be 
provided depending on the design of the boiler with special attention to the provision of sub-

(2) (a) In case of multi-tubular boilers,for both front and rear attachment of 
furnaces, the breathing spaces between furnace and tube nests or between 
furnace and shell shall be minimum of 50 mm or 5% of the shell inside 
diameter, whichever is larger, with a maximum requirement of 00 mm. 


(0) Clearances between the furnace and wet-back wrapper plates shall not 
require consideration as breathing spaces. 

(c)In the case of reverse flame boilers, the breathing space at the front end 
between furnace and the tube nests shall be not less than 50 mm and the

larger, with a maximum of 00 mm.

plates shall not require consideration as breathing spaces. 


(6 )Breathing spaces between tubes and shell shall not be less than 40 mm.

than 200 mm except that for shell outside diameters exceeding 800 mm and

for shell outside diameter less than 400 mm and furnace lengths less than 
3000 mm they shall be not less than 50 mm.

inside diameter, whichever is larger, with a maximum requirement of 00 mm.

486. Gusset Link, brace and similar stays.— (l) For welded Lancashire, Cornish and 
Cylindrical Horizontal Multi-tubular type boilers, all welded gussets stays shall not be used. 
To ensure flexibility, link stays, bar stays, brace stays other than the all-welded type shall be 
used. All welded gusset stays, however, may be used in cylindrical horizontal waste heat 
and cylindrical vertical multi-tubular boilers. 


(2) Welded gusset stays and brace may be used for welded Lancashire Cornish and 
Cylindrical Horizontal Multi-tubular type boilers provided their method of attachment is 
approved by the inspecting Authority. 


(3) | Each gusset or link stay supporting the flat end plate of a boiler shall be designed to 
carry the whole load due to pressure on the area it supports. The areas supported by any 
one stay shall be obtained by considering the total area to be supported which lies within

multiplied by L/Li (see Figures 72/04, 2/02 and 2/03).

503.Hydraulic test.— (l) (a) Each Class | Boiler shall, on completion of all welding and/or 
repairs and after heat-treatment, be subjected to a hydraulic test of .5 times the design 
pressure without any indication of weakness or defect. 


(0) Each Class ॥ and Class Ill Boiler shall be tested to a pressure twice the design 
pressure. 


(2) (a) The test shall be witnessed by the Inspecting Authority or Competent Person. 


(b) The test pressure shall be maintained for a period not less than 30 minutes. 
(c) In the interest of safety,it is importantthat the boiler be properly vented, so as to 


prevent the formation of air pockets, before the test pressure as applied. 


Notes: 

i. It is recommended that the temperature of the water shall not be less than 7°C during the 
hydraulic test. 

2. It is further recommended that before the boiler is approached for close examination, the 
pressure shall be reduced to not less than i. times the design pressure and not more 
than 0.9 times the hydraulic test pressure. 

3. Oncompletion of hydraulic test, release of pressure shall be gradual. 

4. Deflection of different pressure parts shall be examined carefully and there shall not be 
any permanent set after release of pressure. 


(3) If any repairs are found to be necessary during or subsequent to the hydraulic 
pressure test, the boiler shall again be subjected to the pressure test specified above 
after completion of the repairs and after any heat treatment provided repaired weld 
joint requires heat treatment as per regulation 453. 


Note: Observations and remarks of Competent Person/ Inspecting Authority shall be 
recorded for filing with maker’s papers. 


504.Safetyvalves.—Boiler shall be provided safety valves complying with regulations 92 to 
29, with following changes:- 


(i) The safety valves shall be reset at a pressure at least 2.5% below, but not more than 5% 
below the safety valve set pressure. 


(ii) The 5% limit is increased to 0% for valves having a body seat bore less than 32 mm and 
or having a set pressure of 24 bar gauge or less.

CHAPTER-3 


QUALIFICATION TESTS FOR WELDERS AND WELDING 
OPERATORS ENGAGED IN WELDING AND REPAIR OF BOILERS 
AND BOILER COMPONENTS, PIPES, HEAT EXCHANGER AND 
HEAT EXCHANGER COMPONENTS UNDER CONSTRUCTION, 
ERECTION AND FABRICATION AT SITE. 


505.Application— (l) These regulations shall apply to testing of welders and welding 
operators engaged in welding and repair of boilers and boiler components, steam-pipes, 
heat exchanger and heat exchanger components of ferrous and nonferrous material under 
construction, erection and fabrication at site. 


PART- 
Definitions 


506. Welder.— Welder means a person who performs manual or semi-automatic welding. 
507.Welding operator— Welding operatormeans a person who operates machine or 
automatic welding equipment. 


508. Reasonable continuity of service.—The continuity of service of the welder orwelding 
operator shall be considered as continuity of service if heretains the initial skill level though 
not engaged in welding for a period of upto six months. 

509. U-Number.—(l) U Number grouping of electrodes and welding consumables in table 
3/5 of regulation 520 is based essentially on their usability characteristics, which determine 
the ability of welders to make satisfactory welds with a given welding consumables. 

(2) This grouping is intended to reduce the number of welding performance qualifications. 


PART-2 
Welding Positions 


50.Plate groove welding—The welding positions as mentioned in Figure 3/ of this 

chapter shall be as following,namely:- 

(i)Flat position 3/LGF; Plate in a horizontal plane with the weld metal deposited from 
above. 

(ii) Horizontal Position 73/LGH; Plate in a vertical plane with the axis of the weld 

horizontal. 

(iii) Vertical Position 3/LGV;Plate in a vertical plan with the axis of the weld vertical. 

(iv) Overhead Position 3/LGO;Plate in a horizontal plane with the weld metal 

deposited from underneath. 


026 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


5. Plate fillet welding —The welding positionsas mentioned in Figure 3/2 of this chapter 
shall be as following,namely:- 

(i) Flat Position 3/LFF; Plates so placed that the weld is deposited with its axis 
horizontal and its throat vertical 

(ii) Horizontal Position 3/LFH;Plates so placed that the weld is deposited with its 
axis horizontal on the upper side of the horizontal surface and against the 
vertical surface. 

(iii) Vertical Position 3/LFV;Plates so placed that weld is deposited with its axis 
vertical. 

(iv) Overhead Position 3/LFO;Plates so placed that the weld is deposited with its 
axis horizontal on the underside of the horizontal surface and against the 


vertical surface. 


52. Pipe groove welding.—The welding position of pipe groove weldingas mentioned in 


Figure 3/3 of this chapter shall be as following,namely:- 


(i) Horizontal Rolled 3/PGR; Pipe with its axis horizontal and rolled during 
welding so that the weld metal is deposited from above with the axis of the 
weld horizontal. 

(ii) Vertical Fixed 3/PGV; One test of groove welded joint with the axis of the 
pipe in a vertical position and the seam welded circumferentially in a 
horizontal position. 

(iii) Horizontal Fixed 3/PGH; One test of groove welded joint with the axis of the 
pipe in a horizontal position and the seam welded without rotating the pipe. 

(iv) Pipe Inclined 73/PGl;One test of groove welded joint with the axis of the pipe 
inclined 45 degree to the horizontal axis and the seam welded without rotating 


the pipe.

PART-3 
53. Engagement of certified weldersorwelding operators.— (l)No welderorwelding 
operator shall be engaged for welding on boilers or steam-pipes under construction, erection 
or fabrication at site or in the repair of boilers or steam-pipes, unless hepossesses a 
certificate as required under the regulations and attains the agenot less than eighteen years. 


(2)He shall have undergone a regular apprenticeship of two years from a recognised 
Industrial training institute or haveat least one year regular on the job industrial 
experience as a welder orwelding operator. 

(3) The holder of such certificate shall be bound to produce it when called upon to do so by 
the Inspecting Authority or Competent Person. 

(4)In case of engaging experienced welders orwelding operators, reasonable continuity of 
service shall be ensured by the employer before engaging them by maintaining proper 
records of test conducted by the employing organisation. 


574. Initial qualification test and issue of certificate— (|) Every welder or welding 
operator shall meet the qualification requirement to the satisfaction of the Competent 
Authority who shall assess hisperformance for qualifying for the certificate. 


(2) The Competent Authority may, thereafter, issue a certificate in the Form-ll indicating the 
class and type of welding in which he has qualified. 


030 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


55. Issue of duplicate certificate— (l)ln case of loss of a certificate issued to a 


welderorwelding operator in Form-XXI, a duplicate certificate may be issued by the 
Competent Authority who issued the original certificate provided that the Competent 
Authority is satisfied with the genuineness of the case. 


(2) Fee for issue of duplicate certificate shall be as per regulation 334. 


56. Validity of certificate— (l) The certificate issued to a welderorwelding operator under 
these regulations shall remain valid for a maximum period of twenty-four months from the 
date of issue, provided that the holder thereof has, subsequent to the test, been employed 
with reasonable continuity on the class and type of work for which heis qualified. 


57. Revalidation or renewal of certificate —() The certificate may be renewed after the 
validity of 24 months from the date of qualification from time to time, for a period not 
exceeding twenty-four months at a time, in case the welder or welding operator is 
continuously engaged in qualified process and certified by the organisation for which he is 
working. 


(2) The details of welding continuity shall be filled up in the Form-XX duly signed by the 
organisation and preserved along with the original certificate and put up to Competent 
Authority for renewal. 


(3) In case of non-fulfilment of continuity criteria the welder or welding operator shall appear 
for the re-qualification test to the satisfaction of the Competent Authority. 


58. Revoking of qualification.— () The performance qualification of a welder or welding 
operator can be revoked by the Competent Authority if there is a specific reason to question 
hisability to make welds that meet the specification. 


(2) The qualificationthat support the welding that heis doing shall be revoked. 


59. Hierarchy of qualifications.— (|) (a) Initially, a welder or welding operator may be 
qualified in carbon steel plate and subsequently, allowed to appear for qualification testing in 
alloy steel plate, carbon steel or alloy steel pipe and tube qualification. or, a welderorwelding 
operator may be tested for higher grades, pipe and tube directly. 


(0) The range of qualification covered by testing of a particular grade of material or product 
form shall be as shown in Table 3/7. 


(2) The qualification certificate of such a welder or welding operator who has successfully 
completed qualification test, may be extended as per regulation 57. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)]

520.Essential 


variables for welder orwelding operator requalification—A welder or 


welding operator shall require requalification whenever a change is made in one of the 
following essential variables,namely:-. 


(i) 


(ii) 


(ii) 


(iv) 


(vii) 


An omission of backing- A welder or welding operator needs requalification 
when the backing is removed and double-welded groove welds are 
considered welding with backing. 

An addition of the backing in gas welding - A welder or welding operator shall 
require requalification when the backing is introduced in gas welding process. 
A change in U number of electrode - A welder shall require requalification 
when the consumable group designation is changed from one U number to 
other U number (refer Table 73/5 & Table 3/6 of this regulation). 

A change in the base metal (M number) to be welded - A welder shall require 
requalification when the base metal is changed (refer Table 2/i in Chapter- 
2and Tablel3/7 in this Chapter). However, a welder who is qualified in a 
higher grade of steel shall be permitted to weld a lower grade of steel. 

A change from one welding process to any other process - A welder shall 
require requalification when the welding process is changed. 

A change from direct current to alternating current, and vice versa - A welder 
shall require requalification when the current type is changed from ‘dc’ to ‘ac’ 
and vice versa. 

A change in welding position —(a) A welder shall require requalification when 
the position in which he is qualified is changed. 

(0) A welder who is qualified in more difficult position shall be deemed to be 
qualified for a less difficult position as given in tablesi3/2, 73/3 and 3/4.

PART-4 


52. Tests for initial qualification of a welderorwelding operator.—For qualification of a 
welder, the welder orwelding operator has to appear for the testsas given in regulations 522 
to 526. 


522.Theoretical examination.— A welderorwelding operator shall be required to answer 
questions on the following subjects, orally or otherwise- 

(i) Weld preparation 

(ii) Elementary knowledge of the working of welding equipment. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


035 


(iii) Elementary knowledge of properties of material to be welded — cold and hot 
working, thermal conductivity, fusion point, oxidation (for welders engaged in 
alloy steel welding). 

(iv) Elementary knowledge of electro-technical principles, - kinds of current, striking 
arc voltage, welding — arc voltage (for arc welders). 

(v) Kinds of welds, welding defects and their prevention, welding technique (forward 
and backward), influence of electrical parameters like amperage (for electric arc 
welders), preheating ofbase material and subsequent heat treatment. 

(vi) Electrodesandfiller metals for different types of welds and steels and joints in 
different positions. 


523.Practical tests—(l) The welderorwelding operator shall be required to undergo and 
pass the testsas given in regulations 524 to 526. 

(2) The material of plates, tubes, pipes and electrodes used for these tests shall conform to 
the requirements of appropriate regulations as may be applicable in each case. 


524.Plate Welding.— ()One groove welded joint of two pieces of plates with single V, 
double V or double U grooves on boiler quality plates in the required positions (see Fig. 3/4 
of regulation 572). 
(2) One fillet welded joint over a length of 38 mm using plates of not less than 6 mm thick 
in the required positions (see Fig. 3/2). 


525.Pipe and tube Welding.— ()A butt welded joint of two pieces of pipes with the axis ina 
horizontal position. (see Fig. 73/PGH) with a pipe diameter 727.5 x 72.5 mm thickness 

(minimum). 

(2) A butt welded joint of two pieces of boiler tubes of diameter 76. mm x 7. mm 
thickness (maximum) with the axis in a vertical position and tubes of same size fixed 
in adjoining positions at a pitch distance of 300 mm (see figure 3/PGV). 

(3) A weld between a branch tubes of diameter 88.9 mm (minimum) to a pipe (see Fig. 
3/7). The branch tube shall not be of size less than 89 mm diameter x 6 mm thick. 


526.Cladding.—_(l) This test is required only for welders or welding operators doing 
corrosion resistant/hard facing overlay. 
(2)The qualification test coupon shall be of minimum size of 50 mm x 50 mm x T 
(thickness of base metal). 
(3) The weld overlay cladding shall be of 38 mm wide (minimum) and 5 mm thick 
(minimum two layers). 
(4) The weld overlay shall consist of a minimum of three weld beads in the first layer. 
(See Table 3/9 of chapter 3 for qualification limits.) 


Note - Every welded test piece for the examination of welders shall be stamped with an identification 
mark on either side of the weld. 


527. Tests for requalification of a welder / welding operator.— (|)The material of plates, 
tubes, pipes and electrodes used for practical tests shall conform to the requirements of 
appropriate regulations as may be applicable in each case. 


036 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(2) For requalification, the welder or welding operator need not be examined in 

theoretical subjects. He shall be required to qualify in the following practical tests, namely: - 

(i) Plate Welding; agroove welded joint shall be made in a position originally qualified. 

(ii) Pipe and Tube welding; as mentioned in regulation 525. 

(iii) Cladding; as mentioned in regulation 526. 

(3) When a welder is continuously engaged on production weld, test on the actual 
production joints to the satisfaction of the Competent Authority may be accepted as 
an alternative to the tests prescribed as above under clauses (i), (ii) and (iii) of sub- 
regulation (2)

(3) The test shall be deemed to have been satisfactory when the requirements as

529.Fillet weldedplatespecimens.— (|) (a) The preparation of the fillet-weld test specimen 
shall conform to Fig. 3/5 of chapter 3. 


(o)The test specimen shall not contain any visible cracks. It shall be cut transversely to 
provide a centre section (254 mm) long and two end sections each approximately (25 mm) 
long. 


(2) (a) The centre section shall be loaded laterally in such a way that the root of the weld is 
in tension. 


(0) The load shall be steadily increased until the specimen fractures or bends flat upon itself. 


(3)The cut end of one of the end sections shall be polished and etched with a suitable 
reagent to give a clear definition of the structure of the weld. 


(4)The test shall be deemed to have been satisfactory when the requirementsas specified in 
sub-regulation(5) are met. 


(5) (a)The bend specimen shall not fracture during loading and if the specimen fractures, 
then the fractured surface shall show no evidence of cracks or incomplete root penetration, 
and the sum of the lengths of inclusions and gas pockets visible on the fractured surface 
shall not exceed (57 mm). 


(0) Visual examination of the cross-section of the weld shall show the following: 
(i)Complete fusion at the root and freedom from cracks. 
(ii)Convexity or concavity of the weld profile not more than 7.6 mm 


(iii) The length of two legs of the fillet within 7.6 mm difference.

53.Welded Tube Joints.— ()A test length approximately 203 mm long shall be cut from 
the tube with the welded joint disposed approximately at the centre. After visual examination, 
one test piece not exceeding 73 mm, for tubes 6 mm in thickness and below and thrice the 
thickness of the tube for thickness of over 6 mm shall be cut longitudinally. 


(2) (a) The test piece shall not be less than 76 mm in length on either side of the weld. 


(0) The slight excess of internal bead may be filed until it is not more than 0.8 mm proud of 
the general surface. 


(c) The test piece shall then be bent back with the root in tension through 90° round a former 
of diameter equal to three times the thickness of the tubes. 


(d) With regard to alloy steel pipes and tubes, the bend test specimen shall be bent without 
being straightened, but after removal of the weld reinforcement down to the level of but not 
below the surface, round a former of diameter 4t and through an angle of 90°. 


[भाग ॥--खण्ड 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 4044 


(6) The bending may be carried out by blows or by pressure. Care shall be taken to ensure 
that the former is so positioned that the weld is maintained at the crown of the bend. 


(f) The test specimen shall be capable of being bent through 90° without signs of failure, 
although slight premature failure at the edges of a specimen need not be considered a 
cause for rejection. 


(g) The opening out of a slight defect due to incomplete root penetration or lack of root fusion 
need not be considered a cause for rejection; provided the defect has sound metal at the 
back and on either side of it.

PART-7 
540. Awarding of marks.— (|) (a) Marks shall be awarded as per the Form-XxXI. 


(0) Candidates obtaining marks not less than 60 per cent in the oral or written examination 
and not less than 75 per cent in the practical tests, shall be deemed to have qualified for a 
certificate provided that the bend tests are found to be satisfactory and in case a candidate 
fail in the oral or written examination but passes in the practical test, hemay be re-examined 
in oral or written examination within a period of twelve weeks from the date of examination of 
practical test, and if he obtains not less than 60 per cent marks in the re-examination, 
heshall be deemed to have qualified for a certificate. 


(2)The Form shall be attested by the Competent Authority. 


54. Award of Certificate.— (|)On successful completion of theoreticaltests mentioned in 
regulation 522 and practical testsmentioned in regulations523 to 526the welder may be 
awarded a certificate in Form-llto the extent of the tests passed by him. 


(2) (a) Welderorwelding operator who pass the tests for groove welds in plates shall 
be considered as having qualified for making fillet welds in plates. 


(0) Weldersorwelding operators who pass the tests for fillet welds, shall be qualified 
to make fillet welds only. 


(c) Any certificate issued for any purpose under any rules made by the State 
Government in this behalf shall be deemed to have been issued for that purpose under this 
Chapter and any action taken under the said rules, shall be deemed to have been taken 
under this Chapter. 


542. Maintenance of records.— (l) Every manufacturer or repairer of boilers and steam- 
pipes shall maintain a record of all welding personnel engaged on welding and repairing of 
boilers and steam-pipes, particulars of each welder and welding operator and the work 
handled by him. Such record shall be produced to the Inspecting Authority or Competent 
Person on demand. 


(2) In the case of welders orwelding operators who undertake welding under their 
own responsibility, the record as aforesaid shall be maintained by themselves. 


543. Fees for examination of Welders or Weldingoperators.—Fees for examination of 
Welders or Welding operators shall be as per regulation 33. 


544. Penalty.—Penalty shall be as per regulation332.

CHAPTER -4 
SMALL INDUSTRIAL BOILERS 


PART-4 
GENERAL 


545. Scope.— This Chapter shall apply to the design, construction, inspection, registration, 
operation and maintenance of small industrial boilers. 


546.For the purpose of this chapter, “small industrial boiler” shall include;- 


(a) A shell type boiler generating steam for use external to itself under pressure up to 7 
kg/cm? (g) and having a volumetric capacity exceeding 25 litres (such capacity being 
measured from the feed check valve to the main steam stop valves), but not 
exceeding 500 litres including the volumetric capacity of all pressure parts being 
heated from the same heating source and connected to the boiler; or 


(0) A coil type or a once through boiler or a water tube boiler having the conditions 
specified in clause (a) above except - 


(i) The limitation of pressure shall be 2 kg/cm? (0), and 
(ii) The capacity shall not be exceeding 750 litres; 


Provided that in case of boilers having combined features of clauses (a) and (b), the 
design pressure shall be restricted to 7 kg/cm? (g) and the volumetric capacity of particular 
pressure parts shall not exceed the limits specified in the respective clauses above subject 
to an aggregate of 500 litres. 


PART-2 


Extent to which variation from the standard conditions laid down in the preceding 
chapters is permissible 


547.—Variations from standards.-The variations from the standard conditions provided in 
the preceding chapters of these regulations shall be permittedfor small industrial boilersas 
provided in regulations 548 to 554. 


548.Materials.—() The materials used in the construction of small industrial boilers shall, 
except as otherwise provided under this chapter, conform to the provisions made in chapter- 
2 of these regulations. 

(2) (a) Steel plates used in the construction of the boilers shall be of IS: 2062 fully killed 
or equivalent and the plate for shell and heads shall be not less than 6 mm in 
thickness and the heads as tube sheets for tubes rolled in shall be at least 8 mm in 
thickness. 


046 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(0) The steel maker certificate provided in Part A of Form V is not required for steel 
plates of IS: 2062 from the steel maker provided all other certification requirements 
as specified in applicable regulations are complied with. 


(3) (a) Heads of parts of boilers when not exposed to direct impact of flame may be 
made of cast iron or malleable iron provided they comply with other requirements of 
these regulations. 


(b) The allowable stress on cast iron or malleable iron shall be based on the 
tensile strength of material with a factor of safety of not less than 4.5. 


549.Design, construction, workmanship and method of computing the Maximum 
Allowable Working Pressure-.— (|) (a) The construction except where otherwise specified 
shall be the same as those provided in the relevant provisions of the preceding chapters of 
these regulations. 


(b) In case of fusion welded boiler, neither stress-relieving nor radiography of welded 
joints shall be required. 


(2) (a) In small industrial boilers,unflanged steel tube plate may be inserted into the shell 
and welded for the entire thickness as shown in Figure 4/ of this regulation with a 
fillet weld having a throat not less than % times the thickness of the shell or tube 
sheet whichever is smaller.

550.Inspection and Testing.—The small industrial boilers shall be subjected to inspection 
during construction by an Inspecting Authority and the inspection of the boilers shall be 
made at the stages as given in regulations 55 and 552: 


55.Shell type boilers—(i) The inspection of shell type boilers shall be made at the 
following stages, namely:- 

(i) material identification and inspection; 

(ii) inspection of each component after completing welding and drilling; 

(iii) assembly of boiler; 

(iv) hydraulic test. 


(2) In case of a boiler wholly or partly welded construction, the hydraulic test pressure 
shall be equal to two times the design pressure of the boiler. 


(3) A test coupon shall be provided by the maker for conducting root and face bend 
tests. 


552.Coil type boilers, once through boilers and water tube boilers—— (l) The 
inspection of coil type boilers, once through boilers and water tube boilers shall be made at 
the following stages, namely:- 


(i) Identification of materials. 
(ii) Hydraulic test, 
(2) The pressure for hydraulic test shall be two times of the design pressure of the 
boiler. 


553.Certificates and maker’s stamps.— (l)The certificate and maker’s stamp shall be in 
conformity with the provisions of Chapter-/ of these regulations. 

(2) Where all information cannot be visibly stamped on the boiler plate due to its small size, 
maker's certificate accompanying the boiler shall contain the necessary details, but in all 
cases, name, works number and the year of the make shall be stamped or exhibited on 
the boiler. 


PART-3 
554. Valves, gauges, fittings and feed supply.— (/) (a) (i) Every boiler shall be fitted with 
at least three brass wash plugs of not less than 25 mm diameter which shall be screwed into 
the openings in the shells near the bottom. 


048 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(ii) In the boilers of closed system type heated by removable internal electric heating 
elements, the opening for these elements when suitable for cleaning purposes may be 
substituted for wash out openings. 


(0) (i) Boilers not exceeding 300 mm internal diameter may have two 25 mm openings 
for cleaning, one of which may be used for the attachment of the blow off valve. 
(ii) Wherever possible,the openings shall be opposite to each other. 
(iii) All threaded openings in the boiler shall be provided with welded reinforcement, if 
necessary, to give four full threads therein. 


(c)(i) Electric boilers of a design employing removable top cover flange for inspection 
and cleaning need not be fitted with washout openings and washout plug. 
(ii) Level gauges are not required for once through boilers. 


(2) Every boiler shall be provided with at least one feed pump or other feeding device 
except where it is connected with a water main carrying pressure to feed that boiler 
or where the steam generator is operated with no extraction of steam (closed 
system). In the latter case, in lieu of the feeding device, a suitable connection or 
opening shall be provided to feed the boilers. Such connection shall be not less than 
73 mm in diameter. 

(3) (a) Every boiler shall be fitted with necessary mounting and fittings as provided in 

Chapter-5 of these regulations, and they shall be of substantial construction suitable 

for 7 kg/cm*(g). 

(0) All these fitting, except safety valves shall be certified by manufacturers of the 

fittings themselves. 


— 


(4) (a) The feed pipe shall be provided with a check valve and a stop valve of a size not 
less than that of the pipe. 
(0) The feed water may be delivered to the boiler through the openings of the same 
size in the shell as that of the blow off connection. 


(5) (a) Each boiler shall be equipped with a blow off connection, not less than 8 mm in 
size located to drain the boiler water from the lowest water space practicable when 
the boiler is under pressure. 

(0) Feed water shall not be introduced through the openings or connection needed 
for the water column, the water gauge glass or the gauge cock. 


(6) (a) Every boiler other than a coil type or a once through boiler shall be fitted with two 
gauge glasses not less than 50 mm long for determining the water level. 
(b) The boiler shall have the lowest visible part of the water gauge located at least 25 
mm above the lowest permissible water level. 


(7) (a) The lowest permissible water level of vertical boilers shall be at a point one-third 
of the height at the shell above the bottom head or tube sheet. 
(0) Where the boiler is equipped with internal furnace, the water level shall not be 
less than one-third of the length of the tubes above the top of the furnace tube sheet. 


(8) (a) The steam pressure gauge shall have its dial graduated to not less than twice 
the maximum allowable working pressure of the boiler. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 4049 


(0) The diameter of the dial shall be at least 00 mm and the pipe connecting the 
pressure gauge shall be minimum 0 mm and the connection shall be through 
siphon. 


(9) (a) Each boiler shall be equipped with two safety valves for relieving the steam 
pressure. The diameter of the valves shall not be less than 73 mm. 
(0) The minimum relieving capacity of the safety valve shall be sufficient to 
discharge all the steam that can be generated by the boiler without allowing the 
pressure to rise more than 0 percent above maximum allowable working pressure. 
(c) The safety valve shall be connected to the boiler independently of any other 
steam connections, without any unnecessary intervening pipe or fitting. Such 
intervening pipe or fitting if unavoidable shall not be longer than the corresponding 
face to face dimension of a tee fitting of the same diameter and the minimum 
opening there through shall be at least equal to the valve inlet. 


(0) No valve of any description shall be placed between safety valve and the boiler not 
on the discharge pipe from the safety valve to the atmosphere. 


(/) The electrically heated boilers shall be effectively earthed with a lead of substantial 
cross section.

under sub-section (2) of section 2 of the Act shall be as per table 8/2 of regulation 304. 


(0) The annual inspection fee for renewal of certificateshall be as per table 8/3 of 
regulation 305. 


(2) The certificate of manufacture and test for small industrial boilers shall be issued in 
Form-XxXIl. 


(3) Operator for these boilers shall possess minimum educational qualification of 
matriculationor equivalent

558. Sampling.—Sampling shall be done by following general directions mentioned in Part-2

be observed, namely:- 


(a) A stainless steel or monel metal coil shall be fitted on the sampling cock so that the 
temperature of the water sample shall be well below the boiling point at atmospheric 
pressure and there is no risk of aeration and concentration due to flashing into 
steam; and 


(0) Samples of feed water shall be collected from the delivery of the boiler feed pump, 
samples of boiler water from the top drum, and samples of condensate from the 
delivery of the condensate extraction pump.

above 3.5 kg/cm7(g). 

(2)Any steam consuming equipment where steam is condensed or open to atmosphere 
shall not be covered under this chapter. 


56. Construction and workmanship.—The construction and workmanship shall 
conform to the requirements of relevant regulations for the particular type of 
construction. 


562. Materials —Materials used in the construction of these vessels shall comply with 
the applicableregulations of Chapter-2. 


563. Welding consumables.—Welding consumables shall comply with the relevant 
provisions of Chapter-2.

subject to pressure on the concave sideshall be determined as per Equation(4/i0) of

569.Girth flange.—() Non-standard bolted flange connections when used shall satisfy 
the requirements of these regulations . 

(2) The design and construction of a flange shall involve the selection of the gasket 
(material, type, and dimensions), flange facing, bolting, hub proportions, flange width, 
and flange thickness. 

(3) Flange dimensions shall be such that the calculated stresses in the flange,does not

577.U-Tubes.—(l) U-tubes used in heat exchangers shall not have ovality more than 
0% after forming. 

(2)Carbon and alloy steel U-Tubes up to mean radius R = 5D (where D = Tube 
outside diameter) shall be stress relieved with minimum soaking time of 5 minutes.

578.Tube bundle assemblies. — Tube bundle assemblies shall be checked for 
free entry by using a ring gauge having inside diameter of baffle equal to Outside 
Diameter(OD) of tube + 7.5 mm. 


579.Initial qualification of tube to tube sheet joints —(l)The method of joining tubes 
to tube sheet shall be any one of the following,namely:- 


(i)Strength expansion only (without welding); 
(ii) Strength welding & light expansion, or 
(iii) Strength expansion & seal welding. 


(2)All the above three process shall be carried out with procedure qualified by the 
manufacturer. 


(3) (a) The boilerorboiler component manufacturer shall prepare written procedures for 
joints that are expanded (whether welded and expanded or expanded only) for joint 
strength. 

(b) The boileror boiler component manufacturer shall establish the variables that affect 
joint repeatability in these procedures. 

(c) The procedures shall provide detailed descriptions or sketches of enhancements, 
such as grooves, serrations, threads, and coarse machining profiles. 


(4) (a) For strength welded joints, minimum eight mock up welds are required to 
qualify each procedure. 

(0) The mock up assembly shall essentially duplicate the tube hole configuration and 
tube-to-tubesheet joint design. 


(5) The materials group (M No. wise), tube hole size, tube size and tube fit up 
with tube sheet shall simulate production. 


(6) Test block arrangementshall be as given under,— 


Minimum number of holes = 3-2-3 for triangular pitch. 
= 3-3-3 for Square pitch 
Thickness = Tube sheet thickness or 50 mm whichever is less. 


(7) (a) The test block simulating the tubesheet may be circular, square or 
rectangular in shape, essentially in general conformity with the tube pitch geometry. 

(0) The test assembly shall consist of an array of tubes such that the tube to be tested 
is in the geometric center of the array and surrounded by at least one row of adjacent 
tubes. (c) The test block shall extend a distance of at least one tubesheet ligament 
beyond the edge of the peripheral tubes in the assembly. 


(8) All tubes in the test block array shall be from the same grade of material and 
shall be installed using identical procedures. 


(9) (a) The length of the tube used for testing the tube joint need only be 
sufficient to suit the test apparatus. 
(b) The length of the tubes adjacent to the tube joint to be tested shall not be less 
than the thickness of the test block to be qualified.

580. Procedure for testing the test block.—(l) The mock-up welds shall be subjected 
to the tests given in regulations 58/ to 583sequentially and shall meet the applicable 
acceptance criteria. 


58. Acceptance criteria for visual examination.— (l) The accessible surfaces of the 
welds shall be examined visually with no magnification required. 

(2) The welds shall show complete fusion and no evidence of burning through the tube 
wall, and shall be free from cracking or porosity. 


582. Acceptance criteria withliquid penetrant—Procedure and performance tests 
examined by liquid penetrant techniques shall be judged unacceptable when the 
examination exhibits any indication in excess of the limitsspecified as the following;- 

(i) relevant linear indications; 

(ii) relevant rounded indications greater than 5 mm; 

(iii) four or more relevant rounded indications in a line separated by 7.5 mm or 

less (edge-to-edge). 


583. Acceptance criteria for macro-examination— (l) The mock up welds shall be 
sectioned through the center of the tube for macro-examination. 
(2) The four exposed surfaces shall be smoothed and etched with a suitable etchant to 
give a clear definition of the weld and heat-affected zone. 
(3) Using a magnification of 0X to 20X, the exposed cross sections of the weld shall 
conformto as under;- 
(i)minimum leak path dimension required by the design; 
(ii) NO cracking; 
(iii) complete fusion of the weld deposit into the tubesheet and tube wall face; 
(iv) complete penetration of the weld deposit to within 0.4 mm of the root of the 
joint; and 
(v) porosity shall not reduce the weld throat below the required minimum leak 
path thickness.

equation given below, based on the measured values. 
(2) The thinning shall be within 5% to 8%.

CHAPTER- 7 
SMALL SOLAR BOILERS 


585.Scope.—This chapter shall apply to the design, construction, inspection, registration, 
operation and maintenance of small solar boilers. 


PART- 
Definitions 


586. Solar receivers.—Solar receivers are the devices that receive solar radiation heat from 
the sun to generate steam. 


587. Small solar boiler .— (.) A small solar boiler shall be a solar steam generating system 
producing steam for use external to itself having area concentration ratio of solar radiation 
capturing aperture area to receiver area less than 300 and having a volumetric capacity 
more than 25 litres. 


(2) A natural or forced circulation type boiler wherein the receiver is the solar heat receiving 
device generating steam at pressure up to 2 kg/cm*(g) 


588. Heating surface area.—The heating surface area of a small solar boiler shall be the 
area of receivers exposed to the receiving radiation. 


589. Volumetric capacity.—Volumetric capacity of a small solar boiler shall be the total 
volume from feed check valve to the main steam stop valve at the outlet of steam header. 


PART-2 


Extent to which Variation from the standard conditions laid down in the preceding 
chapters is permissible 


590.Variations from standards.—The variations from the standard conditions provided 
in the preceding chapters of these regulations shall be permittedfor small solar boilersas 
provided in regulations 59/ to 594. 


59. Materials.— (|) The materials used in the construction of small solar boilers shall 
conform to the provisions made in these regulations. 


(2) (a) Plates used in the construction of the boilers shall be either of IS: 2062 or 
equivalent or as per Chapter-2. 

(0) The plate for shell and heads shall be not less than 6 mm in thickness and the heads 
as tube sheets for tubes rolled in shall be at least 8 mm in thickness. 


(3)The tubes and pipes shall be made of carbon steel, alloy steel, stainless steel or 
copper. 


[भाग ॥--खण्ड 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 057 


(4) Corrosion allowance of 0.75 mm shall be provided for parts of the boiler directly exposed 
to atmosphere and solar radiation. 
(5) No corrosion allowance is required for stainless steel parts of the boiler. 


(6) Materials need not be certified with Indian Boiler Regulations forms from the maker 
provided all other certification requirements as mentioned in applicable regulations are 
complied with. 


592. Design, construction, workmanship and the method of computing the maximum 
allowable working pressure.— (l) The construction except where otherwise specified 
shall be the same as those provided in the relevant provisions of the preceding chapters 
of these regulations. 


(2) In the case of Fusion welded small solar boilers, radiography or stress relieving of 
the weld joints shall notbemandatory. 


593. Inspection and testing.— (l) The small solar boilers shall be subjected to 
inspection during construction and after completion of construction by an Inspecting 
Authority. 

(2) The inspection of small solar boilers shallbe made at the following stages, namely:- 


(i) Material identification and inspection. 

(ii) Hydraulictest; every completed boiler wholly or partly welded construction, the 
hydraulic test pressure shall be equal to two times the design pressure of 
theboiler. 


594. Certificates and maker’s stamps.— (l) The certificate and maker's stamp shall be in 
conformity with the provisions of Chapter-/of theseregulations. 


(2) Where all information cannot be visibly stamped on the boiler plate due to its small 
size, maker's certificate accompanying the boiler shall contain the necessary details, but 


in all cases name, works number and the year of make shall be stamped or exhibited on 
theboiler. 


PART-3 


595. Valves, gauges, fittings and feed supply.— (|) Small solar boiler shall be fitted with 
the following, namely:— 


(i) wash plugs for cleaning; 
(ii) Suitable provision to indicate the water level; 
(iii) one water feeding device; 


(iv)one feed pipe shall be provided with a check valve and a stop valve of a size 
not less than that of the pipe; 


058 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(v) suitable provision to drain the boiler water; 
(vi) one steam pressure gauge having minimum i00 mm dial size; and 
(vii) one safety valve for relieving the steam pressure. 


(2) Safety valves shall be certified under Indian Boiler Regulations and all other fittings 
may be certified by the manufacturers of such fittings. 


596. Registration, operation and maintenance.—()The fees required to accompany an 
application under sub-section (2) of Section 2 of the Act shall be such as provided in 
regulation 304. 

(2) The inspection fee for renewal of certificate after every four years shall be as 
provided in regulation 305. 

(3) The certificate of manufacture and test for small solar boilers shall be issued in 
Form-XXIll. 


(4) Operator for these boilers shall possess minimum educational qualification of 
matriculationor equivalent.

(4) No structural alteration, addition of renewal shall be made to the boiler otherwise than in accordance 
with section 8 of the Act. 


(2) Under the provisions of Section 3 of the Act this certificate shall cease to be in force: 
(a) onthe expiry of the period for which it was granted; or 
(b) when any accident occurs to the boiler; or 


(c) when the boiler is moved the boiler, except a vertical boiler, the heating surface of which is less 


than two hundred square feet, or a portable or vehicular boiler; or 


(d) save as provided in section 7 of the Act, when any structural alteration, addition or renewal is 


made in or to the boiler; or 


28 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


(e) if the Chief Inspector in any particular case so directs when any structural alteration, addition or 


renewal is made in or to any steam-pipe attached to the boiler; or 


(f) onthe communication to the owner of the boiler of an order of the Chief Inspector or Inspector 
prohibiting its use on the ground that it or any boiler component attached thereto is in a 


dangerous condition. 


Under Section 5 of the Act, when the period of a certificate relating to a boiler has expired, 
the owner shall, provided that he has applied before the expiry of that period for a renewal of the 
certificate be entitled to use the boiler at the design pressure entered in the former certificate, 
pending the issue of orders on the application but this shall not be deemed to authorise the use of a 
boiler in any of the cases referred to in clauses (0), (c), (d), (e) and (f) of sub-section (4) of section 3 
occurring after the expiry of the period of the certificate. 


(3) The boiler shall not be used at a pressure greater than the pressure entered in the certificate as 
the Design pressure nor with the safety valve set to a pressure exceeding such design pressure. 


(4) The boiler shall not be used otherwise than in a condition which the owner reasonably believes 
to be compatible with safe working. 


(5) Form Xllshall be countersigned by the Chief Inspector at the time of registration only, as per the 


provisions of sub-section (6) of section 2 of the Act. 


Note: The particulars and dimensions regarding this boiler may be obtained by the owner on payment in the 
prescribed manner on application to the Chief Inspector.

(2) This certificate shall cease to be in force— 
(a) onthe expiry of the period for which it was granted, or 
(b) when any accident occurs to the Economiser, or 
(c) when any structural alteration, addition or renewal is made in or to the Economiser, or 


(d) save as provided in section 47 of the Act, when any structural alteration, addition or renewal is made 


in or to the Economiser; or 


(e) onthe communication to the owner of the Economiser of an order of the Chief Inspector or Inspector 


prohibiting its use on the ground that it is in a dangerous condition. 


(3) The Economiser shall not be used at a pressure greater than the pressure/temperature entered in the 
certificate as Maximum allowable working pressure /temperature not with the relief valve set to 


pressure/temperature exceeding such Maximum allowable working pressure /temperature. 


(4) The Economiser shall not be used otherwise than in a condition which the owner reasonably believes to 


be compatible with safe working.

APPENDIX-A 
INSPECTION AND TESTING OF BOILERS, BOILER COMPONENTS 
AND OTHER PARTS DURING MANUFACTURE 


GENERAL 

The Inspecting Authority/Competent Person shall have access to the works of the 
manufacturer at all reasonable times and shall inspect the manufacture of the boiler at least 
at the following stages and may reject any part that does not comply with the requirements 
of the Indian Boiler Regulations, 2026. In case of any doubt, the Inspecting 
Authority/Competent Person may examine at any stage other than the stages stipulated 
below. The manufacturer shall give at least 4 working days’ notice to the Inspecting 
Authority/Competent Person before reaching each stage. Before undertaking any of the 
stage inspections, the Inspecting Authority/Competent Person shall satisfy himself that the 
testing equipment/instrument has been properly calibrated. 


STAGES OF INSPECTION 

Each boiler shall be inspected during manufacture by a Competent Person nominated by the 
Inspecting Authority. Sufficient inspections shall be made to ensure that the materials, 
manufacturing and testing conform to the requirements of these regulations. 


Stages of Inspection During Manufacture 

A. Shell Type Boilers 

(a) (i) When the materials are ready for identification with the relevant material test 
certificates at boiler maker’s works; 

(ii) In laying out and cutting the plates, the plate identification mark shall be located so as to 
be clearly visible after the boiler part is completed. If the plate’s identification mark is 
unavoidably cut out, it shall be transferred by the manufacturer to another part of the 


component to the satisfaction of the Inspecting Authority/Competent Person; 


(iii) The Inspecting Authority/Competent Person shall identify weld test plate material if 
production weld tests are required; 


(0) When the Shell plate and end plates have been formed with plate edges prepared for 
welding and test plates are attached; 


(c) When the welding of main cylindrical shell is completed and checked for circularity; 
(d) To examine radiographs and/or reports of non-destructive testing; 


(e) When openings have been prepared and stand pipes and similar connections including 
end plates have been tackwelded in position and subsequently on completion; 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 4455 


(f) When welding of drum or shell is completed and to check the records of heat-treatment 
when heat treatment is required under these regulations; 


(g) When weld test specimens have been prepared from the test plate, previously selected 
to witness the required testing; 


(h) During hydraulic test, followed by external and internal examination and stamping. 


B. Water Tube Boilers 
(I) Welded drums, headers, separators and vessels 


(a) (i) When the materials are ready for identification with the relevant material test 
certificates at boiler maker’s works; 


(ii) In laying out and cutting the plates, the plate identification mark shall be located so as to 
be clearly visible after the boiler part is completed. If the plate’s identification mark is 
unavoidably cut out, it shall be transferred by the manufacturer to another part of the 
component to the satisfaction of the Inspecting Authority/Competent Person; 


(iii) The Inspecting Authority/Competent Person shall identify weld test plate material 
ifproduction weld tests are required; 


(0) When the plates are formed to cylindrical shape with the edges prepared for welding and 
set up in readiness for commencement of welding and attachment of test plates; 


(c) When the welding of the main cylindrical shell is completed, the shell checked for 
circularity and the radiographic or ultrasonic test reports, records are available for scrutiny; 


(d) When the end plates are ready for identification with the mill certificate, formed to shape 
with weld edges prepared and set on to the cylindrical shell in readiness for the 
circumferential welding operation; 


(e) When the welding of the end plates to the drum or the header is complete and the 
radiographs or ultrasonic examination records are available for scrutiny; 


(f) When each drum or header is prepared to receive any compensation plates and 
attachments, and when at least 0% of each type of branch of tube stub is set up ready for 
welding;

Authority/Competent Person will check the records of heat treatment, and mark off of 
specimens for preparation and testing from test plates; 

(h) During non-destructive examination, after stress relieving, on alloy steel drums and 
carbon steel drums with carbon content exceeding 0.25 % or thickness more than 00 mm;

APPENDIX-B 
TRANSVERSE RUPTURE STRESS (MODULUS OF RUPTURE) 


The transverse strength of cast iron may be expressed by a figure shown as the 
Transverse Rupture Stress; this figure is obtained by dividing the maximum bending moment 
at failure by the modulus of the section. Thus, the Transverse Rupture Stress is the 
maximum stress which would have existed if the material had behaved in accordance with 
the assumptions made in the ordinary theory of bending, and in that event it would be 
independent of the size and shape of the section. Bars fractured in transverse, however, are 
stressed beyond the elastic limit, and under these conditions the theory of bending no longer 
holds good. Furthermore, the influence of rate of cooling in cast metals is such that the 
Transverse Rupture Stress of a Thick Bar is less than that of a thinner bar of the same 
metal. The Transverse Rupture Stress, therefore, is not strictly independent of the size and 
metal. The Transverse Rupture Stress, therefore, is not strictly independent of the size and 
shape, of the section, but nevertheless forces a convenient way of expressing the result of 
transverse tests without the necessity for giving full details of bar dimensions. The formula 
required is obtained as follows: 


A bar supported at both ends and centrally loaded with a load ‘W’ is subject to a 
bending Moment WL/4, ‘L’ being the distance between supports. The resistance offered by 
the bar may be expressed as fZ, ‘f being the stress and ‘Z’ the modulus of the section. At 
fracture, ‘f' becomes the breaking stress of Transverse Rupture Stress, and WL/4 = fZ, 
where f = (LW)/ (42). If ‘W’ is in tons and ‘L’ in inches, ‘f’ is in tons per square inch. For a 
round bar, Z = 0.0982d?, where 0 diameter in inches. 


Since for a standard round bar ‘L’ and ‘Z’ are constant, the value WL/4Z is fixed and 
hence the Transverse Rupture Stress f = KW, where ‘Kk’ is a constant. 


The factor ‘K’ for converting actual breaking loads into Transverse Rupture Stress 
are given in the following tables both for the Standard test bars and the test bars varying 
within the limits of regulation 65. In the same table are given factors for converting actual 
breaking loads into equivalent breaking loads on the bars of Standard diameter.

or SFA Specification. The test specimen shall not be subjected to any mechanical or thermal

The assembly shall be welded together with these plates pre-set so that the gap at 
the top between the chamfered edges of the plates is 25 mm and the plates may be 
approximately level when the butt-weld is completed. 


The weld metal shall be deposited in single or multi-run layers and the direction of 
deposition of each layer shall be alternatively from each end of the specimen. Each run of 
weld metal shall not be less than .5 mm and not more than 3 mm thick. The time interval 
between the completion of one run and the commencement of deposition of the succeeding 
run shall be not less than 5 minutes. The assembly shall not be quenched between the 
deposition of individual runs. The welding current used shall be within the appropriate range 
given by the manufacturer. The welding position for the assembly shall be flat, unless this is

contrary to the recommended position for the electrode, in which case the position of weld

portion including the weld shall then be removed by cutting away the excess plates at the 
places indicated in Fig. 2/2.

the dimension given in Fig. 2/3 taking care that the longitudinal axis of the specimen

Fig. 2/2. The specimen then shall be tested for tensile strength.

(5) Transverse tensile test 


Transverse tensile tests specimens shall conform to the dimensions given in Fig. 2/7. 
The upper and lower surfaces of the weld shall be filed, ground or machined level with 
the respective original surfaces of the plates. Where the plates are not level with each 
other the metal many be cut away to bring them approximately level, provided that the 
thickness of the plate is not reduced by more than a total of mm. 


The test specimens shall then be tested for tensile test as in Appendix-D. 
(6) Transverse bend test 


The bend test specimens shall be 38 mm in width. The upper and lower surfaces of 
the weld shall be filled, ground or machined level with the respective original surfaces of 
the plates, with the proviso as in item (6) above. The tool marks should be avoided as 
they lead to location of stress and may cause premature failure. For this reason the 
direction of machining of the surfaces should be along the specimens and transverse to 
the weld. The sharp corners of the test specimens shall be rounded to a radius not 
exceeding .3 mm. 


The test specimens shall be bent through an angle of 780° over a former having a 
diameter equal to three times the thickness of the specimen, as shown in Fig. 2/8. One

DEFINITION OF WELDING TERMS, CLASSIFICATION OF COVERED ELECTRODES, 
DEFINITIONS & PRINCIPLES — DEFINITIONS 


Weld Slope: The slope of a weld is the angle formed between the line of weld root and a 
horizontal reference plane placed below the lowest portion of the weld. (See Fig. 2/9) 


SLOPE 


Fig. 2/9: Figure to Illustrate Weld Slope 


Weld Rotation: The rotation of weld is the angle formed between the upper portion of vertical 
reference plane which passes through the line of the weld root and a line drawn from the line of the 
weld root which intersects the weld surface at a right angle and a point equidistant from either edge of 
the weld (see Fig. 2/0)
