APPENDIX-E 


PROOF TEST FOR CREEP QUALITY OF CARBON STEEL 
BOILERQUALITY PLATE- SPECIFICATION 


NATURE OF TEST 


i. The test shall consist of a tensile creep test carried out over a period of at least 48 
hours at a temperature of 450°C and with stress of /.25 kg/mm*. Under these 
conditions the slope of the chord to the creep curve between the 247" and 48" hour 
shall not exceed 50 x 0 = 4 strain per hour. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3(i)] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 


7! 


CONDITION OF MATERIAL 


2. The test shall be made on the material in the normalized condition. The normalizing 
temperature shall be between 875°C — 925°C, and the plate sample shall be 
maintained at the normalizing temperature for one hour per inch of thickness and 
cooled freely in still air. 


TEMPERATURE OF TEST 


(०) 


STRESS 


3. (8) Temperature Measurement - The temperature of the 
specimen shall be measured by thermocouples suitable for the temperature 
specified. Two thermocouples situated one at each end of the gauge length 
shall be used in the case of test pieces having gauge lengths upto 57 mm, 
and for longer gauge lengths and additional thermocouple situated at the 
middle of the gauge length shall be used. 


Thermocouples shall make good thermal contact with the test piece and the 
protected from the direct heat of the furnace of being covered with asbestos 
tape or equivalent insulation. 


The cold junction shall be maintained at a known temperature which shall be 
registered by a mercury thermometer. Alternatively, a suitable means shall be 
provided for correcting automatically errors in reading due to changes in 
temperature of the cold junction. 


Temperature Control - The two (or three) thermocouples specified in clause 
(a) shall agree with one another within 3°C and the average of these readings 
shall be taken as the test temperature which shall not vary from 450°C by 
more than + 2°C throughout the test. 

Either a continuous record of sufficient readings of the temperature shall be 
made to indicate that the temperature conditions have been satisfactory. 


Heating period before loading — The specimen shall be maintained at the 
specified temperature for at least an hour prior to the application of the load. 


4. The load required to produce the specified stress shall be gradually applied without 
shock during a period not exceeding five minutes and the stress shall be accurate to 
+ 2 Ye percent. 


SENSITIVITY OF STRAIN-MEASUREING EQUIPMENT 


5. The sensitivity of the extensometer must be such that strains can be measured to the 
nearest 0.00002. 


72 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


READINGS 


6. A sufficient number of strain readings shall be taken clearly to define the creep curve 
upto 48 hours, and the chord slope shall be measured from a chord drawn between 
points on the curve at the 24™ and 48" hours. 


REPEAT TEST 


7. If the materials fail to pass the test, but the chord slope does not exceed 60 x 0 = 6° 
strain per hour, a retest may be made at the request of the manufacturer and shall be 
accepted if satisfactory, or at the Competent Person discretion a pass test at a stress 
5 percent less than that specified may be accepted.

APPENDIX-G 
SAFETY VALVE DISCHARGE EFFICIENCY TESTING 


A. General. 


(i) The purpose and manner of testing shall be such as to provide suitable data from 
which a constant 'c' may be determined in Equation(5/7). To this end the following 
information shall be supplied to the Inspecting Authority before testing is undertaken: 


(a) Full particulars on the values to be tested and range of valves and springs which 
they represent. 


(0) Details of the testing rig including instrumentation and proposed calibration 
procedure. 


(c) Proposed source, capacity, pressure, temperature of steam used for the test. 
(ii) All testing shall be witnessed by Inspecting Authority or the Competent Person. 


(iii) Tests shall be made to determine the operative characteristics of the safety valves 
for which a constant is to be determined and also to establish the discharge 
efficiency of the safety valve. 


(iv) Where possible, the tests to determine operating characteristics and discharge 
efficiency shall be carried out using the same steam, the same pressure conditions 
and the same location. When the tests are carried out separately, the valves in each 
case shall be complete and shall include all internals, e.g. blow-down adjustments 
rings. 


(v) The set pressure at which the operating characteristics are determined shall be the 
minimum set pressure for which the spring used is designed. The tests shall be 
carried out using steam and shall determine the set pressure, the lift at the over 


pressure specified for the type of valve, as defined in regulations 93 to 95. 


(vi) The Inspecting Authority may dispense with Operating Characteristic tests described 
in A(v). 


(vii) Discharge efficiency tests shall be carried out using steam and shall be carried out 
relative to the operative characteristic tests described in A(v). 


(viii) When the Inspecting Authority is satisfied that the design of valve will operate 
satisfactorily it shall if desired, be permissible to hold the valve head mechanically at 
the proven lift while carrying out the tests to ascertain the discharge efficiency. 


[भाग ॥-खण्ड 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 4483 


B. VALVES USED IN THE TEST PROGRAMME 


(i) The safety valves tested shall, as far as is practicable, be representative of the 
pressure and size range of valve manufactured. 

(ii) The tests for operative characteristics and the discharge efficiency test shall be 
carried out on the three sizes or half the number of sizes in the range, whichever is 
smaller, with a minimum of two sizes. 


(iii) When the range is extended, due consideration shall be given, in consultation with 
the Inspecting Authority, to whether further witnessed tests are necessary. 


(iv) The test for operating characteristics shall be carried out at three significantly 
different set pressure for each size of valve. 


(v) The discharge efficiency tests shall be carried out relative to one set pressure for 
each size of valve. 


(vi) Each tests shall be carried out a minimum of three times to obtain acceptable 
average results. 


(vii)For the case of valves of either novel or special design of which one size only is 
being manufactured, tests at one set pressure are permitted by agreement with the 
Inspecting Authority. When the range of sizes or pressure is extended, due 
consideration shall be given in consultation with the Inspecting Authority, to whether 
further witnessed tests are necessary. 

C. DETERMINATION OF CONSTANT ‘C’ 

Let 

E, be the measure capacity, on test of saturated steam (Kg/h.) 

P,be the pressure at safety valve inlet at which the capacity was measured (bar gauge); 


A be the area appropriate to the type of valve (7, [see regulation 96(t)]. 


X be the allowable percentage over pressure for the type of valve under test. (See 
regulation 96) . 


Ct be the constant determined from test. 


Et 
ct= 


To accommodate the permitted spread on test results, tolerance on valve parts and 
springs, this calculated value of ‘Ct’ shall be derated to 80% to obtain the value of ‘C’ to be 


84 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


used in equation (5/7) of regulation 796(/). This is to ensure that all production valves will 
achieve their rated discharge capacity at not more than the over pressure allowed for the 
type of valve tested. 


The Inspecting Authority may accept a more favourable derating factor of up to 90% 
of the calculated value of ‘Ct’ where the performance of the valves under test and the 
manufacturing and spring tolerance applicable ensure that the allowable overpressure for 
the type of valve under test will not be exceeded when a valve is discharging its rated 
capacity in service. 


[भाग ॥--खण्ड 3()] भारत का राजपत्र : असाधारण 4485

IX duly filled in shall be allowed for running for another period of twelve months:—

(d) Water quality to the boiler is maintained as per the requirement of such boilers and 
on line data of the quality be provided through Data Acquisition System (DAS) or 
through water quality record logbook maintained at plant or at source of water; 


(e) Boiler tube failure record (location, number of tubes repaired/replaced). 


(2) Inspection shall be carried out by the concerned Competent Person at the expiry of thirty 
six months as provided in regulation 3. However, in case of shutdown of fifteen days or 
more any time before expiry of the certification period and after six months of the 
certification, Competent Person shall be duly informed so that inspection can be scheduled 
during the said shutdown period. 


B. Waste Heat Boilers (Unfired) up to twenty years of age used exclusively in 
continuous process plant. 


(!) For Waste Heat Boilers (Unfired) up to twenty years of age used exclusively in 
continuous process plant, at the expiry of twenty-four months from the date of inspection 
carried out in accordance with the procedure provided in regulation 3/and certification of 
fitness by the concerned Competent Person in the State, and having satisfied with the 
operation records at paragraph “A”, shall be allowed for running for another period of twenty- 
four months. 


(2) Inspection shall be carried out by the concerned Competent Person at the expiry of forty- 
eight months as provided in regulation 3!. However, in case of shutdown of fifteen days or 
more any time before expiry of the certification period and after six months of the 
certification, Competent Person shall be duly informed so that inspection can be scheduled 
during the said shutdown period. 


C. Waste Heat Boilers (Fired) more than twenty years of age used exclusively in 
continuous process plant. 


88 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)] 


Boiler more than twenty years of age shall continue to be subjected to inspection as 
provided in regulation 3i/every year to the satisfaction of concerned Competent Person in 
the State. However, if Remnant Life Assessment (RLA) as per the provisions of these 
regulations is carried out on the boiler and if found satisfactory, then procedure as given at 
paragraph ' above shall be followed. 


D. Waste Heat Boilers (Unfired) more than twenty years of age used exclusively in 
continuous process plant. 


Boiler more than twenty years of age shall continue to be subjected to inspection as 
provided in regulation 3/every year to the satisfaction of concerned Competent Person in 
State. However, if Remnant Life Assessment (RLA) as per the provisions of these 
regulations is carried out on the boiler and if found satisfactory, then procedure as given at 
paragraph 'B' above would be applicable.
